The static joint model (LIBRARY_MODE = 'static', Mode = 'static', phase_mode: multi_depth) raises an error. Entries that already hold a static offset still load.

How the model is fitted and library model version

fit_transducer_model fits the on-axis field p(z) = H(z)·w, linear in the complex element drives w, to the measured profile at each depth. H comes from axial_transfer_matrix (Rayleigh by default).

Library model version. Entries with meta.library_model_version: 2 apply per-ring gains to elem_p_amp; version 1 applies a phase offset only. Version-3 entries (library_mode: per_depth) take phases, gains, and drive from the refinement at each measured depth.

One calibration core

All entry points run the same functions, so a calibration done with calibration_transducer is identical to one done with refine_transducer_library or the GUI for the same profiles, depths and settings.

Calibration call graph 
calibration_setup ─► calibration_pipeline_start ─► calibration_transducer ─┐   (config_calibration.yaml;
refine_transducer_library ─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤    chosen depths and
                                                                            ▼    intensities)
                                   calibrate_library_entry(lib, tran, meas, options)
                                     ├─ interpolate_axial_profiles   profile at each requested depth
                                     ├─ calibration_fit_depths       one fit_transducer_model fit per depth
                                     │    (calibration_fit_options: 'rayleigh_phase_gain' | 'oneil_phase_only')
                                     ├─ library_refinement_from_fits phases, gains, drive → refinements
                                     ├─ kwave_calibrate_drive        optional: drive calibrated in free-water k-Wave
                                     └─ evaluate_library_entry       R² / focal error before and after
build_transducer_library ─► calibration_fit_depths (same fit loop and presets)
calibration_gui, Nexus Calibration page ─► calibration_fit ─► calibration_fit_depths

calibrate_library_entry reads and writes no files; the callers decide where the result goes.

Library build and run-time loading

The shipped library is built by build_transducer_library.m from the profiles in local/profiles/: every measured depth becomes a refinement fitted by fit_transducer_model (phase offsets and gains on top of geometric steering from set_real_phases, plus the drive that reproduces the measured peak), written to config/calibration/model-<MODEL>/tran-<TRAN>_ds-<DS>_calib.yaml (LIBRARY_PATH). The entry schema is documented in the library YAML schema. At run time, load_transducer_from_library(combo_name, focal_depth_ep, isppa, equip_param) loads the calibrated parameters.

items.title: Fit Presets
items.text:
Presets come from calibration_fit_options. Any fit_transducer_model option can be set on top of a preset (fit_options in the config, FitOptions in the functions).

Preset settings Preset Free parameters Forward model Loss Optimiser Pull to prior rayleigh_phase_gain (default) phase offset + gain per ring Rayleigh pseudo-Huber on intensity (δ 0.8) lsqnonlin, 16 starts Lambda 1e-3 oneil_phase_only phase offset per ring O'Neil (practically) least squares on intensity FEX-minimize (or GlobalSearch) none

items.title: Unmeasured Depths
items.text:
A requested depth within 0.5 mm of a measured one uses that measurement.

Interpolated profiles, the gap warning, and interpolating fits instead

Any other depth is interpolated from its two neighbouring measured profiles (aligned on their focus, profile_align) and then fitted, and is stored with profile_type: interpolated. A warning is issued when the neighbouring measurements are more than max_gap_mm (default 10 mm) apart.

Between calibrated depths, studies interpolate the stored offsets and gains (library_model_at_depth). On held-out measured depths both ways predict the profile about equally well when the measured depths are up to ~10 mm apart (median R² 0.975 each, vs 0.976 for a direct fit and 0.90 for geometric steering). Fitting the interpolated profile is more robust where the focal behaviour changes quickly. Neither bridges a large gap across a change in focal behaviour.

items.title: Calibration and I<sub>SPPA</sub> Targeting
items.text:
Calibration and intensity targeting are separate steps:

Calibration (calibration_transducer, library) ISPPA targeting When Once per transducer/depth, before any study Every run, after the acoustic simulation What is set Phases and drive per focal depth Neither; the simulated field is scaled Input Hydrophone axial profiles transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 (free-water ISPPA, W/cm²; default 30) Output Library entry (YAML) used by studies Pressure field scaled by √(target / free-water baseline)

The acoustic simulation runs at the drive elem_p_amp. A short free-water baseline of the same source (modules.run_water_baseline: auto, the default) gives the free-water ISPPA of that drive, and the field is scaled to the target, so changing the target never re-runs the head simulation. A target that cannot be met stops the run; it is never reported unscaled. ISPPA targeting describes the rules, the provenance fields, and the error messages; Multi-intensity runs several targets from one acoustic simulation.

The typical workflow:

  1. Once per transducer (library build): run build_transducer_library.m to fit every measured depth. Results are stored in config/calibration/ (layout).
  2. Optionally, at chosen depths: run calibration_transducer (or refine_transducer_library) with your own profiles or at unmeasured depths, writing a user library entry (transducer.library_path). Calibrated depths are used exactly there and blended into the rest of the entry within blend_mm.
  3. Per subject simulation: set transducer.serial, combo.ds_serial, and focal_distance_ep (PRESTUS loads the calibrated parameters via load_transducer_from_library) and transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 to the desired free-water intensity. The water baseline and scaling handle the rest; the acoustic simulation is not re-run when the target intensity changes.

items.title: Calibrating at Chosen Depths and Intensities
items.text:
Script: examples/calibration_standalone.m → calibration_setup → calibration_pipeline_start → calibration_transducer

Calibration reads its own config (config_calibration.yaml), loaded as parameters.calibration (as in the example script). For each equipment combination listed there, calibration_setup locates the hydrophone profile CSV (equipment YAML char_data_path, relative to path_input_axial), drops depths outside the transducer's focal range and calibrates all requested depths and intensities in one call (locally, or as one HPC job per combination via platform).

combinations:
  - IS_PCD15287_01001_IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch
  - IS_PCD15473_01001_IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch
focal_depths_wrt_exit_plane:   # [] = every measured depth
  - [40, 50]
  - [40]
desired_intensities:           # free-water ISPPA [W/cm²]; the first is the stored reference
  - [30, 60]
  - [30]

calibration_transducer can also be called directly:

[lib, report, out] = calibration_transducer(csv_path, 'IS_PCD15287_01001_IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch', ...
    [30 60], [40 50], parameters);

profile_empirical may be the profile CSV, a read_axial_profiles struct, or a single profile with axial_intensity and axial_distance_bowl.

items.title: Calibration Outputs
items.text:
Calibration writes a library entry {library_path}/{combo}.yaml, which studies use through transducer.library_path, and a calibration output folder path_output_profiles.

Files written to each endpoint
  1. Library entry {library_path}/{combo}.yaml (default {path_output}/library): the calibrated depths as refinements on top of the existing user entry, or else the shipped one. Studies use it by setting transducer.library_path to that folder.
  2. Calibration output folder path_output_profiles (default {path_output}/profiles):
    • PRESTUS_virtual_{combo}.csv: phases and amplitude per intensity (rows) × depth (columns)
    • {combo}-F{depth}mm-I{intensity}wpercm2.yaml: one PRESTUS transducer block per depth × intensity, with target_isppa_wcm2 and tx_calibration.isppa_wcm2 set to that intensity (can be ingested with update_transducer_library)
    • {combo}_settings_I{intensity}.csv: per-depth phases, per-ring amplitudes, gains, model focus (library_settings_table)
    • {combo}_calibration_profiles.csv: the measured or interpolated profiles that were fitted
    • {combo}_calibration_report.csv, {combo}_calibration.png, and {combo}_kwave_drive_calibration.csv if the k-Wave drive calibration ran

All values in the output folder are resolved from the library entry (library_model_at_depth), so both endpoints agree exactly. The drive for other intensities scales as √(I / I_ref).

items.title: Calibration Configuration
items.text:
Keys of config_calibration.yaml beyond the combinations, depths, and intensities above.

Calibration config keys

All keys of config_calibration.yaml are listed in Calibration Parameters.

Key Meaning phase_mode single_depth (default): fit each depth · geometric: no fit, geometric steering with the measured drive (multi_depth raises an error) fit_preset rayleigh_phase_gain (default) · oneil_phase_only (see Fit presets) forward_model, fit_options Optional overrides of the preset opt_phase_precession false · linear · monotonic phase constraint (PhaseConstraint) opt_weights 0 = uniform; ≥ 1 Gaussian weights around the focus (FocalWeight) opt_limits [min max] fitted window, mm from the bowl apex (FitWindowMm, converted to the exit plane) skip_front_peak_mm Near field ignored in fit and metrics (NearFieldSkipMm) profile_align, max_extrapolation_mm, max_gap_mm Profile interpolation at unmeasured depths ring_profile auto (default: keep the entry's) · fit: within-ring velocity profile shared by all depths (fit_ring_profile) · none: uniform rings; ring_profile_n_sub (4), ring_profile_smooth (0.3), ring_profile_near_field_skip_mm (4); ring_profile_offaxis (plane-scan file, '' = axial only) and ring_profile_offaxis_kind (all). See Within-ring velocity profile add_FDO 1 (default): profile distances are from the exit plane · 0: from the bowl apex focal_reference FLHM convention of the profile headers; see Focal depth convention kwave_drive_calibration Free-water k-Wave simulation per depth that rescales the stored drive to the simulated ISPPA (default true; run_free_water_sim is still read); force_kwavearray, axisymmetric2D set up its grid opt_method, opt_seed Optimiser and seed of the oneil_phase_only preset

elem_phase_correction in the equipment YAML is used as the prior the fits are regularised towards. save_elem_correction, opt_amp_validation, and opt_upper_velocity are not used: offsets are written to the library entry, and since the drive scales exactly with √ISPPA, one k-Wave drive calibration per depth replaces a validation run per intensity.

items.title: Emulating Hydrophone Profiles
items.text:
A shipped library entry is fitted to reference hydrophone profiles of the transducer model where such profiles exist, not to your own device. Refining fits the entry to the axial profiles you measure in your own water tank and writes it to your own folder, so a study reproduces the focus and drive of your setup. This page covers the refinement, with its optional within-ring velocity profile and free-water k-Wave drive calibration, and the profile files the fits read.

On this page:

  • Refining a Library Entry: the usual path, from your measured profiles to your own library entry.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You have hydrophone profiles of your own device and want a library entry fitted to them.
  • Before you start: Free-water axial profiles in the axial profile CSV format; the Optimization Toolbox for fitting. The focal depth convention and calibration methods are on Calibration.

items.title: Refining a Library Entry
items.text:
Measure axial profiles in your water tank at the depths you will stimulate (CSV format). One call fits them and writes an entry to your folder, with a before/after report and, with Plot, a figure:

refine_transducer_library('CTX_250_001_SC_105_010', 'my_profiles.csv', ...
    '/project/my_study/transducer_library', struct('Plot', true));

Then set transducer.library_path in the study config. examples/demo_transducer_refinement.m runs the whole path on demonstration profiles.

To inspect an entry, plot_transducer_library(combo, library_path) plots the ring phases, drive, and ring gains across depths, and generate_calibration_report(combo, library_path) writes an HTML summary with the fit quality and the settings at the fitted depths.

GUI. The same steps are available interactively:

calibration_gui(struct('OutputPath', '/project/my_study/transducer_library'))

Predict shows the fit at the depths you will stimulate before you save (Predictions at desired depths). The Nexus's Transducer ▸ Calibration page gives the same results for the transducers of a study config and saves to the study's transducer.library_path (Calibration page). A saved entry records its fit settings (mode, FitOptions, depths, profile CSV, reference ISPPA, interpolation, and k-Wave options) in meta.fit; opening the entry restores them.

Config-driven. calibration_transducer (examples/calibration_standalone.m) runs the same calibration (calibrate_library_entry) and writes the library entry plus a calibration output folder; see Calibration at chosen depths and intensities. To ingest per-run YAMLs ({combo}-F*mm-I*wpercm2.yaml) as refinements:

update_transducer_library(combo_name, path_output_profiles, my_library_path)
Fit defaults and fit options

Per-depth fits free the phase offsets and per-ring gains (FreeParams = {'phase','amp'}), with an intensity-domain loss (Domain = 'intensity', HuberDelta = 0.8). They are regularised towards geometric steering. The GUI, calibration_fit, and build_transducer_library use the same defaults (calibration_fit_options); fit_transducer_model called on its own defaults to an amplitude-domain loss with HuberDelta = 0.05, so pass it calibration_fit_options() to fit as they do. z_shift stays at 0, because a study does not apply it; correct a persistent axial misregistration in the equipment geometry or the profiles.

Fit options (FitOptions, see help fit_transducer_model) in both GUIs:

Panel Options Main Free parameters, forward model, near-field skip, loss domain, Huber δ, starts Advanced… Phase constraint and priors (Lambda, LambdaAmp), gain bounds (AmpBounds, PlausibleGain), amplitude fit, focal weighting and fit window, near-field penalty (NearFieldPenalty, NearFieldMargin, NearFieldMinMm), medium (CWater, Rho), optimiser and seed, desired-profile Tolerance, k-Wave drive calibration GridDims and ApplyCorrection Start from preset Loads a calibration_fit_options preset into both

Not offered: z shift and steering sound speed (not applied at run time), ChannelGroups (from the equipment), Prior (the entry), and EvaluateOnly (Evaluate measured).

items.title: Predictions at Desired Depths
items.text:
Predict models the profiles at the depths in Desired depths, for example 20:5:60 or 30, 42.5, 50 (default min_foc:5:max_foc). The depths need not have been measured. Each model is resolved as a study resolves it (evaluate_library_entry → library_model_at_depth):

  • Geometric: geometric steering only.
  • Library: the library entry with its refinements (the entry in Save to folder if there is one, else the shipped entry).
  • Fit: the current unsaved fit, with k-Wave-calibrated drives if that calibration ran.

Interpolation and blending follow How phases are computed; outside the refined span, the drive and gains of the nearest refinement are mixed with the global ones by the same blend weight, so beyond blend_mm (5 mm) the global drive and gains apply. Without a global drive, the nearest refined drive is used at any depth. fit_z_shift_mm is not applied.

The GUI plots modelled against measured (solid) or derived (dashed) profiles, and focus against target depth. The table lists, per desired depth: profile type, phase model (refined, blend w=…, static, or geometric), drive at the reference ISPPA, predicted focus, R², and element phases. Without a profile CSV, the GUI opens in prediction view only (no R², no fitting).

Calibrating at desired depths. Set Calibrate at to Desired depths and press Fit. The GUI calibrates at every desired depth with a profile and reports skipped depths. With Fit depths (measured), Fit uses the depths selected under Fit depths.

Profiles at desired depths, exports, and headless refinement

Profiles at desired depths. With a profile CSV loaded, each desired depth gets a profile from the measurements (interpolate_axial_profiles):

Type Source Measured The desired depth was measured Interpolated The two neighbouring measured profiles, shifted so their foci coincide at the interpolated position, blended linearly by distance Extrapolated Outside the measured range but within extrapolate ≤ (default 0 mm, off): the nearest profile shifted to the desired depth None Further outside the range

Desired profiles sets what the foci are aligned on: label (default, the column headers; see focal-depth labels) or peak (intensity peak beyond the near-field skip). The shifted near field is not physical; fits skip it.

Exports.

  • Save entry writes refinement.profile_type. If any depth was fitted to a derived profile, it also writes {combo}_calibration_profiles.csv next to the entry and records it in refinement.calibration_profiles_csv.
  • Export profiles… writes the profiles of the last fit, or else those at the desired depths on view.
  • Export settings… writes per-depth settings of the fit (else the entry) at the depths on view, via library_settings_table: profile type, phase model, weight, drive, focus, and per ring phase, drive, and gain.

Profile CSVs use the format read_axial_profiles reads, with a YAML sidecar recording, for every derived column, its source depths, weights, and shifts. ExportFolder writes both exports without a file dialog.

Headless. refine_transducer_library accepts unmeasured depths in Depths: a depth within 0.5 mm of a measurement uses it; any other is interpolated (InterpolateOptions: Align, MaxExtrapolationMm). It writes the calibration profiles (ExportProfiles, on by default when any depth is derived) and optionally the settings table (ExportSettings, SettingsDepths):

refine_transducer_library('CTX_250_001_SC_105_010', 'my_profiles.csv', lib, struct( ...
    'Depths', [30 42.5 55], 'ExportSettings', true, ...
    'InterpolateOptions', struct('MaxExtrapolationMm', 3)));
% writes {combo}.yaml, {combo}_calibration_profiles.csv (+ .yaml sidecar), {combo}_settings.csv
T = library_settings_table(tran, lib_struct, 20:5:70, struct('IsppaWcm2', 30, 'CsvPath', 'settings.csv'));

items.title: Within-Ring Velocity Profile
items.text:
Experimental

The ring profile is not validated. On-axis profiles alone do not determine the sub-ring weights; without off-axis or plane measurements, the off-axis field it predicts is unvalidated.

Optional. The library models each ring as a uniformly vibrating piston. For several Sonic Concepts CTX transducers no choice of phases and gains then reproduces the measured near-field to focal peak ratio. On CTX-500-026, the measured near-field peak (8–12 mm from the exit plane, 0.4–0.6 of the focal intensity at deep settings) comes out about 7× too weak. Uniform rings match Imasonic transducers well.

The ring profile splits every ring into n_sub sub-rings with a complex weight that is the same at every focal depth. Each depth keeps one phase and gain per channel. On-axis profiles alone do not determine the weights uniquely. Without off-axis data, keep the library fit and treat the off-axis field of a ring profile as unvalidated. Off-axis scans (format) constrain the weights and are fitted together with the axial profiles.

Where to enable the ring profile Where How to enable calibration_gui, Nexus Calibration page Ring profile → fit (shared by all depths); Options… sets the fit_ring_profile options and a plane-scan file. The GUI shows the profile (plot_ring_profile) and R² per plane. refine_transducer_library, calibrate_library_entry RingProfile = 'fit'; RingProfileOptions: NSub, Smooth, NearFieldSkipMm, AmpBounds, Iterations, NStarts, Seed, HeldOut, OffAxis, OffAxisOptions. With Plot, the profile figure is saved next to the entry. config_calibration.yaml (calibration_transducer) ring_profile: fit, ring_profile_n_sub, ring_profile_smooth, ring_profile_near_field_skip_mm, ring_profile_offaxis (plane-scan file), ring_profile_offaxis_kind build_transducer_library RING_PROFILE = 'fit' or a list of combos (default 'none')

'auto' (the default everywhere) keeps an entry's profile if it has one; 'none' removes it.

ro = struct('OffAxis', 'SC CTX-500-026 (4 ch.).zip', 'OffAxisOptions', struct('Kind', 'transverse'));
[lib, fits, report] = calibrate_library_entry(lib, tran, meas, struct('RingProfile', 'fit', 'RingProfileOptions', ro));
How the profile is fitted, what changes in the entry, validation

fit_ring_profile fits the weights jointly over all measured depths, with a smoothness penalty and the near field included from 4 mm. Each ring's area-weighted mean weight is 1.

Uniform rings Ring profile, depth held out CTX-500-026 (4 rings), median R² (worst) 0.957 (0.79) 0.989 (0.93) CTX-250-009 (2 rings) 0.894 (0.87) 0.980 (0.95) CTX-250-001 (4 rings) 0.978 (0.96) 0.980 (0.96) CTX-500-026 near-field / focal ratio error 7× 33 %

Exploratory analysis: peak-normalised intensity from 4 mm, held-out depth with its channel drive refitted. "Uniform rings" here is an unregularised per-depth fit, not the shipped library fit.

What changes.

  • The profile is stored in global_model.ring_profile (n_sub, weight_abs, weight_phase_deg per sub-ring, smooth, near_field_skip_mm, fit quality).
  • All per-element arrays of the entry then refer to sub-rings. Adding, removing, or refitting a profile drops the entry's refinements (with a warning); only the depths calibrated then are stored.
  • Inline elem_phase_deg / elem_p_amp in a study config refer to the equipment rings and bypass the profile.
  • Dephased conditions are not supported with a profile.

Off-axis data. A refit from synthetic axial profiles reproduces the profiles (R² > 0.998) but not the weights. Validation on CTX-500-026 hydrophone planes at the 40 mm setting (R² of intensity normalised by the axial peak, planes held out of the fit):

Model (fitted to 12 axial profiles) Axis (40 mm) Sagittal XZ (z < 25 mm) XY 35 mm XY 40 mm (focus) −3 dB width Shipped library fit (uniform rings, rayleigh_phase_gain) 0.87 0.89 (0.26) 0.96 0.97 2.7 mm Same, gain regularisation 10× weaker (LambdaAmp 1e-3) 0.89 0.90 (0.33) 0.94 0.96 2.6 mm Uniform rings, unregularised 0.90 0.86 (0.31) 0.90 0.90 2.4 mm Ring profile, axial 0.97 0.88 (0.64) 0.88 0.87 2.4 mm Ring profile, axial + XY 35 mm plane 0.97 0.94 (0.65) 0.95 (fitted) 0.98 2.9 mm Hydrophone 2.8 mm

The shipped fit predicts the transverse planes and focal width well but misses the axis and near field. A ring profile fitted to axial profiles alone fixes the axis and loses the planes. Adding one transverse plane gives both.

Sub-ring source in the simulation

The simulation gets an annular source of sub-rings, each driven with its channel's phase and drive times its weight (ring_profile_drive). transducer.tx_calibration.ring_profile records it. Sub-rings are steered with their ring (annular.steer_r_mid_mm).

items.title: Free-Water k-Wave Drive Calibration
items.text:
Optional. kwave_calibrate_drive simulates every refined depth in free-water k-Wave as a study would resolve it, with ISPPA targeting off. It rescales the stored drive so the simulation hits the reference ISPPA (elem_p_amp × √(I_ref / I_kWave), amp_source: kwave). Phases are validated, not changed.

Why run it. In free-water k-Wave the analytical drive overshoots the reference ISPPA, consistently per transducer and almost independently of depth: by about 3 % (IGT 32-channel, 10 rings), 6–9 % (CTX-250), and 14–16 % (CTX-500), over three depths each. A study inherits that error in every ISPPA-dependent output (intensity, MI, heating) when it skips the free-water baseline. That happens with a target equal to the entry's calibration ISPPA (within 1 %; the default 30 W/cm² is the shipped reference), because PRESTUS then trusts the entry's drive (ISPPA targeting). A different target, or modules.run_water_baseline: 1, removes the error at the cost of one water simulation per run. The drive calibration removes it once per entry.

Run it.

refine_transducer_library('CTX_250_001_SC_105_010', 'my_profiles.csv', lib, struct( ...
    'KWaveDriveCalibration', true, 'KWaveDriveOptions', struct('SimConfig', 'my_study_config.yaml')));
GUI, Nexus, simulation settings, grid, and run time
  • In calibration_gui, tick k-Wave drive: calibrate in free water, after fit (per-depth mode). The simulated profiles are overlaid in green, and Save entry stores the corrected drives.
  • The Nexus Calibration page writes the unsaved fit and a kwave_drive_<combo>.m script, to run on its Run tab or on the cluster.
  • SimConfig supplies grid, code_type, and platform/HPC settings. Without it, PRESTUS runs locally with config_default (CPU on macOS).
  • GridDims (kwave_grid_dims in config_calibration.yaml) selects the free-water grid; 'auto' sizes it to the aperture and focus (grid.default_dims: 'auto').
  • Each depth is one free-water simulation: about 3–20 min per depth in 3D on 16 CPU cores, about 1 min on the axisymmetric grid. 3D removes the error; the axisymmetric grid leaves at most about 3 % (2D and 3D agree within 0.98–1.03 in ISPPA, with the same focus). Use 3D for final entries.

When the drive at the requested depth is not k-Wave-calibrated, loading an entry warns (load_transducer_from_library:uncalibratedAmplitude) and names the nearest checked depth with its R² and focal error.

Report fields

Report (kwave_drive_metrics), which also scores the absolute level that peak-normalised R² cannot show:

Field Meaning isppa_err_pct How far the analytical drive misses the reference ISPPA in k-Wave i_at_target_ratio Simulated intensity at the measured FLHM centre relative to the reference kwave_over_analytical k-Wave ISPPA over Rayleigh ISPPA at the same drive (the Rayleigh ISPPA of a shipped drive equals the reference to within 2 %) nrmse_before, nrmse_after RMS difference from the hydrophone profile scaled to the reference ISPPA, before and after correction sim_seconds, grid_points Cost

It also reports simulated ISPPA, R², and FLHM-centre error against the hydrophone profile.

BabelBrain's water_amp_calibration (BabelBrain Backend) is independent: it scales every BabelBrain run so that BabelBrain's own free-water ISPPA equals transducer.target_isppa_wcm2.

Uncalibrated-drive flag

load_transducer_from_library sets tx_calibration.amp_kwave_calibrated, true only when the drive at the requested depth comes wholly from a refinement with amp_source: kwave.

The profile files the fits read are described in Profile File Formats.

items.title: Matrix Arrays: Steering Correction
items.text:
The focal peak a matrix array delivers changes with the steering target in ways the geometric model does not predict. The steering correction scales the drive by a factor measured at a set of targets, so that a simulated condition matches what the device delivers. Only users of matrix (2D) arrays need this page.

On this page:

  • Steering Correction of Matrix Arrays: how the correction is applied, building an entry from hydrophone peaks, and its limits.

Experimental

The steering correction is not yet validated in PRESTUS against hydrophone measurements. It is on by default (transducer.matrix.use_steering_correction: true) whenever the library entry holds a correction.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You simulate a matrix (2D) array steered to targets away from its geometric focus.
  • Before you start: Hydrophone focal-peak measurements at 30–40 steering targets at one drive voltage, and the array's equipment YAML.

items.title: Steering Correction of Matrix Arrays
items.text:
A matrix (2D) array's delivered focal peak can differ from the geometric model by a factor that changes with the steering target (element directivity, crosstalk, manufacturing spread). The steering correction measures that factor at a set of targets and scales the drive by it.

How it is applied. create_matrix_karray multiplies every element amplitude by k(target) and records it in transducer.matrix.steering_k. elem_p_amp stays the nominal drive setting, and the simulated field is what the device delivers at that setting. With ISPPA targeting the results are reported at the target ISPPA either way; the correction changes the drive that achieves them: elem_p_amp × isppa_scale_p, or in volts drive_ref_v × elem_p_amp × isppa_scale_p / elem_p_amp_ref. With target_isppa_wcm2: [] the results are reported at the corrected drive. Switch it off with transducer.matrix.use_steering_correction: false.

Building an entry. Measure the focal peak at 30–40 targets spread through the steering range you will use, including its edges and the geometric focus, plus a few kept back to check the fit. Use one drive voltage and the geometric phases PRESTUS computes for each target. Write one CSV row per target, then build the entry with build_steering_correction.

CSV columns and build call Column Unit Required Meaning target_x_mm, target_y_mm, target_z_mm mm yes Steering target in the transducer frame: origin at the apex (curved) or array centre (flat), z along the beam peak_pressure_mpa MPa yes Largest pressure amplitude in the plane through the target, normal to the beam axis drive_v V no Drive voltage; rows at other voltages are scaled to the median voltage peak_x_mm, peak_y_mm mm no Where the peak was found model_pressure_mpa MPa no A modelled peak at the same drive, used instead of the Rayleigh model

Then, with the array's geometry in tr (from its equipment YAML) and tr.matrix.elem_p_amp the element amplitude that stands for the measurement drive:

% run from the PRESTUS folder; writes the library entry next to the shipped ones
sc = build_steering_correction(parameters, tr, 'steering_peaks.csv', ...
    struct('out_file', fullfile('config', 'calibration', '<serial>.yaml'), 'serial', '<serial>'));

resolve_transducer_from_serial attaches the entry to a matrix transducer given by serial (the entry for <serial> with combo.ds_serial first, then the driving-system-agnostic one, or transducer.library_path; see Library keys). Without an entry the array is simulated uncorrected. The entry stores the fit, its cross-validated errors, elem_p_amp_ref, and drive_ref_v. An inline transducer.matrix.steering_correction takes precedence.

Limits. Only the focal peak is corrected, not side lobes or field shape. The model assumes the beam along +z of the transducer frame and does not support Clover setups. The Rayleigh model treats each element as a baffled piston in free water; check it against k-Wave with a free-water run at a few targets.

What is fitted

At each measured target x, k(x) = measured / modelled focal peak, both at the same drive. The modelled peak is the largest free-field pressure in the plane through the target, normal to the beam axis, from a Rayleigh integral over the array (matrix_focal_peak, matrix_rayleigh_pressure). The measured peak is the same quantity from a hydrophone scan of that plane. fit_steering_correction fits k as one constant (scale) or a full quadratic surface in x, y, z (quadratic, 10 coefficients, linear least squares), and scores both by leave-one-out cross-validation. The default auto keeps the quadratic surface only with at least 15 targets and a median cross-validated error at most 0.8 times that of the constant. A quadratic map is not extrapolated: targets outside the measured range use the value at its edge, with a warning.

Dadgar-Kiani et al. (2026) fit such a correction with a Gaussian of the difference in MPa; PRESTUS fits the ratio, which applies to the drive at any level.

References

Dadgar-Kiani et al. (2026). Calibrated simulations for dynamic focusing of ultrasound through the temporal window. Cell Reports Methods 6:101568.

items.title: Profile File Formats
items.text:
The calibration fits read your hydrophone measurements from files. This page gives the layout of each file, how its focal depth is labelled, and how the files are named and placed, so the fits find them.

On this page:

  • Input File Formats: axial profile CSVs, plane and volume scans, depth labels, and folder naming.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You prepare hydrophone profiles for Emulating Hydrophone Profiles.
  • Before you start: Axial profiles (and optionally plane or volume scans) measured at the focal depths you use.

items.title: Input File Formats
items.text: refine_transducer_library and build_transducer_library need one axial profile CSV per transducer–driving-system combo. Steering phases are computed from the ring geometry (set_real_phases), so manufacturer phase tables are not used. Plane and volume scans are optional: they constrain a within-ring velocity profile.

items.title: Axial Profile CSV
items.text:
,Focal depths (mm),,,,,,,
Distance WRT Exit plane (mm),40.0,50.0,60.0,70.0,80.0
0.5,0.12,0.31,0.04,0.01,0.0
1.0,0.18,0.44,0.08,0.02,0.0
...
Row Content 1 (title) Label strings only; skipped 2 (depth) First cell a label (ignored); then the focal depth of each column in mm from the exit plane 3 onward (data) Axial distance from the exit plane in mm; then intensity in W/cm² at each focal depth

Rules:

  • Separator: comma. Encoding: UTF-8 (a BOM is tolerated).
  • Any number of focal-depth columns ≥ 1.
  • Axial distance starts at or below the transducer face (0 mm is fine; negative values are ignored).
  • Intensity is non-negative and always W/cm² (no units row). Trailing NaN columns are trimmed.
  • Focal depths outside the transducer's [min_foc, max_foc] give a warning. check_equipment_config(equip_path) validates the equipment YAML before a rebuild.

items.title: Focal-Depth Labels
items.text:
Column headers are nominal driver setpoints. They correspond to the FLHM centre of the measured profile, at a manufacturer-dependent threshold (focal depth convention). On the Donders profiles (2026-09-30; median |header − FLHM centre|, first 10 mm skipped):

Equipment Convention Median error Sonic Concepts CTX + TPO flhm_3db 0.03–0.26 mm (−6 dB: 1.0–7.0 mm) Imasonic + IGT 32 ch flhm_6db 0.04–0.08 mm (−3 dB: 2.1–2.6 mm) Imasonic + IGT 128 ch closest to flhm_6db 0.60–0.75 mm (−3 dB: 1.2–1.7 mm)

items.title: Depth Coverage Recommendations
items.text: Cover the full intended depth range and include the natural focal depth.

items.title: Profile Folder and File Naming
items.text:
Measured profiles are site data in local/profiles/ inside the PRESTUS root (ignored by Git), one subfolder per transducer. build_transducer_library and calibration_setup read them from there.

Folder layout, file names, and sidecar 
local/profiles/
├── IS_PCD15473_01001/
│   ├── tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch_axial.csv
│   ├── tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch_axial.yaml         ← sidecar
│   ├── tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch_acq-OPM_axial.csv  ← repeat measurement
│   ├── tran-IS_PCD15473_01001_ds-IGT_128_ch_comb_10_ch_axial.csv
│   └── sourcedata/        ← never read: vendor spreadsheets, steering tables, deprecated files
└── CTX_250_001/
    ├── tran-CTX_250_001_ds-SC_105_010_axial.csv
    └── tran-CTX_250_001_ds-SC_203_035_axial.csv

File names follow tran-{TRAN_SERIAL}_ds-{DS_SERIAL}[_acq-{LABEL}]_axial.csv, using the serials of config/equipment/ (underscores, not hyphens). acq- marks a repeat or alternative measurement of the same pair. One subfolder per transducer holds all its measurements whatever driving system recorded them.

char_data_path in the equipment YAML is relative to this folder, for example CTX_250_001/tran-CTX_250_001_ds-SC_105_010_axial.csv. Point calibration.path_input_axial (for calibration_setup) or CHAR_DATA_ROOT (for build_transducer_library) at the folder.

Sidecar. Each CSV has a YAML sidecar with the same stem, recording quantity and units, distance_reference (exit_plane | bowl), whether headers are nominal setpoints or measured positions (focal_label_is), their FLHM convention (focal_label_reference), acquisition conditions, and provenance. PRESTUS does not read sidecars: set calibration.add_FDO and calibration.focal_reference in the calibration config to match it.

items.title: Plane and Volume Scans
items.text:
Optional. Off-axis hydrophone scans for the ring-profile fit, read by read_offaxis_scans (OffAxis in RingProfileOptions; Ring profile ▸ Options… in the GUIs; ring_profile_offaxis in config_calibration.yaml).

What to measure. One transverse plane a few millimetres before the focus, at a setting that also has an axial profile, made the ring profile identifiable on CTX-500-026 (see Within-ring velocity profile). Further planes or a volume add checks (e.g. of an off-centre or tilted axis) more than constraint.

Accepted files are a Sonic Concepts FUS Metrology export or a CSV with one row per point.

Accepted files, CSV columns, and reading call

Accepted files.

  • Sonic Concepts FUS Metrology export: FUS_Metrology_Export_BableBrain.mat, its folder, or a .zip of the export folder with Planes/ and Axial/. Each entry of the cell array data needs type, focus (focal setting, mm from the exit plane), x, y, z (mm), and ISPPA.data with ISPPA.unit = 'W/cm2'. Entries of type Axial are used only to rescale the scans.
  • CSV, one row per point:
Column Meaning focus_ep_mm Focal setting the scan was recorded at [mm from the exit plane] x_mm, y_mm Lateral position [mm]; the beam axis at x = y = 0 (or use Centre = 'centroid') z_ep_mm Distance from the exit plane [mm] intensity_wcm2 Intensity [W/cm²] label (optional) Name of the scan; separates scans at the same setting 
focus_ep_mm,x_mm,y_mm,z_ep_mm,intensity_wcm2,label
40,-15.0,-15.0,35,0.012,XY 35
40,-14.5,-15.0,35,0.014,XY 35
...

[oa, scans] = read_offaxis_scans('SC CTX-500-026 (4 ch.).zip', struct('Axial', meas));
% oa: OffAxis input of fit_ring_profile; scans: maps for plotting
How scans are read and reduced

  • Kind from the coordinates. Points need not lie on a grid.

    Varying coordinates Kind Reduced to x, y (constant z) Transverse plane Azimuthally averaged radial profile x or y with z Axial plane (|x|, z) map, both sides folded together x, y, and z 3D volume (r, z) map, averaged around one axis parallel to z in each z bin

  • One scan per setting and label. Several planes at the same setting need distinct label values in a CSV; without them, their points read as one volume.

  • Absolute level. A scan is compared with the axial profile at its focal setting (within 1 mm) relative to that profile's peak, so it must be in W/cm² at the same drive. When a Sonic Concepts export includes its own axial profiles, each scan is rescaled by the ratio of the fitted axial peak to the export's at that setting.
  • Axis. The scan axis is x = y = 0, or with Centre = 'centroid' the intensity centroid of the top 50 % of a transverse plane or volume. A volume's axis is assumed parallel to z; tilt is not corrected.
  • Reduction options (OffAxisOptions): Kind (all, transverse, axial, volume, or a list), Weight (per scan, relative to one axial profile; default 1), RMaxMm (30), BinMm (radial bin, 0.5), ZBinMm (z bin of axial planes and volumes, 1; the fit's field matrix grows with the number of reduced points), Centre.

items.title: Concepts
items.text:
This page shows the steps PRESTUS takes from an MRI to a simulated field and its safety metrics, and where each step is configured. The sequence helps to place the other pages and to see which inputs a result depends on. Terms used throughout the documentation are defined in the Glossary.

On this page:

  • The Simulation Pipeline: the pipeline from MRI to outputs, and what a free-water run leaves out.

items.title: The Simulation Pipeline
items.text:
PRESTUS estimates where an ultrasound transducer on the head focuses its energy, how strong the field is inside the brain, and how much it heats the tissue. It does so in a sequence of steps, each building on the previous one:

  • MRI: the participant's T1, optionally with a T2 or UTE scan.
  • Segmentation: SimNIBS charm labels skin, skull, brain, and other tissues.
  • Transducer: geometry, drive, and calibration from the library.
  • Placement: where the transducer sits and where it aims.
  • Grid & medium: a 3D grid of tissue properties (sound speed, density, attenuation).
  • Acoustic: the pressure field of the transducer through the head (k-Wave), scaled to the intensity you asked for.
  • Thermal: heating over the sonication protocol (optional).
  • Outputs: metrics table, NIfTI maps, and an HTML report with safety checks.

Every step reads its settings from a config file (Configuring a study), and each can be switched on or off (Pipeline Modules). A simulation in free water skips segmentation, and placement and grid set-up run in reduced form (positions on a homogeneous water grid): no MRI is needed, which makes it the quickest way to try PRESTUS (First simulation).

Simulations are estimates. Tissue properties, especially of the skull, are uncertain, and results depend on the segmentation, the grid, and the placement. PRESTUS is a research tool; it is not approved for clinical use.

items.title: Configuring a Study
items.text:
All PRESTUS settings live in YAML config files, and the config decides what a run simulates: the head, the transducer and its placement, and the protocol. You never write a complete config: PRESTUS starts from its defaults, and your files contain only what differs. Every parameter is listed in Parameters.

On this page:

  • How a Config Is Assembled: the four layers load_parameters merges, and how to override settings per run.
  • Project Config Folder: setting up a project folder that pins its defaults.
  • Example Study Config: an example config for head simulations.
  • Configs From Earlier PRESTUS Versions: how renamed and retired keys are handled.
  • Editing Configs With a GUI: the Nexus, which writes the same files.
  • Prompts for Missing Tool Paths: when PRESTUS asks for missing tool paths.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To set up a study, or to change settings for one subject or run.
  • Before you start: PRESTUS installed (Installation).

items.title: How a Config Is Assembled
items.text:
load_parameters builds one parameters struct from up to four layers, each merged onto the previous one:

Layer Source Notes 1. Toolbox defaults config/config_default.yaml in the PRESTUS folder Always loaded first. Never edit it for a study. 2. Project defaults a copy of config_default.yaml in your project config folder (optional) Pins the defaults your project started with (see below). 3. Study config(s) the YAML file(s) or struct you pass in Only the values your study changes. 4. Overrides a trailing {'dotted.key', value; ...} cell Per-run changes, e.g. the subject or one row of a study manifest. 
parameters = load_parameters();                                       % defaults only
parameters = load_parameters('config_projectX.yaml', '/path/to/project/config');
parameters = load_parameters('config_a.yaml', dir_a, 'config_b.yaml', dir_b);   % merged left to right
parameters = load_parameters('config_projectX.yaml', cfg_dir, ...
                             {'subject_id', 3; 'io.output_affix', 'M1'});         % plus overrides

The merge is deep: a study file that sets only grid.resolution_mm keeps every other grid setting at its default.

Merge rules and validation

Lists of transducers (transducer(2), …) keep their own fields. One exception: medium_properties.<tissue>.absorption_fraction and absorption_coeff exclude each other, so a layer that sets one empties the other (see Heat deposition).

Before merging, keys from earlier PRESTUS versions are converted to their current names (see below). After merging, load_parameters validates the result: it resolves transducer.serial against the transducer library, checks the timing protocol and the backend combination, and turns io.output_affix into a _desc-<label> file-name entity. Keys PRESTUS does not know produce the warning prestus:unknownConfigKey, with a suggestion when it looks like a typo.

You can also change the struct in MATLAB after loading (parameters.subject_id = 2;), as in First simulation. The exception is the transducer library keys (transducer.serial, combo, library_path, and the focal_distance_ep they resolve phases for): load_parameters looks up geometry, phases, and drive from them, so set them in a file or as an override rather than in the struct afterwards.

items.title: Project Config Folder
items.text:
Keep your configs in a project folder outside the PRESTUS toolbox, and start it with prestus_config_init:

prestus_config_init('/path/to/project/config', project_name='projectX');
% optionally open the GUI to review the values:
prestus_config_init('/path/to/project/config', project_name='projectX', open_gui=true);

This writes two files:

  • config_default.yaml, a copy of the toolbox defaults (layer 2). It keeps your project's baseline fixed when PRESTUS changes its defaults later, which matters for reproducibility.
  • config_projectX.yaml, an empty study config (layer 3) for your own values.

Load them with load_parameters('config_projectX.yaml', '/path/to/project/config'). PRESTUS looks for the project config_default.yaml next to the study config, else in the folder you pass, else in the current folder (with the warning prestus:cwdDefault).

Updating a project copy of the defaults

When PRESTUS later adds new settings, a project copy made earlier does not contain them. They then take their toolbox default, and load_parameters warns (prestus:staleProjectDefault). prestus_config_upgrade(folder) replaces the copy with the current toolbox default, keeps a dated backup, and can first write the values your copy pinned differently into the study config, so the simulation settings stay the same. The Nexus offers the same under Tools ▸ Update project defaults….

items.title: Example Study Config
items.text:
A study config for head simulations typically sets the paths, the transducer, the placement, and the protocol:

# config_projectX.yaml
path:
  anat: /data/projectX/anat            # T1 (and T2/UTE) images
  t1_pattern: 'sub-%1$03d/anat/sub-%1$03d_T1w.nii.gz'   # %03d = subject_id
  seg: /data/projectX/simnibs          # SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folders
  sim: /data/projectX/sim              # simulation outputs
startup:
  simnibs_bin_path: /home/user/.conda/envs/simnibs_v4.6.0/bin

simulation:
  medium: layered
  code_type: matlab_gpu

transducer:
  serial: CTX_500_026
  combo: {ds_serial: SC_203_035}
  focal_distance_ep: 55
  target_isppa_wcm2: 30

placement:
  mode: mni
  mni:
    trans_pos_mm: [-52, -8, 58]
    focus_pos_mm: [-29, -6, 7]

timing:
  pd: 0.02
  pri: 0.2
  ptd: 20
  ptri: 20
  ptrd: 20
modules:
  run_heating_sims: 1

On a workstation without a job scheduler, also set platform: matlab: the default auto only detects SLURM or qsub and stops with an error when neither is found. The subject is usually not in the file but set per run (parameters.subject_id = 3, an override, or a study manifest).

Where to look next Topic Keys Page Paths and input images path.*, startup.* Parameters Medium and tissue properties simulation.medium, layers, medium_properties, pct.* Medium Setup, pseudo-CT Transducer transducer.* Transducer, Transducer Library Position and target placement.*, transducer.trans_pos/focus_pos Placement Protocol and heating timing.*, thermal.* Thermal Which stages run modules.* Pipeline Modules Where and how it runs platform, hpc.*, simulation.code_type, acoustic_backend HPC, Backends, k-Wave Output files io.* Outputs

items.title: Configs From Earlier PRESTUS Versions
items.text:
load_parameters reads configs written for PRESTUS v0.5.0 or later. It converts each renamed key to its current name, in every config layer and in the overrides, and lists the conversions in one warning (prestus:renamedConfigKey); keys without a replacement are dropped. Old keys without an exact counterpart stop the run (see below), as does a layer that sets an old key and its current name to different values (prestus:configKeyConflict). Update the config with the names from that list; the Nexus marks the same keys when you open the file.

Study scripts written for earlier versions run as well. Old key names a script sets on the struct after loading (parameters.code_type = 'cpp_gpu', or a transducer read from an old YAML file) are converted when the run starts, with the same warning. The call form before v0.6.0, prestus_pipeline_start(subject_id, parameters), and the v0.5.0 functions single_subject_pipeline, single_subject_pipeline_with_slurm, and single_subject_pipeline_with_qsub still work and warn (prestus:legacyCallForm, prestus:legacyFunction) with the current call to use instead.

Old keys without a current name

A few old keys have no exact counterpart. These stop the run (prestus:legacyConfigKey) with a message naming the key to set instead:

Old key Set instead smooth_window [voxels] headmodel.smooth_fwhm_mm [mm] expected_focal_distance_mm transducer.focal_distance_ep (from the exit plane) or transducer.focal_distance_bowl (from the bowl apex); when every transducer in the same file sets one of them, the old key is ignored with a warning (prestus:legacyRedundantKey) pseudoCT_variant: marquet pct.mapping_density, pct.mapping_soundspeed, pct.mapping_attenuation calibration.weights: 0 calibration.opt_weights (now 0 = uniform weighting) subject_subfolder: 0, custom seg_labels not supported: outputs always go to sub-XXX folders, and the SimNIBS charm labels are fixed

A config that sets an old key and its current name to different values also stops the run. Conversion covers names only: defaults that changed since your config was written (for example transducer.target_isppa_wcm2) apply unless the config sets them, as listed in the changelog. calibration.skip_front_peak_mm kept its name but is now measured from the exit plane rather than the bowl apex.

items.title: Editing Configs With a GUI
items.text: The PRESTUS Nexus (GUI) is a desktop app that writes the same YAML files, checks the config as you type and shows a placement viewer. It writes only the values that differ from the defaults, so its files load with load_parameters like hand-written ones.

items.title: Prompts for Missing Tool Paths
items.text: Missing tool paths (startup.simnibs_bin_path, hpc.ld_library_path) only prompt for input in an interactive MATLAB desktop session with simulation.interactive: 1. Otherwise PRESTUS warns and continues, so batch and cluster runs never wait on a dialog.

items.title: Coordinate Reference Systems
items.text:
A position given in the wrong coordinate space puts the transducer or the focus in the wrong part of the head, in the case of a wrong image header by tens of millimetres. PRESTUS converts every externally given position once to T1 voxel indices and maps results back to T1 and MNI space. This page defines each space and the functions that convert between them.

On this page:

  • Canonical Coordinate Convention: the entry-point space and where conversion happens.
  • Coordinate Spaces: voxel, RAS, Localite, and MNI spaces.
  • Coordinate Flow for Head Models: from neuronavigation to simulation and back.
  • Coordinate Flow for Phantoms and Water: positions and an optional RAS affine for phantom grids.
  • MNI Voxel Order and Laterality: why MNI laterality needs no manual flip.
  • Localite Planning Image Header: which header to use for Localite coordinates.
  • SimNIBS Warps and Transforms: the SimNIBS warps and point transforms.
  • NIfTI Affine in MATLAB: 1-based voxels and the NIfTI affine.

At a glance

  • When you need it: When positions end up in the wrong place, or before changing any coordinate transform in the code.
  • Before you start: Nothing; for the basic idea see Glossary.

items.title: Canonical Coordinate Convention
items.text: RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) mm is the entry-point space in PRESTUS. Localite markers and any externally specified positions arrive in RAS mm. They are converted once to T1 voxel indices via ras_to_grid() and stored in parameters.transducer.trans_pos / focus_pos. Everything downstream of that call works in voxel indices. The simulation grid passed to k-Wave uses 1-based MATLAB voxel indices and is anatomy-agnostic, because k-Wave operates in grid space, not world space.

items.title: Coordinate Spaces
items.text: Name Unit Label Description Simulation grid voxels (1-based) grid k-Wave internal space: the T1 voxel grid rescaled to grid.resolution_mm, rotated per grid.mode (focal_axis, the default, and transducer_axis turn the beam axis onto z; ras_plus keeps the T1 axes) and cropped. planimg.transf maps T1 voxels to this grid. Subject / scanner space mm ras_plus RAS mm in the subject's native scanner frame. PRESTUS's entry-point space: Localite markers and external coordinates arrive in RAS mm and are converted to T1 voxels via ras_to_grid(). Localite planning image mm ras_plus (adjusted header) Subject space expressed via the diagonal affine written by canonical_affine_transform. Voxel-to-world mapping is world = (voxel − 1) × voxel_size_mm for 1-based PRESTUS voxels (no rotation). See Save Localite planning image. MNI space mm mni MNI152 standard space of FSL's 1 mm template (MNI152NLin6Asym, the template SimNIBS ships), standard world-mm convention (negative X = left, positive X = right, the same laterality sense as RAS). The template's voxel array is stored in LAS order, but going through the NIfTI affine (as ras_to_grid()/transform_coordinates() do) accounts for that. See MNI voxel order and laterality. MNI voxel voxels (1-based) (unnamed) Integer indices into an MNI template volume (e.g. 182×218×182 for SimNIBS's toMNI/final_tissues_MNI.nii.gz). Convert via the template's NIfTI affine.

items.title: Coordinate Flow for Head Models
items.text:
Localite XML
  → neuronav_compute_series_statistics   [RAS mm, native]
  → localite_matrix_to_positions         [RAS mm]  → ras_to_grid() → [T1 voxels]
                                          stored in parameters.transducer.trans_pos / focus_pos
  → grid_transducer_location             [T1 voxels] → planimg.transf → [sim-grid voxels]
  → k-Wave simulation                    [sim-grid voxels]
  → nifti_to_t1w                         [T1 voxels]    ← planimg.inv_transf
  → nifti_to_mni                         [MNI voxels]   ← SimNIBS warp

Key rule: ras_to_grid() / grid_to_ras() are the sole boundary between RAS mm and T1 voxel indices (1-based). Downstream of that call, everything is voxels. Do not replicate affine inversion elsewhere: for several points or a sub-voxel (unrounded) index, use ras_to_voxel(), which ras_to_grid() itself calls. Other 4×4 affines (grid transforms, SimNIBS matrices) are inverted with affine_inverse(), which reads both conventions and keeps the fixed row or column exact.

items.title: Coordinate Flow for Phantoms and Water
items.text:
Phantom and water grids have no patient-space anchor, so grid indices are arbitrary. Transducer and focus positions are either specified directly as grid voxel indices via parameters.transducer.trans_pos / focus_pos, or placed automatically (transducer at the near face, focus at the expected focal distance).

To register phantom outputs spatially (for example to overlay a simulated focal profile on a planning image, or to compare with k-Plan), set:

grid:
  origin_ras_mm: [x, y, z]   # RAS mm of voxel [1,1,1]

PRESTUS then writes output NIfTIs with a diagonal RAS affine built from origin_ras_mm and grid.resolution_mm, so they open in ITK-SNAP, 3D Slicer and k-Plan with correct spatial positioning. The simulation itself is unaffected.

The phantom affine 
T = [ res   0    0   ox ]
    [  0   res   0   oy ]
    [  0    0   res  oz ]
    [  0    0    0    1 ]

items.title: MNI Voxel Order and Laterality
items.text:
The MNI152 template's voxel array is stored in LAS order (its sform has a negative X scale factor). This is a storage-order detail only: world-mm coordinates derived through the NIfTI affine (as ras_to_grid() and transform_coordinates() always do) come out in standard MNI convention, negative X = left hemisphere, positive X = right, with no manual flip.

The side_order clamp in neuronav_convert_native_to_MNI

neuronav_convert_native_to_MNI has a separate, unrelated side_order-conditional block that pins the transducer's (not the target's) MNI voxel X-coordinate to the FOV edge (min_voxel_mni/max_voxel_mni). This is a visualisation/robustness workaround for the cropped out-of-skull MNI window, not a laterality correction. It only runs when the optional side_order argument is supplied, and it never touches the target coordinate. Laterality is correct by construction once you go through the affine.

items.title: Localite Planning Image Header
items.text:
Neuronavigation software (e.g. Localite TMS Navigator) writes a planning T1 with a diagonal, zero-origin affine:

affine = diag([voxel_size_mm, voxel_size_mm, voxel_size_mm, 1])

The "RAS mm" values stored in Localite XML trigger matrices are therefore planning-image space coordinates (world = voxel_0 × voxel_size_mm, with voxel_0 the 0-based NIfTI index), not scanner-isocenter-relative RAS mm. ras_to_grid() called with the planning T1 header inverts this back to the 1-based PRESTUS voxel (voxel = round(localite_mm / voxel_size_mm) + 1).

Do not re-project Localite coordinates using the SimNIBS m2m T1 header

The m2m T1 (m2m_{sub_id}/T1.nii.gz) has a full world-space affine (non-zero origin, possible small rotation). Calling ras_to_grid(localite_mm, simnibs_t1_header) applies the wrong inverse affine and shifts positions by tens of millimetres.

When the same T1 was used for both neuronavigation and SimNIBS input, the m2m T1 and the planning T1 share the same voxel grid: SimNIBS preserves the voxel dimensions and layout and updates only the affine. Voxel indices from the planning T1 (ras_to_grid(localite_mm, planning_t1_header)) are then directly valid for PRESTUS simulations that load the m2m T1, with no reprojection. If the planning T1 and the SimNIBS input T1 differ (different acquisitions, different resolution), a registration step is required before the voxel indices can be used with the m2m T1.

items.title: SimNIBS Warps and Transforms
items.text:
PRESTUS reuses nonlinear warp fields produced by SimNIBS/charm:

  • Conform2MNI_nonl.nii.gz: subject native → MNI (displacement field, mm)
  • MNI2Conform_nonl.nii.gz: MNI → subject native (inverse displacement field, mm)

The segmentation (final_tissues.nii.gz) is the spatial anchor for these warps. If the planning T1 differs from the segmentation T1, the affine mismatch is handled in neuronav_convert_native_to_MNI.

For point (coordinate) transforms, mni2subject_coords_LDfix / subject2mni_coords_LDfix wrap the SimNIBS CLI with charm's nonlinear warp (nonl), the only MNI transform SimNIBS 4 writes. The warp is most accurate inside the brain and less exact near the scalp, so mni transducer placement (see MNI placement) converts both points via mni → nonl warp → RAS+ → grid and then snaps the transducer point to the scalp.

items.title: NIfTI Affine in MATLAB
items.text:
niftiinfo() stores the NIfTI voxel-to-world affine in Transform.T (transposed, row-vector convention). Like the NIfTI standard, it takes 0-based voxel indices, whereas PRESTUS voxels are 1-based MATLAB indices into the niftiread array:

  • World from PRESTUS voxel: world = T' * [vox - 1; 1] (grid_to_ras)
  • PRESTUS voxel from world: vox = round(T' \ [world; 1]) + 1 (ras_to_grid; ras_to_voxel without the rounding)

PRESTUS reorders the T1 and segmentation voxels to RAS+ when it loads them (axis permutations and flips, no resampling). The affine keeps any oblique rotation, so every voxel keeps its world position.

Always use ras_to_grid() / grid_to_ras() rather than applying Transform.T to voxel indices directly. Affines composed on 1-based grids (e.g. grid_to_ras_affine) must include the 1-based → 0-based shift before Transform.T. Such an affine becomes a NIfTI header via nifti_affine_from_1based.

items.title: Developer Guide
items.text:
Many changes to PRESTUS touch more than one file: a new config key also needs a row in the parameter docs, and a change to a cached stage needs an updated cache signature. This page shows how the code is organised and what happens during a run, so that you know where a change belongs, what else to update, and which checks to run before you commit.

On this page:

  • Pipeline and Design Principles: the pipeline in one paragraph and the three ideas that hold the code together.
  • Code Layout: which folder holds which subsystem, and the file to start reading at.
  • Steps of a Run: the steps of a run in order, from loading the config to writing outputs.
  • Required Updates per Change: what to edit, what else to update, and which check catches an omission.
  • Pre-Commit Checks: the checks CI runs, and which test levels a change needs.
  • Nexus Code Structure: how the Nexus builds its forms, and which Python file does what.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Before your first change to the pipeline, the config, or the Nexus.
  • Before you start: A working installation (Installation) and one finished simulation (First Simulation).

items.title: Pipeline and Design Principles
items.text:
PRESTUS turns one configuration into one simulation. The configuration is a set of YAML files merged into a single MATLAB struct, parameters. The pipeline then runs a fixed sequence of stages: segment the head, place the transducer, build the grid and the tissue properties, simulate the sound field, simulate heating, and write reports. Each stage receives what it needs as function arguments and returns its results, so a stage can be read, tested, and skipped on its own.

Three ideas hold the code together:

  • The config is the interface. Every behaviour a user can choose is a key in config/config_default.yaml. Code reads its settings from parameters, not from globals.
  • Expensive stages are cached. Grid, medium, acoustic, and thermal results are saved under the subject's cache/ folder. A re-run reuses them; grid, medium, and acoustic caches are first checked against the settings they were made with.
  • Results are reported at a free-water intensity. Simulations run at a nominal drive, and the field is scaled afterwards so that the same transducer in water would give the requested ISPPA.

The Nexus is a separate Python application. It edits the YAML and starts MATLAB; it never simulates.

items.title: Code Layout
items.text:
Folder Holds Start reading at functions/core/ Config loading, output folders, logging load_parameters.m functions/prestus_pipeline.m The stage sequence this file functions/head/, medium/ Segmentation, head preprocessing, tissue properties medium_setup.m functions/transducer/, source/ Transducer geometry, placement, k-Wave source source_sensor_setup.m functions/acoustic/, thermal/ Solver calls and their analysis acoustic_stage.m, thermal_stage.m functions/transform/ Coordinate conversions ras_to_grid.m functions/calibration/ Fitting transducers to hydrophone data refine_transducer_library.m functions/hpc/ SLURM and qsub submission hpc_submit_job.m functions/report/, group/ Subject and group reports generate_simulation_report.m functions/helper/ Shared utilities, cache signatures, sidecars cache_signature.m config/ Defaults, equipment library, calibrations config_default.yaml nexus/ The Nexus (Python, PyQt6) prestus_nexus/app.py tests/ MATLAB tests, grouped in levels run_all_tests.m tests/docs/ Doc generator and checkers run in CI doc/ This documentation (MkDocs) mkdocs.yaml for the navigation

Functions lists every MATLAB function with a one-line description.

items.title: Steps of a Run
items.text:
1. Load. load_parameters merges the toolbox defaults, an optional project copy of the defaults, the study YAML, and any overrides, in that order. It then fills in derived values, such as the transducer geometry from the equipment library, and validates the result.
  2. Decide where to run. prestus_pipeline_start runs the pipeline in the current MATLAB session or submits it as a cluster job. Some modes (several transducers fired separately, several intensities, uncertainty) split into chained jobs.
  3. Place. The placement stage turns the chosen placement method into transducer and focus positions in T1 voxels. This is the only place where RAS millimetres become voxels.
  4. Build the head model. The grid stage crops and resamples the head onto the simulation grid; the medium stage maps tissue labels (or a pseudo-CT) to sound speed, density, and attenuation.
  5. Simulate sound. The source stage builds the transducer on the grid. A free-water run of the same source gives the baseline intensity, and the acoustic stage calls the chosen solver (k-Wave, jwave or BabelBrain) and scales the field to the target ISPPA.
  6. Simulate heat. The thermal stage runs the sonication protocol on the scaled field.
  7. Write outputs. Analysis functions write the metrics CSV, NIfTI maps and the HTML report to the subject's output folder.

The stage table in How PRESTUS Works gives each stage's functions, inputs, and cache files. Each stage can be switched off with a modules.* flag (Pipeline Modules).

items.title: Required Updates per Change
items.text:
To Edit Also update Checked by Add a config key config/config_default.yaml, with a comment (the Nexus shows it as help) a row on the matching Parameters page check_param_docs.py, Nexus test_schema.py Read a key the defaults do not define the reading function an entry under extra: in nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml Nexus test_schema.py Rename a released key config_default.yaml an entry under deprecated: in overlay.yaml; upgrade_config_keys then converts old configs Nexus test_schema.py Change what a cached stage computes the stage function cache_signature.m for that stage, so old caches are rejected test_cache_signature.m Add an output a later run can start from the writing stage a JSON sidecar via write_sidecar check_sidecar_signature on reuse Add a function a new file with a first help line % NAME Short description nothing: the function index is generated gen_function_index.py --check Add a test tests/test_*.m the test's level in run_all_tests.m test_suite_wiring Change a coordinate transform read Coordinate Systems first unit and demo tests Change results a line in the changelog with ⚠️ and the action users must take physics and golden-metric tests

Docs describe current behaviour as tasks, and the changelog has one line per change (Contributing).

items.title: Pre-Commit Checks
items.text:
Run the checks CI runs before you commit:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt   # once: the docs toolchain CI uses
python tests/docs/gen_function_index.py --check
python tests/docs/check_param_docs.py
python tests/docs/check_links.py
python tests/docs/check_images.py
zensical build --strict -f mkdocs.yaml           # writes site/ (gitignored); preview: zensical serve -f mkdocs.yaml
(cd nexus && python -m pytest -q -m "not matlab")
matlab -batch "cd tests; run_all_tests('unit')"

Unit tests need no data. A change to the physics needs run_all_tests('physics') as well; a change to the pipeline needs the demo levels, which use the demo subject. Testing lists every level, the data it needs, and its run time.

items.title: Nexus Code Structure
items.text:
The Nexus builds its forms from config_default.yaml: every key becomes a field and its comment becomes the help text (schema.py). overlay.yaml adds what the YAML cannot say: widget types, choices, units, advanced flags, and the extra and deprecated keys. A new config key therefore appears in the Nexus without Python changes.

File Does model.py, merge.py, yamlio.py Hold the study config and merge and write it the way MATLAB reads it checks.py The Issues panel: checks run before MATLAB sees the config quickstart.py The QuickStart tab's logic launcher.py, remote.py, jobs.py Run locally, submit over SSH, follow cluster jobs bridge.py The persistent MATLAB session for the Calibration and Localite pages (functions/gui/nexus_bridge.m) results.py Finds the runs in a subject's output folder ui/ One module per tab or page; main_window.py assembles them

The Nexus tests run without MATLAB (pytest -m "not matlab"); the tests marked matlab check the round trip through MATLAB.

items.title: Further Reading
items.text:
• How PRESTUS Works: config layers, chained jobs, stage inputs and outputs, caches, intensity scaling.
  • Coordinate Systems: before touching any position or transform.
  • Testing: test levels and how to add a test.
  • Contributing: issues, pull requests, doc and changelog style.

items.title: First Simulation
items.text:
This page takes you from a fresh installation to a finished simulation and its outputs. It starts in free water (no MRI, no SimNIBS, a few minutes on a CPU) and then points to what changes for a head simulation.

On this page:

  • 1. Run a Free-Water Simulation: a complete run in MATLAB and the files it writes.
  • 2. Use a Transducer From the Library: naming a device instead of typing its geometry and drive.
  • 3. Set Up a Head Simulation: the inputs and settings a head simulation adds.
  • 4. Next Steps: where to go for study configs, the Nexus, and larger studies.

At a glance

  • When you need it: After installing, to run PRESTUS for the first time.
  • Before you start: PRESTUS and its MATLAB dependencies installed (Installation); SimNIBS only from step 3 on.

If terms such as exit plane, ISPPA, or free-water baseline are new to you, keep the glossary open alongside.

If you prefer forms to code, the PRESTUS Nexus builds the same config from a T1 and the defaults, and runs it. The steps below show what the Nexus writes for you.

items.title: 1. Run a Free-Water Simulation
items.text:
Free water needs no images: the transducer sits in a homogeneous water grid. The settings below are the ones the pipeline test tests/test_integration_water.m runs (a single-element 250 kHz bowl on a small 1 mm grid).

prestus_setup(Check=false);                   % PRESTUS on the path (in the PRESTUS folder)

out = fullfile(tempdir, 'prestus_first');  mkdir(out);

parameters = load_parameters();               % toolbox defaults only
parameters.subject_id = 1;
parameters.platform   = 'matlab';             % run in this MATLAB session
parameters.path.sim   = out;                  % outputs
parameters.path.anat  = out;                  % not used in water, but must be set
parameters.path.seg   = out;

parameters.simulation.medium    = 'water';
parameters.simulation.code_type = 'matlab_cpu';   % 'matlab_gpu' with a GPU

parameters.grid.resolution_mm = 1.0;          % coarse grid for speed
parameters.grid.default_dims  = [72, 72, 128];
parameters.modules.run_posthoc_water_sims = 0;

% single-element annular bowl, driven at elem_p_amp (no ISPPA scaling)
parameters.transducer.type = 'annular';
parameters.transducer.freq_hz = 250e3;
parameters.transducer.annular.elem_n          = 1;
parameters.transducer.annular.elem_id_mm      = 0;
parameters.transducer.annular.elem_od_mm      = 32.0;
parameters.transducer.annular.curv_radius_mm  = 63.2;
parameters.transducer.annular.dist_geom_ep_mm = 52.38;
parameters.transducer.annular.elem_p_amp      = 91590;
parameters.transducer.annular.elem_phase_deg  = 0;
parameters.transducer.target_isppa_wcm2       = [];

% transducer (bowl apex) and focus in grid voxels, beam along z
parameters.transducer.trans_pos = [36, 36, 5];
parameters.transducer.focus_pos = [36, 36, 64];

prestus_pipeline_start(parameters);

The run takes a few minutes on a CPU. When it finishes, out/sub-001/ holds the results:

  • sub-001_water.csv: the metrics table (ISPPA, focal distance, focal volume, …);
  • sub-001_water_report.html: the HTML report with the safety dashboard and figures;
  • nii/, img/, log/, and cache/: maps, figures, the run log, and intermediate files.

Reading your results explains what to check first; Outputs lists every file and column.

items.title: 2. Use a Transducer From the Library
items.text:
Real studies rarely type in element geometry and drive. PRESTUS ships an equipment and calibration library: name the transducer and its driving system, set the focal depth and the free-water intensity you want, and PRESTUS fills in geometry, phases, and drive. The library is resolved when the config is loaded, so put these keys in a YAML file rather than setting them in MATLAB afterwards:

# config_first.yaml
transducer:
  serial: CTX_500_026            # an entry in config/equipment
  combo:
    ds_serial: SC_203_035        # selects its calibration entry for this driving system
  focal_distance_ep: 50          # focal depth setting, mm from the exit plane
  target_isppa_wcm2: 30          # report results at 30 W/cm² free-water ISPPA

parameters = load_parameters('config_first.yaml', pwd);
% ... then the same subject, path, simulation and grid settings as in step 1
%     (without the transducer geometry lines), and prestus_pipeline_start(parameters)

With a target ISPPA set, PRESTUS also runs a short free-water baseline and scales the field to that intensity (ISPPA targeting). The available devices, how the library works, and how to calibrate your own are described in Transducer Library.

items.title: 3. Set Up a Head Simulation
items.text:
A head (layered) simulation adds an MRI, a SimNIBS segmentation, and a target. Compared to step 2 you need:

What Where it is set See T1 (optionally T2/UTE) per subject path.anat, path.t1_pattern, path.t2_pattern Configuring a study SimNIBS installation and segmentation folder startup.simnibs_bin_path, path.seg Installation Medium simulation.medium: layered Medium Setup Transducer position and target transducer.trans_pos/focus_pos, or a placement.mode Placement Sonication protocol (for heating) timing.*, modules.run_heating_sims: 1 Thermal

On the first run PRESTUS runs SimNIBS charm (this takes an hour or more); later runs reuse the segmentation unless io.overwrite_simnibs is set. To segment first and simulate later, set modules.segmentation_only: 1. Head simulations are much larger than step 1: use a GPU (simulation.code_type: cpp_gpu, recommended once the C++ binaries are installed, or matlab_gpu, see k-Wave) or a cluster (HPC). Thermal simulations are off by default (modules.run_heating_sims: 0); switch them on once the acoustic result looks right.

items.title: 4. Next Steps
items.text:
• Keep your settings in a project folder and a study config: Configuring a study.
  • Prefer forms to YAML: PRESTUS Nexus.
  • Use subject-specific skull properties from a UTE scan: pseudo-CT.
  • Re-run only part of the pipeline: Pipeline Modules.
  • Many subjects or conditions: Group analysis.
  • Sweeps over intensities, several transducers, sequences, or tissue-property uncertainty: Advanced modes.

items.title: Demos and Examples
items.text:

  • A 3D demo on SimNIBS' Ernie head as a DataLad dataset. It was made with an earlier PRESTUS version, but shows one way to organise data.
  • examples/ in the toolbox holds runnable scripts (calibration, Localite, pseudo-CT, uncertainty); see examples/README.md.

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
This page defines the terms the PRESTUS documentation uses, grouped by topic; for the overall workflow see Concepts.

On this page:

  • Transducer and Equipment: the device and its driving system, reference points on the bowl, focal depth, and calibration.
  • Intensity and Safety Metrics: free-water and in-situ intensity, MI, temperature rise, CEM43, and the ITRUSST levels.
  • Head Model: segmentation, media and their properties, pseudo-CT, placement modes, and coordinate spaces.
  • Simulation: solvers, grid and sampling, the sonication protocol, and where a run executes.
  • Files and Runs: study config, output affix, cache, and study manifest.

items.title: Transducer and Equipment
items.text: Transducer The device that emits the ultrasound. PRESTUS models focused, bowl-shaped transducers. Annular array A transducer made of concentric rings. Changing the phase of each ring moves the focus along the beam axis (deeper or shallower), but not sideways. Most TUS transducers are annular. See Transducer Definition. Matrix array A transducer made of many small elements that can steer the focus in 3D. Driving system The electronics that drive the transducer (e.g. Sonic Concepts TPO, IGT). The same transducer behaves slightly differently with different driving systems, so calibrations are per transducer and driving-system pair. Serial, combo The identifiers of a transducer (transducer.serial) and its driving system (transducer.combo.ds_serial) in the shipped transducer library. Setting them fills in geometry, phases, and drive. Bowl apex The centre of the back of the transducer bowl. PRESTUS positions the transducer by this point (transducer.trans_pos). Exit plane The plane of the transducer's front face, where the ultrasound leaves the device. Focal depths are usually given from here. Geometric focus The natural focus of the bowl, at its centre of curvature, without any phase steering. Focal depth setting (transducer.focal_distance_ep) The depth, from the exit plane, that the device is set to focus at. For annular arrays it selects the ring phases. Target depth The distance from the exit plane to the target you planned. Ideally it matches the focal depth setting; if not, the simulated focus lands at the setting, not at the target. FLHM Focal Length at Half Maximum: the stretch of the beam axis where the intensity is above half its peak. Manufacturers quote focal depths as the centre of this stretch. See Calibration. Calibration Fitting the phases and drive of the simulated transducer so that its field in water matches measurements (hydrophone profiles) of the real device. See Calibration.

items.title: Intensity and Safety Metrics
items.text: Free water A simulation in water only, without a head. Measurements and manufacturer specifications refer to free water. ISPPA Spatial-peak pulse-average intensity (W/cm²): the highest intensity in the field, averaged over the duration of a pulse. PRESTUS reports it in free water and in each tissue (e.g. Isppa_brain). Target ISPPA (transducer.target_isppa_wcm2, default 30 W/cm²) The free-water ISPPA you want to deliver. PRESTUS scales the simulated head field so that the same drive would give this ISPPA in free water (ISPPA targeting). Free-water baseline A short free-water simulation of the same transducer that PRESTUS runs to know what ISPPA the simulated drive gives. It is the reference for that scaling. In situ In the tissue, after the skull. The in-situ intensity at the target is usually much lower than the free-water value, mainly because of the skull. Ipa, Ita Pulse-average and time-average intensity at a location. Ita includes the off-time of the protocol (the duty cycle). See Outputs. MI Mechanical index, a measure of the risk of cavitation (peak negative pressure in MPa divided by the square root of the frequency in MHz). MI_tc is the transcranial MI inside the skull. Temperature rise The increase over the starting temperature (37 °C by default) during the protocol.
