  • Property uncertainty: the shear properties come from few ex vivo skulls (Pichardo et al. 2017: 3 formalin-fixed skulls plus 1 for validation; Gao et al. 2026: 1 skull). Gao et al. note that no single property set fits all incidence angles, so treat absolute values with caution.
  • Caches: the acoustic result cache is not keyed on the backend. Use a distinct io.output_affix when comparing kwave and kwave_elastic runs.
References
  • Gao, Y., et al. Influence of shear waves on transcranial ultrasound propagation in cortical brain regions. IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng. 73(3):1298–1306 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1109/TBME.2025.3603836
  • Pichardo, S., et al. A viscoelastic model for the prediction of transcranial ultrasound propagation: application for the estimation of shear acoustic properties in the human skull. Phys. Med. Biol. 62(17):6938 (2017). https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6560/aa7ccc
  • White, P. J., Clement, G. T., & Hynynen, K. Longitudinal and shear mode ultrasound propagation in human skull bone. Ultrasound Med. Biol. 32(7):1085–1096 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2006.03.015

items.title: Medium Properties
items.text:
The medium sets the sound speed, density, and attenuation the simulated wave travels through, and the thermal properties that govern heating. Whether you simulate free water or a head, and which tissue properties you assume, therefore shapes the predicted focus, intensity, and temperature rise. This page shows how to choose the medium and which tissue properties PRESTUS assumes by default.

On this page:

  • Choosing the Medium: the water, layered, and phantom media and what each needs.
  • Default Tissue Properties: the acoustic and thermal defaults per tissue, and how much of the attenuation heats the tissue.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To choose between a free-water and a head simulation, or to change tissue properties (e.g. for a more conservative estimate).
  • Before you start: Nothing; the defaults apply until you change them.

items.title: Choosing the Medium
items.text:
Set simulation.medium to one of three values:

Medium What is simulated Needs water The transducer in homogeneous water, placed at the inner edge of the requested PML layer. Free-water specifications and measurements refer to this. No images layered A head built from the SimNIBS segmentation. With the default layers and a charm segmentation: water (including CSF), brain, skin, cortical skull bone, and trabecular skull bone; the default skull layer has no charm label and is dropped. See Layer mapping and smoothing. The skull can instead take voxel-wise properties from a (pseudo-)CT. T1 (and T2/UTE), SimNIBS phantom A designed test object. The segmentation file is mapped onto medium masks without rotation, cropping, or other preprocessing. A final_tissues.nii.gz in a (dummy) SimNIBS output folder 
simulation:
  medium: layered

Which layers a layered simulation contains is set under layers. A layer whose segmentation label is missing is dropped from the run. The HTML report lists the layers that were modelled and their properties.

A phantom NIfTI holds artificial layers of a SimNIBS segmentation. It covers the simulation domain only: the PML is added outside the grid. Its voxels must be isotropic. The phantom medium accepts the same layers flexibility as layered, but applies no image processing, so 2D phantoms are a quick way to benchmark or debug.

items.title: Default Tissue Properties
items.text:
The properties below apply in a full layered simulation. They are set under medium_properties in config_default.yaml (Parameters) and can be changed per tissue in your study config, for example for a more conservative estimate of intensity or heating. The defaults follow the literature and commercially available tools; they are not ground truth. The uncertainty mode runs the ITRUSST bounds for you.

Tissue Densitykg/m³ Sound speedm/s Attenuation coefficientdB/(cm·MHzy) Power lawy Water 994 1500 0.00217 2 Brain 1046 1546 0.59 1.2 Skin 1090 1610 0.4 1 Skull (single layer) 1850 2800 13.3 1 Skull (cortical) 1850 2800 13.3 1 Skull (trabecular) 1700 2300 13.3 1

Additional parameters for thermal simulations:

Tissue Thermal conductivityW/(m·K) Specific heatJ/(kg·K) PerfusionmL/min/kg Absorption fraction Equivalent absorption coefficientdB/(cm·MHzy) Water 0.6 4178 0 1 0.00217 Brain 0.51 3630 559 1 0.59 Skin 0.37 3391 106 1 0.4 Skull (single layer) 0.32 1793 20 0.28 3.78 Skull (cortical) 0.32 1313 10 0.28 3.78 Skull (trabecular) 0.32 2274 30 0.28 3.78

For thermal simulations, PRESTUS uses only part of the attenuation as absorbed energy in the bioheat equation. Each tissue sets either absorption_fraction (a fraction of alpha_coeff) or absorption_coeff (a coefficient in dB/(cm·MHz^y) used directly); setting one empties the other (Heat deposition). The defaults set absorption_fraction; absorption_coeff stays empty.

The skull default of 0.28 lies between the BabelBrain default (16 %) and the k-Plan default (100 %). More measurements are needed to narrow the uncertainty about how much acoustic energy the skull absorbs.

Origin of skull absorption fraction

The bulk attenuation coefficient includes contributions from both longitudinal and shear waves. Longitudinal waves contribute most (about 80 %, Wang et al., 2018) to absorption and heating in the skull (Pinton et al., 2012; White et al., 2006). For longitudinal and shear waves, absorption values of 2.7 dB/(cm·MHz) and 5.4 dB/(cm·MHz) have been reported (Pinton et al., 2012), with a bulk attenuation of 13.3 dB/(cm·MHz). PRESTUS therefore assumes absorption fraction = (longitudinal absorption + 0.2 × shear absorption) / bulk attenuation = (2.7 + 0.2 × 5.4) / 13.3 = 0.28. The equivalent absorption_coeff is 2.7 + 0.2 × 5.4 = 3.78 dB/(cm·MHz).

References
  • Pinton, G., Aubry, J., Bossy, E., Muller, M., Pernot, M., & Tanter, M. Attenuation, scattering, and absorption of ultrasound in the skull bone. Med Phys 39, 299–307 (2012). https://doi.org/10.1118/1.3668316
  • Wang, X.-D., Lin, W.-J., Su, C., & Wang, X.-M. Influence of mode conversions in the skull on transcranial focused ultrasound and temperature fields utilizing the wave field separation method: A numerical study. Chin Phys B 27, 024302 (2018). https://doi.org/10.1088/1674-1056/27/2/024302
  • White, P. J., Clement, G. T., & Hynynen, K. Longitudinal and shear mode ultrasound propagation in human skull bone. Ultrasound Med Biol 32, 1085–1096 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2006.03.015

items.title: Pipeline Modules
items.text:
A run segments the head, places the transducer, and simulates acoustics and heating; segmentation alone can take an hour or more. Each stage of prestus_pipeline is switched on or off with a modules.* flag in the config. This allows partial runs: re-running only the analysis after changing output thresholds, or stopping after segmentation before committing to a full simulation.

On this page:

  • Pipeline Stages: the stage order and the flag of each stage.
  • Partial Runs: the settings for the common partial runs.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To run only part of the pipeline, e.g. segmentation first, or heating on top of an earlier acoustic run.
  • Before you start: Nothing.

items.title: Pipeline Stages
items.text:
prestus_pipeline_start decides where a run executes (local MATLAB or an HPC job) and hands uncertainty, pose-workflow, async multi-transducer, and multi-ISPPA runs to their own pipelines (pose workflow: Time Reversal). prestus_pipeline then runs the stages below. How PRESTUS works describes what each stage reads, writes, and caches.

load_parameters                 toolbox default → project default → study config (+ overrides)
      │
prestus_pipeline_start          platform: matlab | slurm | qsub;  special modes, in this order:
      │                           simulation.uncertainty = 1           → uncertainty_pipeline
      │                           time_reversal.pose_workflow.enabled  → pose_workflow_pipeline
      │                           async coupling                       → async_transducer_pipeline
      │                           target_isppa_wcm2 is a vector        → multi_isppa_pipeline
      │
prestus_pipeline
      │  special modes (run instead of the stages below):
      │    simulation.uncertainty = 1          → uncertainty_pipeline
      │    target_isppa_wcm2 is a vector       → multi_isppa_pipeline
      │    time_reversal.pose_workflow.enabled → pose_workflow_pipeline
      │    modules.combine_async = 1           → combine_async_intensity
      ▼
[segmentation]          SimNIBS charm (layered media only)
      │                 modules.segmentation_only = 1 → stop here
      ▼
[placement]             modules.run_transducer_placement
      │                 placement.mode → trans_pos / focus_pos in T1 voxels
      ▼
[grid]                  modules.run_grid_setup              (grid cache)
      │                 reorient, crop, smooth the head; positions → grid voxels
      ▼
[medium]                modules.run_medium_setup            (medium cache)
      │                 tissue labels / pseudo-CT → acoustic & thermal properties
      │                 NIfTI export of masks and property maps
      ▼
[acoustic FOV crop]     grid.acoustic_fov_*  (optional sub-grid for the acoustic run)
      ▼
[source]                modules.run_source_setup
      │                 kWaveArray / mask source, sensor, CFL check
      ▼
[free-water baseline]   modules.run_water_baseline (auto | 1 | 0)
      │                 free-water ISPPA of the current drive, for target_isppa_wcm2 scaling
      ▼
[time reversal]         time_reversal.enabled  (refocusing phases, aberration report, pose search; skipped with BabelBrain)
      │                 time_reversal.only = 1 → stop here (no water baseline either)
      ▼
[acoustic]              modules.run_acoustic_sims           (acoustic cache)
      │                 k-Wave / jwave / BabelBrain, or a prior pressure map (path.acoustic_input);
      │                 field scaled to target_isppa_wcm2; dry-run backends stop here
      ▼
[acoustic analysis]     modules.run_acoustic_analysis
      │                 Isppa, MI, focal metrics → CSV; NIfTI (modules.run_nifti_creation);
      │                 targeting accuracy (modules.run_targeting_analysis)
      │                 BabelBrain input export (io.export_babelbrain)
      ▼
[thermal]               modules.run_heating_sims
      │                 k-Wave diffusion or BabelBrain BHTE over the timing protocol
      ▼
[thermal analysis]      modules.run_thermal_analysis
      │                 peak temperature, CEM43 → CSV; NIfTI
      ▼
[reports]               modules.generate_report / generate_group_report /
      │                 multi_isppa_report / uncertainty_report
      ▼
[post-hoc water]        modules.run_posthoc_water_sims  (one water run per transducer)
      ▼
[sequential]            options.sequential_configs  (follow-up run on the same medium)

items.title: Partial Runs
items.text:
To Set Segment first, simulate later modules.segmentation_only: 1: the run stops after SimNIBS segmentation. Reuse an earlier heuristic, PlanTUS, or TUS_entry placement Nothing: placement.reuse: auto reuses a recorded run whose settings match; always requires one. See Starting from earlier stage outputs. Simulate heating on top of an earlier acoustic run path.acoustic_input: <earlier run>/nii/sub-XXX_<medium>_T1w<affix>_pressure.nii.gz, with the other modules left on (grid and medium take seconds to a minute). The map is rescaled to transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 from its sidecar. Redo the acoustic analysis only modules.run_acoustic_sims: 0 and modules.run_heating_sims: 0. The acoustic stage then loads cache/…_results….mat, which the earlier run wrote only with io.save_acoustic_matrices: 1; without it, use path.acoustic_input as above. Skip the post-hoc free-water runs modules.run_posthoc_water_sims: 0

For example, heating on top of an earlier acoustic run (modules.run_heating_sims is off by default):

path:
  acoustic_input: /project/sim/sub-001/nii/sub-001_layered_T1w_pressure.nii.gz
modules:
  run_heating_sims: 1

Note

Downstream modules depend on outputs from upstream ones. Within-run caches in cache/ are reused subject to io.overwrite_files, and a reused grid or medium cache must match the current settings (Cache reuse checks). The grid, medium, and acoustic caches are only written when io.save_grid_cache, io.save_medium_cache, and io.save_acoustic_matrices (or io.save_matrices) are on; by default they are not. If a stage is switched off and its cache does not exist, the stage does not stop the run: the grid and medium stages continue with empty results, and the acoustic and thermal stages report that no results are available and skip their analysis. To start a run from the results of an earlier one, use its stage outputs instead (Starting from earlier stage outputs).

items.title: Multi-I<sub>SPPA</sub> Mode
items.text:
Heating and safety metrics depend on the intensity a study applies, and choosing one often means comparing several candidates. In the linear regime the pressure field scales with the square root of intensity, so this mode runs the acoustic simulation once and scales it to each target before a separate thermal simulation. The scaling holds only below the onset of nonlinear effects; at very high targets the scaled field may not be valid.

On this page:

  • Configuration: giving several target intensities.
  • Output Files: per-target files and the summary report.
  • Validity of Post-Hoc Scaling: when one acoustic result can serve every target.
  • Resuming a Partial Run: re-running a partial sweep, stages, and HPC options.
  • Combining with Uncertainty Mode: running a sweep for each uncertainty variant.
  • Combining with Async Transducers: per-transducer targets and sweeps.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To compare heating and safety metrics across candidate intensities without repeating the acoustic simulation.
  • Before you start: A study config whose single-intensity run works; targets within the linear regime (below roughly 50–100 W/cm² free-water).

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Give transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 more than one value:

transducer:
  target_isppa_wcm2: [10, 20, 30, 50]   # W/cm²; triggers multi-ISPPA mode
  elem_p_amp: ...
  # ... other transducer fields

PRESTUS then runs one acoustic simulation, caches it, and runs the thermal analysis at each requested intensity, each with its own output files and HTML report, plus a summary report. The free-water baseline that the scaling needs runs automatically (modules.run_water_baseline: auto, the default); see ISPPA targeting. In the Nexus, Sweep… next to the target ISPPA (Transducer tab) edits the list.

Note

The older form calibration.target_isppa_wcm2 is still accepted and is moved to transducer(1).target_isppa_wcm2 at load time with a deprecation warning.

items.title: Output Files
items.text:
Each thermal stage writes output under its own affix. For target_isppa_wcm2: [10, 30]:

sub-001_layered_desc-isppa010.csv
sub-001_layered_report_desc-isppa010.html
sub-001_layered_desc-isppa030.csv
sub-001_layered_report_desc-isppa030.html
sub-001_layered_desc-multiIsppa_report.html   ← summary

items.title: Validity of Post-Hoc Scaling
items.text:
The acoustic simulation (k-Wave skull propagation) is the expensive step. In the linear acoustic regime the pressure field scales as \(p \propto \sqrt{I}\), so one acoustic result serves every target. Linear scaling is valid when:

  • the acoustic simulation was run in the linear regime (target amplitudes below the onset of nonlinear harmonic generation, roughly < 50–100 W/cm² free-water for typical TUS setups);
  • the spatial pressure pattern is the same at all target intensities (guaranteed in the linear regime);
  • the thermal simulation uses the scaled pressure as input (the pipeline scales sensor_data.p_max_all before thermal_simulation is called).

A warning is printed if the scale factor relative to the baseline exceeds 4× or falls below 0.25×. Large scale factors mean the baseline and target are far apart in amplitude; at very high targets, nonlinear effects may invalidate the scaled field.

items.title: Resuming a Partial Run
items.text:
Each stage checks for its sentinel output file before submitting (HPC) or running (MATLAB). Re-running prestus_pipeline_start with the same config resumes a partially completed run; completed stages are skipped. With io.overwrite_files: always (default), only the acoustic stage resumes from its cache; thermal and summary stages always re-run. force re-runs every stage. See Overwrite behaviour.

Pipeline stages and HPC options 
[Stage 1]   Acoustic simulation + water baseline
            Runs once at the configured elem_p_amp.
            Saves sensor_data + acoustic_provenance.freefield_isppa_wcm2.
            No thermal simulation.

[Stage 2…N] Thermal analysis: one job per target_isppa_wcm2
            Loads cached acoustic results.
            Scales p_max_all by sqrt(target / baseline).
            Runs thermal simulation and analysis.
            Writes output files with affix _desc-isppaNNN (NNN = integer W/cm²).
            Generates per-target HTML report.

[Stage N+1] Summary report (optional, default: on)
            Aggregates results across all target intensities.

On HPC (SLURM/qsub), stages 2…N are submitted in parallel with an afterok dependency on stage 1. The summary depends on all thermal jobs.

Pass an options struct to prestus_pipeline_start to control per-stage resources:

options.acoustic_timelimit  = '08:00:00';   % wall time for stage 1
options.thermal_timelimit   = '02:00:00';   % wall time per thermal job
options.summary_timelimit   = '00:30:00';   % wall time for summary
options.acoustic_memorylimit = 80;           % GB for stage 1
options.thermal_memorylimit  = 40;           % GB per thermal job
options.generate_summary_report = false;     % skip summary stage

items.title: Combining with Uncertainty Mode
items.text:
Multi-ISPPA mode and uncertainty mode compose. When both simulation.uncertainty = true and transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 is a vector, uncertainty is the outer mode and each variant runs its own multi-ISPPA pipeline:

Stage 1    preproc / source setup                      (shared)
Variants   default, Temp-H, Temp-L, Trans-H, Trans-L, each:  (after stage 1)
             acoustic + free-water baseline
             thermal: one job per target               (_desc-temphigh_desc-isppa030 …;
                                                        none for Trans-H/L)
             multi-ISPPA summary
Stage 7    uncertainty report: one per target          (after every variant job)

Affixes compose: the variant affix (_desc-temphigh) prefixes the per-target affix, yielding _desc-temphigh_desc-isppa030. Each target gets an uncertainty report comparing the five variants at that intensity, e.g. sub-001_layered_desc-uncertainty_report_desc-isppa030.html (with the base io.output_affix before the target suffix when one is set). No report aggregates across intensities. See Combining with Multi-ISPPA or Async Modes.

items.title: Combining with Async Transducers
items.text:
When simulation.transducer_coupling = 'async' and multiple transducers are defined, each transducer carries its own target_isppa_wcm2. The async pipeline scales each transducer's pressure field independently before summing intensities incoherently. If any transducer has a vector target, one combine+thermal pair is run per sweep point. See Multi-Transducer Modelling.

See also: Transducer Calibration, Uncertainty Quantification, Pipeline Modules

items.title: Multi-Transducer Modelling
items.text:
When several transducers sonicate the same head, the exposure depends on how their fields combine, which a run per transducer does not capture. PRESTUS simulates them in one layered setup: transducers that fire together (coherent) add as complex pressures and interfere, while for transducers that fire in separate windows (async) acoustic safety metrics take the per-voxel maximum of the fields and heating uses the sum of their intensities.

On this page:

  • How the Fields Combine: an interactive comparison of the coupling modes.
  • Configuration: listing transducers and choosing how they fire.
  • Grid Setup: how the grid is aligned and cropped around several beams.
  • ISPPA Targets: per-transducer free-water targets and their baselines.
  • Complex Pressure Field: saving fields and superposing them afterwards at any relative phase.
  • Transducers at Different Frequencies: firing together or in turn at more than one frequency.
  • Partial Acoustic FOV: limited fields of view with several transducers.
  • Known Limitations: what refers to the first transducer only, and unsupported setups.
  • Subpages: async firing in separate windows.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Bilateral or dual-site stimulation, or any protocol with more than one transducer on the head.
  • Before you start: A layered (skull) simulation in a 3-D grid; one equipment entry and placement per transducer.

Experimental support

See this pull request for examples.

items.title: How the Fields Combine
items.text:
One focused transducer as the reference, then two on opposite sides firing together at one frequency, together at different frequencies, or in turn. Switch between the setups, and for one frequency change the phase of transducer 2; the readout gives the peak pressure and time-averaged intensity at the focus relative to one transducer.

The illustration is schematic: a lossless, homogeneous 2-D medium, slowed down, with pulses shortened in the async setup. The combination rules are the ones PRESTUS applies; see Transducers at different frequencies and Async Multi-Transducer Mode.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
List several transducers in a layered simulation:

transducer:
  - name: right
    serial: IS_PCD15473_01001
    combo: {ds_serial: IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch}
    # ... trans_pos, focus_pos, focal_distance_ep

  - name: left
    serial: IS_PCD15473_01001
    combo: {ds_serial: IGT_32_ch_comb_10_ch}
    # ...

simulation.transducer_coupling sets how the transducers fire:

Firing Setting Simultaneously, same frequency, known phase coherent (default): one k-Wave run with all sources active; the fields interfere. All transducers must share the fundamental frequency (a warning is issued otherwise). In separate, non-overlapping windows async: see Async Multi-Transducer Mode. In sequence, or with partial overlap Use Sequential Simulations: carry each heating run's temperature and CEM43 maps into the next via adopted_heatmap / adopted_cem43. This assumes the acoustic fields do not overlap in time.

In the Nexus, Multi-transducer coupling (Sonication tab, shown once the config has more than one transducer) selects the row above, and Target free-water ISPPA is set per transducer on the Transducer tab. The card can show an analytic prediction of both forms: the at-target intensity when the beams add independently and its range over their relative phase when coherent, and free-water maps of both in the beams' plane. The maps use Gaussian focal spots from each transducer's aperture and focal distance, with no skull and no side lobes; they guide the choice and do not replace the simulation.

items.title: Grid Alignment
items.text:
The default focal_axis mode rotates the grid so that the mean beam axis of all transducers aligns with z. Beams are averaged as axes, not directions, so opposed (bilateral) beams do not cancel: z bisects their two axes. Each beam off z is drawn obliquely on the grid, which costs accuracy at coarse resolution (for async runs, see grid.async_layout: per_transducer).

grid:
  mode: 'focal_axis'   # default; omit to get the same behaviour

With three or more transducers whose axes are too spread to average (mean-axis norm below grid.focal_axis_min_norm, default 0.5), focal_axis falls back to transducer(1)'s axis and warns.

To align the grid to transducer(1)'s focal axis instead, set transducer_axis. ras_plus keeps the RAS+ orientation without rotation (isotropic rescaling only), so every beam is oblique; it does not work with grid.axisymmetric. See Preprocessing: Orientation for the mode table. In the Nexus, Placement ▸ Transducers shows the grid z axis and each beam's tilt for the chosen mode.

items.title: Grid Cropping
items.text: The grid is cropped to the bounding box that encloses the CSF-expanded head tissue and the bowl geometry of every transducer. See Preprocessing: Cropping.

items.title: I<sub>SPPA</sub> Targets
items.text:
transducer(k).target_isppa_wcm2 is the free-water ISPPA of transducer k alone, for every coupling mode. Each transducer has its own drive (elem_p_amp), so the target rescales that transducer's drive, not the combined field.

simulation:
  transducer_coupling: coherent
transducer:
  - name: left
    serial: IS_PCD15473_01001
    target_isppa_wcm2: 20     # left transducer alone: 20 W/cm² in free water
  - name: right
    serial: IS_PCD15473_01003
    target_isppa_wcm2: 40     # right transducer alone: 40 W/cm²
Coupling How the targets are applied Sweeps (vector targets) coherent Before the simulation (coherent_drive_calibration): each transducer's elem_p_amp is multiplied by √(target / baseline), where baseline is the free-water ISPPA of that transducer alone at its configured drive. The combined field is simulated at these drives and not rescaled afterwards. Not available. Errors (prestus:isppa:coherentSweep); run one config per point, or use async. async After the per-transducer simulations: each field is scaled to its own target in combine_async_intensity, then combined. Yes: one acoustic run per transducer, one combine + thermal pair per sweep point (see Async Multi-Transducer Mode).

Coherent baseline. The rule is the same as for one transducer (ISPPA targeting). If the target matches the transducer's calibration ISPPA (tx_calibration.isppa_wcm2) within 1 %, the calibration is the baseline. Otherwise PRESTUS simulates that transducer alone in water (others at zero amplitude, same grid). With N transducers that is up to N extra free-water simulations. A transducer with target_isppa_wcm2: [] keeps its configured drive.

Provenance and cache checks

The result records targets, baselines, their source, and the drive scale in acoustic_provenance.coherent_drive. The combined free-water ISPPA (both firing) is reported but is not a target. A coherent cache without coherent_drive is refused when targets are set (prestus:isppa:coherentWithoutDriveCalibration): re-run its acoustic simulation. path.acoustic_input cannot be rescaled per transducer and errors when targets are set.

items.title: Complex Pressure Field
items.text:
Experimental

Superposition of saved complex fields (io.save_p_complex, superpose_complex_fields) is not yet validated in PRESTUS. Check a superposed field against a coherent simulation before you rely on it.

io:
  save_p_complex: true

This writes sub-XXX_<medium>_p_complex<affix>.mat with the complex amplitude at the fundamental on the simulation grid, at the simulated drive level, before ISPPA rescaling. Propagation in PRESTUS is linear, so fields simulated one at a time can be summed. superpose_complex_fields does this on one shared grid, back-projecting partial-FOV fields:

out = superpose_complex_fields({'.../sub-001_layered_p_complex_trans-01.mat', ...
                                '.../sub-001_layered_p_complex_trans-02.mat'});
out.p_coherent    % |p1 + p2|          coherent (simultaneous) firing
out.p_incoherent  % sqrt(|p1|^2+|p2|^2) async heat source
out.p_max         % max(|p1|, |p2|)    async peak pressure
out = superpose_complex_fields(files, Weights=[1, exp(1i*pi/2)]);   % relative phase of transducer 2

One async run (grid.async_layout: shared) with io.save_p_complex: true therefore also gives the coherent field for any relative amplitude and phase, without another simulation. Fields on different grids (per_transducer mode) and fields at different frequencies are not combined. With k-Wave (acoustic_backend: kwave or kwave_elastic, every code_type), p_complex is fitted to the pressure recorded over the last quarter period, which keeps the recording small (about 3 GB on a 0.75 mm head grid). k-Wave takes p_max_all and p_min_all over the same window, so in runs with save_p_complex they are ± the fitted amplitude, and ISPPA, MI and heating follow from it. In a steady field the two agree within 0.1 % where the pressure exceeds half its peak and within 0.5 % above a tenth of it; in low-pressure regions the fitted amplitude can be a few percent lower than a peak over several periods. Compare runs with and without save_p_complex with this in mind. Multi-frequency setups record the whole steady-state window instead (the tones are only separated over several periods) and stop above 8 GB (PRESTUS:pComplexTooLarge); use a partial FOV.

The other backends write the same file without these limitations:

Backend How p_complex is computed p_max_all Phase reference k-Wave (kwave, kwave_elastic) fit over the last quarter period ± fitted amplitude t = 0 jwave pseudo_spectral, finite_differences running fit over the steady-state window, no time series stored maximum over the window (unchanged) t = 0 jwave helmholtz the solver's complex field |P| (unchanged) t = 0 BabelBrain BabelBrain's own field (one frequency bin over its last cycles) BabelBrain's amplitude (unchanged) BabelBrain's recording window

superpose_complex_fields adds fields referred to t = 0 (k-Wave and jwave runs, in any mix), or BabelBrain fields with each other; it refuses to mix the two.

File contents
  • p_complex: complex amplitude at the fundamental on the simulation grid (the acoustic FOV sub-grid with a partial FOV), at the simulated drive level, before ISPPA rescaling. The phase refers to t = 0 of the simulation, when every source starts.
  • p_complex_info: phase_reference ('simulation_t0'), freq_hz, record_t0_s, dt_s, method ('quarter_period' or, multi-frequency, 'steady_state_window'), n_samples, p_max_from_fit (whether p_max_all/p_min_all are ± the fitted amplitude), drive_level ('simulated'), grid_dims, and fov_offset_ac / full_ac_dims with a partial FOV.

Files without p_complex_info are accepted only all together, with a warning (valid only for runs with the same time step and length).

items.title: Transducers at Different Frequencies
items.text:
When the transducers do not all share one frequency, each is simulated alone, at its own frequency and on a medium mapped for that frequency, and the results are combined. With transducer_coupling: async they fire in separate windows (Async Multi-Transducer Mode). With coherent (the default) they fire together; this uses the same pipeline as async mode, on a shared grid (grid.async_layout: shared), with complex fields saved automatically. Runs where every transducer has the same frequency are unchanged: one joint simulation.

Firing together, the pressure is the sum of the complex fields, p(t) = Re(Σ_f P_f·e^{iω_f t}), where P_f is the coherent sum of the fields of the transducers at frequency f. Transducers at one frequency interfere with a fixed relative phase, so their fields add as complex numbers. Between different frequencies the relative phase drifts at the beat frequency |f1 − f2|, so the cross terms average out of the time-averaged quantities but not out of the peaks:

Output Firing together, more than one frequency Pulse-average and time-average intensity (ISPPA, ISPTA) Σ_f |P_f|²/(2ρc) Heat source Σ_f α(f)·|P_f|²/(ρc), all on together; α(f) from each tissue's power law Peak pressure, MI maximum and minimum of p(t) over the pulse or the common period 1/gcd(f), whichever is shorter; MI uses the lowest frequency Temporal-peak intensity (Itp) from the peak pressure

When the common period needs more than 20000 time samples (frequencies close together or in a high-order ratio), the peak pressures are the upper bound ±Σ_f|P_f|; acoustic_provenance.combination_peak records which. Each pulse is assumed to start with the phases of t = 0. Nonlinear propagation (harmonics, sum and difference frequencies) is not modelled, as in every PRESTUS run.

Implementation

is_simultaneous_multifreq routes these runs to async_transducer_pipeline. combine_async_intensity (mode 'simultaneous') sums the scaled complex fields per frequency and writes p_intensity_equiv (intensity sum, read by acoustic_analysis for Ipa and Ita), p_max_async/p_min_async (phase-sampled peaks), and p_async_tx with one field |P_f| per frequency (p_async_freqs_hz). thermal_simulation heats each field with its frequency's absorption, all on together (thermal_schedule mode 'simultaneous'). Validation against one joint simulation with both tones: code/report/08_multitransducer/multitransducer_multifreq_* in PRESTUS_dev.

items.title: Partial Acoustic FOV
items.text:
A partial acoustic FOV (grid.acoustic_fov_diameter_mm, grid.acoustic_fov_length_mm) works with several transducers:

  • Coherent: the FOV box is the union of one box per transducer, each enclosing a cylinder of the FOV diameter along that transducer's beam axis. 'auto' is resolved per transducer (its outer element diameter; its focal depth + grid.z_beyond_focus_mm). For opposite transducers the union spans most of the head, so the saving is mostly lateral.
  • Async: each transducer's run gets its own FOV box. Fields are back-projected onto their full grid before combining, in both grid modes. Partial-FOV and full-grid caches can be mixed.
  • Complex superposition: each field is zero outside its own box, so the sum is complete only where boxes overlap (out.coverage counts the fields per voxel). Make the boxes cover the region around both foci.

The Nexus placement viewer draws every transducer's FOV box.

items.title: Known Limitations
items.text:
• Simulations without a skull or layered setup (e.g. medium: water) only model the first transducer.
  • kWaveArray mode supports multiple transducers only in non-axisymmetric mode (grid.axisymmetric = 1 is single-transducer). Matrix-type transducers in kWaveArray mode assume a +Z beam axis; see Transducer geometry.
  • Different carrier frequencies: see Transducers at Different Frequencies.
  • Exit-plane metrics (real_focal_distance_ep_mm, real_focal_distance_bowl_mm, max_Isppa_after_exit_plane) refer to the first transducer only.
  • Focal-plane heating plots show only the first transducer's focal plane. Always inspect the 3D maxT and CEM43 NIfTI volumes for a complete safety assessment.
  • Post-hoc water-only simulations are not implemented for multiple transducers.
  • The PRESTUS BabelBrain backend (acoustic_backend / thermal_backend: babelbrain) supports one transducer per run. Multi-transducer runs need kwave or jwave with thermal_backend: kwave. See BabelBrain: Geometry limits.
Comparison with BabelBrain

BabelBrain models one transducer per simulation. It treats several foci of one phased array as time-multiplexed, like PRESTUS async mode: the safety field is the per-voxel maximum of the pressure amplitudes (CalculateFieldProcess.py), and the thermal simulation switches between the spots' fields by duty-cycle share (BHTEMultiplePressureFields in ThermalModeling/CalculateTemperatureEffects.py). It does not add complex fields across foci.

items.title: Subpages
items.text:
• Async Multi-Transducer Mode: for transducers that fire in separate, non-overlapping windows; covers configuration, the physical model, grid modes, outputs, and constraints.

See also: Transducer Calibration, Multi-ISPPA Mode, Sequential Simulations, Pipeline Modules, Transducer Definition

items.title: Async Multi-Transducer Mode
items.text:
When transducers fire in separate, non-overlapping windows, their fields never interfere, so the coherent sum of Multi-Transducer Modelling would misstate the exposure. Async mode simulates each transducer on its own, scales each field to its own ISPPA target, and combines them: acoustic safety metrics take the per-voxel maximum and heating uses the sum of intensities.

On this page:

  • Async Configuration: switching on async mode, per-transducer targets, and ISPPA sweeps.
  • Physical Model: how the fields are combined for safety metrics and heating.
  • Firing Schedule: when each transducer fires, which sets its heating.
  • Example Protocols: sequences, transducers firing together, interleaved and partly overlapping pulses, and a mixed protocol with uncertainty, as the Nexus shows them.
  • Grid Geometry Mode: one shared grid or one grid per transducer.
  • Output Files: per-transducer, combined, and joint outputs, resumption, and HPC stages.
  • Constraints: required grid, head model, and regime.

At a glance

  • When you need it: Transducers fire with non-overlapping duty cycles or alternating pulses, or you want an ISPPA sweep across several transducers.
  • Before you start: A multi-transducer layered setup as in Configuration; a 3-D grid.

Experimental

For transducers that fire with non-overlapping duty cycles or alternating pulses, so their fields never superpose coherently. Configure it only with a clear view of the intended exposure and the linear-regime assumptions below.

items.title: Async Configuration
items.text:
Async mode runs when transducer_coupling is 'async' and there is more than one transducer. prestus_pipeline_start(parameters) dispatches to it; no other entry point is needed.

simulation:
  transducer_coupling: async

transducer:
  - name: CTX500-A
    target_isppa_wcm2: 5.0
    freq_hz: 500000
    trans_pos: [x1, y1, z1]
    focus_pos: [fx1, fy1, fz1]
    annular:
      elem_p_amp: 100000

  - name: CTX500-B
    target_isppa_wcm2: 3.0
    freq_hz: 500000
    trans_pos: [x2, y2, z2]
    focus_pos: [fx2, fy2, fz2]
    annular:
      elem_p_amp: 100000

The per-transducer acoustic runs always record a free-water baseline, which the combine step needs for scaling.

Multi-ISPPA sweep. A vector target_isppa_wcm2 triggers a sweep.

Multi-ISPPA sweep

Every transducer carries either a scalar (held fixed) or a vector of the same length:

transducer:
  - name: CTX500-A
    target_isppa_wcm2: [3.0, 5.0, 10.0]   # swept across 3 points

  - name: CTX500-B
    target_isppa_wcm2: 2.0                  # fixed across all 3 sweep points

This gives three combine + thermal pairs (A→3.0, 5.0, 10.0; B→2.0 each time).

items.title: Physical Model
items.text:
Acoustic safety metrics (ISPPA, MI, peak pressure) use the per-voxel maximum of the scaled fields. Thermal heat deposition follows the firing schedule: each transducer heats with its own scaled field while it is on, and the heat sources of the transducers on at the same time add up.

Equations

Acoustic safety metrics:

\[p_\mathrm{safety} = \max_i\bigl(p_{i,\mathrm{scaled}}\bigr)\]

where \(p_{i,\mathrm{scaled}} = p_i \cdot \sqrt{I_{i,\mathrm{target}} / I_{i,\mathrm{baseline}}}\). This is sensor_data.p_max_async in the combined cache.

Thermal heat deposition at time \(t\):

\[Q(t) = \sum_{i \in \mathrm{on}(t)} Q_i, \qquad Q_i \propto I_i = \frac{p_{i,\mathrm{scaled}}^2}{2\rho c}\]

where \(\mathrm{on}(t)\) is the set of transducers firing at \(t\). The scaled fields are sensor_data.p_async_tx in the combined cache. sensor_data.p_max_all holds the intensity sum of all transducers on at once, \(p = \sqrt{\sum_i p_{i,\mathrm{scaled}}^2}\).

items.title: Firing Schedule
items.text:
timing.async_schedule sets when each transducer fires. Heating follows each transducer's own on-time, so the schedule changes the temperature rise but not the acoustic safety metrics.

timing.async_schedule Firing Requires 'pulses' (default) Every transducer uses the timing block; transducer \(i\) starts \((i-1)\cdot\mathrm{PRI}/N\) later, so the pulses alternate within each PRI. \(N \cdot \mathrm{PD} \le \mathrm{PRI}\) 'trains' Every transducer uses the timing block; transducer \(i\) starts \((i-1)\cdot\mathrm{PTRI}/N\) later, so the pulse trains alternate. \(N \cdot \mathrm{PTD} \le \mathrm{PTRI}\) 'custom' Each transducer starts after its timing_offset_s and may override the timing block. No overlap at the same frequency, except within a firing group

Transducers that fire together. With 'custom', transducers with the same timing_offset_s and the same timing form a firing group. Each still runs its own acoustic simulation and is scaled to its own target ISPPA. Their complex fields are then summed, so they interfere, and the group heats in its own windows like a single transducer. One run can therefore mix transducers that fire together with transducers that fire one after another, and uncertainty mode wraps it like any async run. A group's peak intensity is not the sum of its members' targets: it depends on their relative phase where the beams overlap. On per-transducer grids (grid.async_layout: per_transducer), the complex fields are resampled onto transducer 1's grid with the carrier along each beam removed; the shared grid needs no resampling and is the more accurate choice.

Pulses that partly overlap. Transducers at one frequency whose pulses overlap without starting together interfere only while both are on. PRESTUS adds their interference heat in exactly those time segments and takes the peak pressure of the summed field for the safety metrics. timing.overlap_phase sets their relative carrier phase: clock (default) when the channels share one clock, so the simulated drive phases hold in every pulse; burst when each pulse starts its carrier at its own onset, so the phase also shifts with the delay. Ramped pulses (timing.pulse_ramp_dur) that partly overlap are not modelled and stop the run.

Custom schedule 
simulation:
  transducer_coupling: async
timing:
  async_schedule: custom

transducer:
  - name: CTX500-A
    timing_offset_s: 0
  - name: CTX500-B
    timing_offset_s: 0.1       # first pulse 100 ms after transducer A
    timing:
      pd: 0.04                 # replaces timing.pd for this transducer

transducer(i).timing_offset_s [s] defaults to 0. transducer(i).timing may set pd, pri, ptd, ptri, and ptrd, so transducers fired one after another can each sonicate for their own duration (sequences of stances). post_ptri_dur and the time steps stay global; the protocol ends post_ptri_dur after the last pulse train. Overrides are read only by 'custom'; with another schedule they are an error.

Transducers at the same frequency with the same timing_offset_s and timing form a firing group; pulses that overlap without starting together interfere while both are on (timing.overlap_phase). Within a group, the complex fields (io.save_p_complex, set automatically) are summed per frequency; fields at different frequencies heat with their own absorption, and the group's peak pressure is sampled over the pulse as for transducers at different frequencies. Overlap between groups at different frequencies gives a warning: the summed intensities are right for heating when the pulse is long against 1/|f1 − f2|, but the peak pressure then reaches the sum of the amplitudes at the beat maxima, more than p_max_all and MI report.

Transducers at different frequencies may fire in separate windows (here) or together (coherent coupling). Each transducer's acoustic run uses its own frequency for the time step, PPW, steady-state window and attenuation; a transducer at a frequency other than the first one's maps its own medium on the shared grid. The joint heat source gives each transducer the absorption at its frequency, α(fᵢ) = α(f₁)·(fᵢ/f₁)^y with each tissue's power-law exponent y. MI of the combined field uses the lowest frequency, which never underestimates MI = p/√f.

items.title: Example Protocols
items.text:
Each example below is one config and one async run, so uncertainty mode can wrap any of them. Build them on the Nexus's Sonication tab: the Sonication sequence card places the steps, and the timing diagram above it shows each transducer's firing lane. The figures are the Nexus's own drawings. Positions are given in MNI mm, so the same config fits any head.

Stances one after another. The left stance sonicates for 20 s, then the right stance for 20 s, then the left stance again for 40 s, with 30 s pauses between them. In the card, Add a later sonication (then Add step) adds a step, Place in Viewer sets its stance, and Pulse timing… sets the 40 s duration. Each stance gets one acoustic simulation, and step 3 reuses step 1's field because it returns to the same stance. One thermal simulation covers the whole 3.3 min, so each step starts in tissue that the earlier steps warmed.

Transducers firing together. Select step 2 and click Fire with previous step: T1 and T2 now sonicate at the same time with the same pulses, and T3 follows on its own. The two fields form a firing group. They are summed with their phases, so they interfere where the beams overlap, and each is scaled to its own target ISPPA first.

Interleaved pulses in one train. Two transducers share the same 1 s pulse trains, and T2's pulses come 100 ms after T1's, so the pulses alternate and never overlap. Set T2's Start delay (Transducers tab, advanced coupling fields) to 0.1 s; the Firing schedule lanes of the timing diagram show the alternating pulses. The fields never meet in time, so heating adds each field during its own pulses and the peak pressure is the larger of the two.

A mixed protocol with uncertainty. T1 sonicates alone, then T2 and T3 converge on a deep target together, then T1 returns to its first stance for 40 s, all with simulation.uncertainty: true. Each of the five variants runs the async pipeline with its own tissue properties: three acoustic simulations (T4 shares T1's field), one combine step, and, for the variants that model heating (default, Temp-H, Temp-L), one thermal simulation over the whole protocol. examples/example_mixed_uncertainty_ernie.m runs this protocol on SimNIBS' Ernie.

Partly overlapping pulses. As above, but T2's pulses come only 10 ms after T1's, so each 20 ms pulse overlaps the other by half. While both are on, the two fields interfere: PRESTUS adds their interference heat in those 10 ms of every pulse and takes the peak pressure of the summed field. Set timing.overlap_phase to burst if your driver starts each pulse's carrier at its onset rather than on a shared clock.

The examples as config

All of them use simulation.transducer_coupling: async, timing.async_schedule: custom, placement.mode: manual with placement.manual.coordinate_space: mni, and the tutorial's timing block (20 ms pulses every 200 ms for 20 s). Only the transducer entries differ; every entry lists the same keys.

# Stances one after another: offsets 0, 50, 100 s; step 3 returns to stance 1 for 40 s
transducer:
  - {serial: CTX_500_026, trans_pos: [-52, -8, 58], focus_pos: [-29, -6, 7], timing_offset_s: 0,   timing: {}}
  - {serial: CTX_500_026, trans_pos: [52, -8, 58],  focus_pos: [29, -6, 7],  timing_offset_s: 50,  timing: {}}
  - {serial: CTX_500_026, trans_pos: [-52, -8, 58], focus_pos: [-29, -6, 7], timing_offset_s: 100, timing: {ptrd: 40}}

# Firing together: give the transducers of a group the same offset and timing
#   T1 and T2 at timing_offset_s: 0, T3 at 50

# Interleaved pulses (timing block: ptd 1, ptri 2): T1 at 0, T2 at 0.1 s
# Partly overlapping pulses: T1 at 0, T2 at 0.01 s; timing.overlap_phase: clock (default) or burst

examples/example_mixed_uncertainty_ernie.yaml holds the mixed protocol in full.

items.title: Grid Geometry Mode
items.text:
grid.async_layout Grid Use when 'shared' (default) One grid for all transducers, aligned and cropped as in Grid alignment and Grid cropping. Default. 'per_transducer' Each transducer gets the grid a solo run would use. combine_async_intensity resamples every field onto transducer(1)'s grid via each run's planimg sidecar. Per-transducer focal distance, ISPPA, or focal volume must match a solo run, or the transducers are widely separated or steeply angled. Grid mode choice and accuracy 
simulation:
  transducer_coupling: async
grid:
  async_layout: per_transducer   # default: 'shared'

In shared mode an off-axis beam is voxelised at an angle, so its per-transducer results can differ from a solo run. The difference shrinks with resolution; at 2 mm (2.5 points per wavelength at 300 kHz) a beam 41° off axis lost 16% of its free-water ISPPA. In per_transducer mode the resampling (linear interpolation; parts outside transducer(1)'s grid are dropped) costs accuracy instead. per_transducer scales better with N: each grid stays sized to its own transducer, at the cost of N preproc jobs.

items.title: Output Files
items.text:
Two transducers, one target each:

cache/sub-001_layered_results_trans-01.mat
cache/sub-001_layered_results_trans-02.mat
cache/sub-001_layered_results_desc-asyncCombined.mat
sub-001_layered_desc-asyncJoint.csv
sub-001_layered_report_desc-asyncJoint.html

Reused acoustic fields. Transducers with the same stance and settings share one acoustic simulation: a step that returns to an earlier stance reads that stance's field. With positions given in the transducer entries (placement.mode: manual), the field is also kept in the output folder as cache/sub-001_layered_results_ac-<key>.mat, and later runs with the same settings read it instead of simulating it again: a follow-up run, a repeated study, or the same stance in another sequence. The key covers everything the field depends on (medium and its properties, so each uncertainty variant has its own field; grid; head model; segmentation; backend; with the shared grid, every transducer of the run; and the PRESTUS version), but not the target ISPPA, start, or pulse timing. On a cluster, a run planned while another run is still simulating the same field waits for that job. io.overwrite_files: force simulates every field again.

When a field is not kept

A field is shared within the run but not kept for later runs when the positions are resolved during the run (placement modes mni, heuristic, localite, plantus, tus_entry), or when the SimNIBS segmentation does not exist yet when the run is planned. A kept field records the PRESTUS version from the VERSION file; after changing the code between runs with the same version, use io.overwrite_files: force. The per-transducer outputs at the simulated drive level (CSV, NIfTI) are written by the run that simulated the field.

Sweep and affix naming

A 3-point sweep writes ..._desc-asyncCombinedS01.mat to S03 and sub-001_layered_desc-asyncJointS01.csv to S03.

With io.output_affix (e.g. run1), every affix starts with it: _desc-run1_trans-01, _desc-run1_desc-asyncJoint. The per-transducer runs also write their own CSV and acoustic NIfTIs at the simulated drive level; the Nexus Results tab shows them under the joint result.

Resumption. Re-running prestus_pipeline_start with the same config resumes from the last incomplete stage. With io.overwrite_files: always (default), preproc, acoustic, and combine resume from their caches; the joint and water-validation stages always re-run. force re-runs every stage. See Overwrite behaviour.

Pipeline stages, HPC options, and provenance Stage Count Affix Preproc 1 (shared) or N (per_transducer, parallel) _desc-asyncPreproc-t01, …, -tNN (per_transducer) Acoustic, at configured elem_p_amp, with water baseline N (parallel) _trans-01, …, _trans-NN Combine: scale each field to target, write p_max_all and p_max_async M sweep points _desc-asyncCombined (M=1) or _desc-asyncCombinedS01… Thermal (kWaveDiffusion) and report M _desc-asyncJoint (M=1) or _desc-asyncJointS01…

On HPC, each acoustic job depends on its preproc job, each combine job on all N acoustic jobs (afterok), and each thermal job on its combine job. prestus_pipeline_start returns the job IDs per stage, so later runs can wait on them:

[~, jobs] = prestus_pipeline_start(parameters);   % jobs.preproc, .acoustic, .combine, .thermal, .water
next.hpc.depend_job_ids = [jobs.preproc, jobs.acoustic];
prestus_pipeline_start(next);

HPC options:

options.acoustic_timelimit   = '06:00:00';   % per acoustic job
options.combine_timelimit    = '00:30:00';   % per combine job (CPU-only, lightweight)
options.thermal_timelimit    = '04:00:00';   % per thermal job
options.acoustic_memorylimit = 60;           % GB
options.thermal_memorylimit  = 40;           % GB
options.acoustic_partition   = 'gpu';
options.combine_partition    = 'cpu';        % combine stage needs no GPU

The combined cache records in acoustic_provenance:

Field Description combined_from Cell array of source cache file paths combination_mode 'async_dual_field': p_max_all holds the thermal intensity sum; p_max_async holds the per-voxel pressure maximum for acoustic safety. 'async_dual_field_grouped': with firing groups; 'async_dual_field_simultaneous': all transducers fire together combination_groups Firing group of each transducer (with firing groups); sensor_data.p_async_source_tx names the transducer whose windows each heat-source field in p_async_tx follows combination_targets Per-transducer target ISPPAs used for scaling [W/cm²] combination_baselines Per-transducer free-water baselines at the simulated drive level [W/cm²] combination_time Timestamp of the combination step

items.title: Constraints
items.text:
• 3-D grid required. Axisymmetric (2-D) simulations are not supported.
  • Shared head model. All transducers use the same segmentation (same subject_id, simulation.medium, and output directory).
  • Linear regime. The validity conditions of single-transducer ISPPA scaling apply (see Transducer Calibration).
  • Complex fields between grids. Transducers that fire together or whose pulses partly overlap are summed as complex fields. On per-transducer grids these are resampled with the carrier along each beam removed, which is exact for a plane wave along the beam and less so in the skull, where the wavelength differs; the shared grid needs no resampling.
  • Uncertainty mode. With simulation.uncertainty: true, each variant runs its own async pipeline (preproc included), and one uncertainty report is written per sweep point. See Combining with Multi-ISPPA or Async Modes.

items.title: PRESTUS Nexus (GUI)
items.text:
The Nexus is a desktop app to set up, check, and run a PRESTUS study, and to look at its placements and results. You fill in forms, the Nexus checks them as you type and writes the study config, and MATLAB runs the simulation. The config is an ordinary PRESTUS YAML that holds only the values that differ from the defaults, so it also runs without the Nexus.

On this page:

  • Installation: the prestus-nexus conda environment and other ways to install.
  • Starting the Nexus: opening the Nexus from MATLAB or a terminal, with a study config and project defaults.
  • A First Simulation: from a T1 image to results in six steps.
  • Beyond the First Simulation: where to go for studies, protocols, calibration, Localite, and remote runs.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To build a study config without editing YAML, check it before it runs, and run it locally or on a cluster.
  • Before you start: The prestus-nexus conda environment (Installation) and MATLAB, which runs the simulations.

Subpages:

  • Tabs and Pages: every tab and page with the config keys it writes, for anyone changing settings beyond the QuickStart tab, running a study of multiple subjects, or following runs and results.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
System Run in the PRESTUS folder macOS, Linux bash nexus/install.sh Windows nexus\install.bat (or double-click it)

The installer creates the conda environment prestus-nexus from nexus/environment.yml. If conda is missing, it offers to install Miniforge into your home folder first. Run it again after a PRESTUS update: it then updates the environment. With conda already set up, conda env create -f environment.yml in PRESTUS/nexus does the same. Installing without conda, the standalone app, and the cache folder are described under Installation options.

items.title: Updating PRESTUS
items.text:
Help ▸ Check for updates… compares your PRESTUS folder with the latest release and, on Update to …, moves it there. Without a window (e.g. on a cluster), use the command line:

prestus-nexus --update --check     # report the installed and the latest release
prestus-nexus --update             # move to the latest release (--to v0.7.1: to that release)
python3 nexus/prestus_nexus/update.py --check   # the same without the Nexus environment

The update needs a PRESTUS folder made with git clone. It changes nothing when PRESTUS files were edited in the folder, or when the folder holds a version with changes of its own (a development version); the message then says what to do. The bundled toolboxes that are installed (such as k-Wave) follow the release. Afterwards, restart the Nexus and MATLAB; when the result says so, run the installer again first. Let running and queued simulations finish before updating: they would switch to the new version part-way through.

What an update leaves alone
  • Untracked files (your study configs, results) and submodules you did not install.
  • A study's own copy of config_default.yaml: see Project defaults.
  • A PRESTUS folder downloaded as an archive: the check names the latest release, which you download yourself.

The check reads the list of release tags from the PRESTUS repository on GitHub. Nothing is contacted unless you ask for a check or an update.

How the update moves the checkout

A release is a git tag vX.Y.Z (nexus/prestus_nexus/update.py). Changed tracked files stop the update. On a branch the update fast-forwards to the tag (git merge --ff-only); a checkout that sits on a tag is switched to the new one (git checkout --detach), and only there --to can also go back to an earlier release. --check exits with 10 when a newer release exists, 0 when not, and 1 on an error.

items.title: Installation Options
items.text:
pip, Qt, and h5py

Without conda, pip install -e . in PRESTUS/nexus installs the same packages into any Python ≥ 3.10 environment; the list lives in nexus/pyproject.toml.

Install Qt from pip only (as environment.yml does). conda's pyqt together with pip's PyQt6-WebEngine fails to load (Library not loaded: …QtPrintSupport). In an older environment built with conda's pyqt, run conda remove pyqt and then pip install -e ..

Reading -v7.3 HEAT files on the Heating sub-tab also needs h5py (not installed by default; PRESTUS saves -v7 unless MATLAB's preference says otherwise).

Cache folder

The Nexus runs from a local copy of its own code in the user's cache folder (~/Library/Caches/prestus_nexus on macOS, ~/.cache/prestus_nexus on Linux); on the Donders project drive this halves the start-up time. The parsed config/equipment files are cached in the same folder while they are unchanged. Set PRESTUS_NEXUS_CACHE to use another cache folder.

Local copy of the code

On start the Nexus copies the files of nexus/prestus_nexus that changed since the last start into the cache folder and runs from there, so Python does not read its modules from a network drive. The checkout stays the source: an edit there is copied on the next start. Set PRESTUS_NEXUS_LOCAL_COPY=0 to run from the checkout directly.

nexus/packaging/prestus_nexus.spec builds a standalone app with PyInstaller (pip install -e . pyinstaller, then pyinstaller packaging/prestus_nexus.spec in nexus/). The app does not contain PRESTUS: on first start it asks for the PRESTUS folder (or use --prestus-root / PRESTUS_ROOT) and remembers it.

items.title: Starting the Nexus
items.text:
From MATLAB:

prestus_nexus                                  % untitled study (File > New / Open)
prestus_nexus('config_study.yaml')             % open a study config
prestus_nexus(Python='/path/to/env/bin/python')

From a terminal:

conda activate prestus-nexus
prestus-nexus [config_study.yaml]

From MATLAB, prestus_nexus finds the environment's Python by itself: $PRESTUS_NEXUS_PYTHON if set, the Python of the last start, the conda environment prestus-nexus, then python3. It uses the first that can start the Nexus and remembers it. If none can, the error lists what it tried; pass Python= to choose one.

items.title: Opening a Study Config
items.text:
The Nexus opens a given config, or an untitled one. File ▸ New study… creates a config and can copy config_default.yaml into its folder, which pins the defaults as prestus_config_init does. Open… and Open recent switch to another config. The subject, paths, T1/T2 patterns, and SimNIBS folder are set on the Setup tab. The Issues panel checks them as you type: the T1 must resolve, and the m2m_sub-XXX folder must exist or SimNIBS must be set.

Compatibility with MATLAB's YAML loader

PRESTUS reads configs with yaml.loadFile (SnakeYAML, YAML 1.1). The Nexus:

  • quotes all strings (unquoted yes/no/04:00:00 would change type);
  • reads floats such as 2.17e-3 the way SnakeYAML does;
  • writes every element of a transducer list with the same top-level keys, which yaml.loadFile requires.

A round-trip test writes configs with the Nexus, loads them with load_parameters, and compares every value. It covers both a serial-based and a fully inline transducer.

Config schema and overlay

The schema is derived from config_default.yaml at startup. nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml adds only widget kinds, allowed values, units, visibility rules, keys the code reads that the default omits, deprecated keys, readable field labels where a key does not read as words (display; other labels are derived in labels.py), readable drop-down labels for choice values (choice_labels; hovering an item shows the value written to the YAML), and the schematic icons shown with drop-down choices. Quote a value that contains a comma ({label: "a, b"}): unquoted, YAML splits it, and the drift test reports the stray key. nexus/tests/test_schema.py fails when the overlay no longer matches the default config or the code. See nexus/README.md for running the tests.

items.title: Project Defaults
items.text: When the study folder holds a copy of config_default.yaml (from File ▸ New study… or prestus_config_init), the Nexus merges it onto the toolbox default exactly as load_parameters does: the copy's values win, keys added to PRESTUS since the copy was made keep their toolbox defaults. The Review YAML page names both files. Tools ▸ Update project defaults… replaces the copy with the toolbox default (keeping a dated backup), optionally after writing the values the copy pinned differently into the study config so the simulation settings stay the same; prestus_config_upgrade(folder) does the same from MATLAB.

items.title: A First Simulation
items.text: The steps below take one participant from a T1 image to results. The screenshots show the demo subject sub-009.

items.title: 1. Fill In the QuickStart Tab
items.text:
The Nexus opens on QuickStart, which asks for four things and keeps every other setting at its PRESTUS default:

  1. Head image: the participant's T1-weighted NIfTI. The Nexus finds the T2, the SimNIBS segmentation, and the subject number from it.
  2. Transducer: the device and driving system from the equipment library, the focal depth, and the free-water intensity. The calibration PRESTUS will use is shown below.
  3. Target: where to focus, in MNI coordinates. Give the target alone and PRESTUS finds a transducer position, or give both.
  4. Check and run: where the simulation runs, and any errors still to fix.

Each step shows Done once it is complete. Continue to Run saves the study and opens the Run tab. The other tabs hold every setting, with the same values the QuickStart tab wrote.

items.title: 2. Check the Transducer
items.text: The Transducer tab shows what the library knows about the device. The device panel gives its focal range and the calibration entry PRESTUS will use; green values mean your focal depth lies inside that range. The cross-section draws the transducer and the focal depth you set (✕). The Calibration sub-tab (Transducer ▸ Calibration) plots how well the calibration fits at each depth, with your study's depth as a vertical line.

items.title: 3. Check the Placement
items.text:
Placement ▸ Viewer draws the transducer, the beam, and the simulated field of view on the participant's T1 and segmentation. The readout on the right reports the placement: how deep the target lies, how far the transducer sits from the scalp, and how much skull the beam crosses. Red values need attention. In the example, the target lies 2.2 mm short of the focal depth setting, which Set focal depth to target corrects.

To change a manual placement, choose under Click sets whether a click moves the focus or the transducer, then click a slice. Snap to scalp moves the transducer onto the scalp along the beam. Placements from Localite, the heuristic search, or PlanTUS are shown read-only.

items.title: 4. Clear the Issues
items.text: The error and warning counts in the header open the Issues panel. It lists what MATLAB would otherwise report only when the run starts: misspelt keys, missing files, intensities that cannot be reached, and the placement viewer's red flags. Clicking an issue opens the field it refers to. Fix the errors; read the warnings and notes.

items.title: 5. Run the Simulation
items.text:
The Run tab lists the pipeline stages, which you can switch off for partial runs, and where to run. Run locally runs MATLAB on this computer and streams its log. Submit to cluster submits from a cluster login node; Submit over SSH submits from a laptop with the project drive mounted. Submitted jobs appear under Jobs. Review YAML shows the exact config that will be written.

The first run on a participant also creates the segmentation, so it takes longest.

items.title: 6. Look at the Results
items.text:
The Results tab reads what the runs wrote to the subject's output folder. Run picks a run when the folder holds several. Acoustic and Thermal show the maps on the T1, centred on their peak; clicking a slice reads the value there. Report opens the HTML report, Data table the metrics, and Compare runs puts the key metrics of all runs side by side, with the air-cavity check columns when a run has them.

Heating plots the temperature of each tissue over the sonication and the steady-state after it.

items.title: Beyond the First Simulation
items.text:
To Go to Details Run multiple subjects or conditions Study tab Study tab, Group analysis Set the sonication protocol, or exchange it with the TUS calculator Sonication tab Timing diagram and TUS calculator Calibrate a transducer to your hydrophone profiles Transducer ▸ Calibration Calibration page Ingest Localite neuronavigation recordings Placement ▸ Localite Localite page Submit from a laptop over SSH Run tab Run tab Rerun with another intensity, timing, or placement, or chain a sequential run Results ▸ Follow-up… Follow-up runs Undo a change, find a setting, find a tab's docs, or export a figure Edit and Help menus, a figure's download button Menus and shortcuts See settings hidden as advanced Advanced on any tab, or the advanced icon on a card Advanced options Pin the defaults for a project File ▸ New study… Project defaults

Tabs and Pages describes every tab, page, and control, with the config keys each one writes, including the Calibration and Localite pages that compute in MATLAB.

items.title: Nexus Tabs and Pages
items.text:
Most Nexus controls explain themselves: each field shows its name, its help from config_default.yaml (hover or ?), its config key, and its default. This page covers what the window does not show: which config keys a control writes, what a button does beyond the obvious, where displayed data comes from, and what a feature needs.

On this page:

  • Tab Overview: what each tab holds, and how fields appear and hide.
  • Menus and Shortcuts: undo, search, offline docs, and errors.
  • Segmentation Step: running SimNIBS charm on its own.
  • QuickStart Tab: the four steps and the config keys they write.
  • Advanced Options: hidden settings and locked tables.
  • Transducer Tab: devices, calibration, and several transducers.
  • Calibration Page: calibrating the study's transducers to hydrophone profiles.
  • Placement Viewer: what the viewer writes and what its checks measure.
  • Localite Page: ingesting Localite neuronavigation recordings.
  • Issues Panel: what is checked before a run.
  • Run Tab: what each run button writes and runs, and submitting over SSH.
  • Results Tab: where the shown values come from.
  • Study Tab: the run table and the study commands.
  • Timing Diagram and TUS Calculator: editing the protocol and exchanging it with the TUS calculator.
  • MATLAB Session: when the session behind the Calibration and Localite pages starts and ends.
  • Standalone MATLAB GUIs: opening neuronav_gui and calibration_gui from the Nexus.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To find out what a control writes or runs, where a value comes from, or why a field or mode is not offered.
  • Before you start: The Nexus installed and started (PRESTUS Nexus (GUI)); A First Simulation walks through the main tabs once.

items.title: Tab Overview
items.text:
Tab Holds QuickStart A first simulation in four steps (below). Setup Subject, paths, environment, input and output. Transducer Device and driving system, geometry, drive and steering; Calibration and Equipment sub-tabs. Placement Placement method and positions; Viewer, Beam axis, 3D, and the method pages (Localite, PlanTUS, TUS entry). Medium Medium type; head model, tissue properties, uncertainty, and skull CT sub-tabs. Sonication Pulse timing, multi-transducer coupling, thermal model. Solver Acoustic and thermal solvers, their compute device, grid, time reversal. Study The run table for several subjects or conditions. Run Pipeline stages, where to run, the run plan, the YAML, launch, and jobs. Results The runs in the results folder, and follow-up runs.

Fields appear only when they apply to the current choices, e.g. the Localite settings only with placement.mode: localite. In the Placement method row, a mode is unavailable (greyed; the tooltip names the missing input) when PRESTUS cannot produce an input it needs: no T1, no SimNIBS segmentation and no startup.simnibs_bin_path to run charm (PlanTUS also needs the mesh sub-XXX.msh), or no recorded Localite poses. Needs setup means charm will run first or the mode's tool paths are still empty. The mode in use always stays selectable.

Figures export as SVG, PDF, or PNG (3D views as PNG only), in the light theme unless Keep current theme is ticked.

items.title: Menus and Shortcuts
items.text:
• Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) cover edits on every tab in one history, including viewer clicks and the Study tab's table. A button that writes several values is one step. Reload from disk and opening another study clear the history; saving does not.
  • Find setting… (Ctrl+F) searches names, config keys, choices, and help text, and opens the setting on its tab. Settings that do not apply to the current choices are listed greyed.
  • Help ▸ Use local documentation files opens the Markdown files in doc/ instead of the published pages, e.g. offline. F1 opens the page of the shown tab.
  • Tools ▸ Usage statistics… records which usage statistics levels you share, in ~/.prestus/telemetry.json. This is needed because the Nexus runs MATLAB with matlab -batch, where PRESTUS never asks. The Nexus itself sends nothing. What you share shows at the right of the status bar; click it to change it. The Nexus asks at launch until you decide, unless PRESTUS_TELEMETRY is set. If you allowed an earlier version of the notice, it asks once more.
  • Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 switch tabs; Ctrl+Shift+V validates in MATLAB; Ctrl+R runs locally.
When something goes wrong
  • An unexpected error shows a dialog instead of closing the Nexus; the traceback is written to nexus_errors.log in the cache folder.
  • Saving writes to a temporary file first, so a full or read-only share leaves the old config intact.
  • The MATLAB session must start within 180 s, and a request may take up to 600 s; after a time-out the session restarts on the next request.

items.title: Segmentation Step
items.text:
charm takes an hour or more, and its output (m2m_sub-XXX) feeds the layered head model, heuristic, MNI, PlanTUS, and TUS_entry placement, and the viewer's scalp checks. It can therefore run on its own first.

  • Run segmentation (Medium tab, Segmentation card) runs only charm for this subject (modules.segmentation_only: 1, simulation.medium: layered): as a cluster job where the Run tab submits there, else in MATLAB on this computer.
  • Segment again… sets io.overwrite_simnibs: 1 for that run only: charm deletes the m2m folder and segments again. Placements, head models, and MNI conversions made from the old segmentation then no longer match it.
  • Incomplete means tissue labels or MNI warps are missing: charm did not finish or failed.

items.title: QuickStart Tab
items.text:
QuickStart writes the same config keys as the other tabs, and every setting it does not show keeps its PRESTUS default.

  1. Head image: the T1 sets path.anat, path.t1_pattern (as sub-%1$03d_… when the name holds sub-<n>), and subject_id. A T2 next to it (T1w→T2w) and an m2m_sub-XXX folder in, under, or next to the anatomy folder (path.seg) are found automatically. Without a segmentation, it looks for SimNIBS 4 (charm on the PATH, then conda environments and the installers' default folders) to set startup.simnibs_bin_path. The results folder defaults to prestus_sim next to the study config (or next to the anatomy folder while the config is unsaved), never inside the anatomy folder.
  2. Transducer: device, driving system, focal depth setting, and free-water ISPPA. A device with one calibrated driving system selects it. Without a calibration entry of its own, a line names the generic entry PRESTUS falls back to, or what to do instead.
  3. Target: the coordinate space decides the placement mode. An MNI target alone gives placement.mode: heuristic (which needs a target name); an MNI target with a scalp point gives mni (the transducer is moved onto the scalp, exit plane placement.skin_gap_mm outside it). A target and bowl apex in the participant's T1 give manual with placement.manual.coordinate_space: ras or voxel, used as given. For a participant-space target without a transducer position, use PlanTUS on the Placement tab.
  4. Check and run: sets platform and lists the errors left. Continue to Run saves the study.

items.title: Advanced Options
items.text:
Each tab hides the settings most studies leave at their defaults; Advanced shows them, on the whole tab or per card. An advanced setting that holds a value is always shown. Settings the chosen setup does not read stay hidden too, e.g. anatomy, SimNIBS, and targeting settings with a water medium.

Locked tables: tissue layers, tissue properties, uncertainty values
  • Tissue layers and the Tissue properties table (medium_properties) are read-only until 🔒 Unlock (with advanced options shown); the unlock lasts for the session. Emptying a cell resets it. Values from a loaded config apply whether locked or not.
  • With a layered medium and a segmentation, a tissue none of whose labels occur in final_tissues.nii.gz is greyed as not modelled, as PRESTUS drops its layer. For a charm segmentation this is Skull (single layer) (label 4); with pct.enabled, the cortical and trabecular columns, which merge into the single skull layer. Volumes are for the whole head, not the simulation grid.
  • A tissue sets either the absorption fraction or the absorption coefficient; the table shows the other in brackets as implied. Typing into an implied cell switches the tissue to that field.
  • On the Uncertainty sub-tab, an edited variant value sets simulation.uncertainty_overrides and raises a warning.
Skull CT sub-tab

For a pseudo-CT, the UTE→pseudo-HU line is read from pct_create_pseudoCT.sh or the subject's fit. The HU→property curves are evaluated by MATLAB (pct_mapping_curves). The in-skull property distributions come from the default run when it exists; otherwise Predict skull properties predicts them without simulating. With the BabelBrain backend, the sub-tab also holds BabelBrain's own HU mapping (babelbrain.ct_mapping, babelbrain.air_*). See Pseudo-CT runs.

Where locked cards are defined

Locked cards are set by locked: true under sections: in nexus/prestus_nexus/overlay.yaml. The tuning: list there (which keys affect speed, accuracy, memory, or disk) is kept for a later Tune for control and is not shown.

items.title: Transducer Tab
items.text:
Devices and driving systems come from config/equipment. Fields filled from the library are marked from library; Geometry starts collapsed when the library supplies it.

  • With several transducers, transducer 2 and later inherit transducer 1's values unless set.
  • Sweep… next to the target ISPPA sets a list of targets, which runs the multi-ISPPA pipeline.
  • The Calibration sub-tab compares, fits, and saves library entries (Calibration page). With Advanced, the Equipment sub-tab adds transducers and driving systems to your library (New transducer or driving system in the Nexus).

items.title: Calibration Page
items.text:
Transducer ▸ Calibration is the transducer-calibration GUI. It computes in the Nexus's MATLAB session and needs a hydrophone profile CSV. It does what calibration_gui does (Transducer library), computed by the same functions (calibration_desired_profiles, calibration_evaluate, calibration_fit, calibration_save_entry). It works on the study's transducers, or, with Any library transducer, on any transducer and driving system of the equipment library: entries are then saved to a folder of your own library (Folder…) without changing the config, and the k-Wave drive check asks for a simulation config (grid, platform, HPC; or PRESTUS defaults). View geometry shows the selected transducer on the Equipment sub-tab.

The plots fill the top of the page and the controls sit below them, grouped in three steps: 1 Data (profile CSV, measured and desired depths), 2 Fit (where to calibrate, reference ISPPA, Fit, Evaluate), and 3 Save (save, Export, Report, k-Wave drive check). The fitter's settings (ring profile, free parameters, forward model, near-field skip, loss, Huber δ, starts) are under Fit options, collapsed by default, because the defaults suit most fits.

The plots

Until MATLAB has answered, the plot area shows the current library entry from its YAML alone:

  • Quality: the global model's R² per calibrated depth, with the geometric and per-depth-fit medians as reference lines.
  • Drive: the drive amplitude per depth.
  • Phases: each ring's phase correction per depth, unwrapped; steps over 30° between neighbouring depths are marked.

The calibrated range is shaded and this study's depths are drawn as lines, coloured by whether the entry covers them. The same plot sits under the transducer drawing on the Settings sub-tab. After Predict, Evaluate, or Fit, the Profiles view shows the profiles with a bar per depth coloured by R² (green ≥ 0.9, amber ≥ 0.8, red below); clicking a bar shows that depth.

The controls
  • Transducer lists the config's transducers that use a device from config/equipment; the driving system and transducer.library_path are taken from the config. The current library entry is the one PRESTUS would use (the user folder first, then config/calibration).
  • Profile CSV defaults to the combination's char_data_path under local/profiles. Loading it shows the geometric model and the library entry against the measured profiles (R² per depth).
