  • Desired depths and Predict model any depths through the runtime library path, with the measured, interpolated, or (within extrapolate ≤) extrapolated profile at each depth. The desired depths are prefilled with the depths this study uses with the device: the focal depth settings (focal_distance_ep or _bowl of every matching transducer, and the manifest's transducer[(i)].focal_distance_ep columns) and each matching transducer's target depth in the placement viewer (exit plane → focus_pos, 0.1 mm). They follow the config and placement each time the page is shown, until you type your own; Study depths fills them in again. Without either, the depths of the entry's meta.fit, then the device's defaults, are used. The plot then shows focus against target per depth, and the table the phases and drive each depth resolves to.
  • Ring profile (keep the entry's / fit / uniform rings) selects the within-ring velocity profile (Within-ring velocity profile); fit fits it on the measured profiles before the per-depth fits. Options… sets the profile fit and a plane-scan file (off-axis data) fitted with the axial profiles.
  • Fit calibrates per-depth refinements at the ticked measured depths or at the desired depths. Reference ISPPA defaults to transducer.target_isppa_wcm2. Advanced… holds the fitter's further options (as in calibration_gui; see Calibration), the desired-profile tolerance and the k-Wave drive check's grid and correction, and loads a preset.
  • Save entry writes <serial>[_<ds>].yaml to transducer.library_path. If that is not set, it asks for a folder and sets it in the config. The entry records how it was fitted (meta.fit), and opening it later restores those settings. The device panel on the Settings sub-tab then shows the new entry as the one PRESTUS will use.
  • k-Wave drive check… (per-depth fits) writes the unsaved fit and calibration/kwave_drive_<combo>.m next to the config. The script runs kwave_calibrate_drive with the study config's grid and platform, then saves the drive-corrected entry; it takes minutes per depth. Submit as a job sends it to the cluster as a CPU job (kwave_drive_submit: 8 GB, wall time = depths × hpc.timelimit + 1 h), which submits one simulation job per depth and waits for them on a compute node; over SSH (Run tab) the Nexus writes a copy with the cluster's paths (kwave_drive_<combo>_cluster.m). The job appears in the Run tab's job list. Run on the Run tab runs it in the Nexus's MATLAB instead, which on a cluster login node keeps MATLAB waiting there; or run the script yourself.
  • Export profiles… and Export settings… write the same CSVs as calibration_gui.
  • Report opens the HTML report of the saved library entry (generate_calibration_report: provenance, fit quality, the settings a study gets at the fitted depths, and the amplitude lookup), written to a temporary folder.

items.title: Placement Viewer
items.text:
The viewer sets positions for manual placement and shows the result of the other modes read-only. Positions are written in the space of placement.manual.coordinate_space (voxel or ras; Manual placement). A clicked transducer position is the bowl apex.

  • MNI coordinates are converted with SimNIBS (mni2subject_coords) when you click, which needs the subject's m2m_sub-XXX folder; startup.simnibs_bin_path alone is not enough. Set focus uses the nonlinear warp and Set transducer the affine, as in MNI placement. If the warp is missing, Set focus falls back to the affine and says so. A study with coordinate_space: mni is not shown in the viewer, because PRESTUS converts its values only at run time.
  • Two depths: the target depth (exit plane → focus_pos) comes from the placement; the focal depth setting (transducer.focal_distance_ep) is set on the equipment. For annular arrays the setting selects the calibrated phases, so the simulated focus lands at the setting even when the target is deeper or shallower. A difference above 2 mm is flagged.
  • Beam checks (with a segmentation): skull on the beam (mean ± SD over 37 rays from the aperture to the focus), mean skull incidence (flagged above 20°), the exit-plane-to-scalp gap (negative means the transducer cuts into the head; a large SD means uneven contact), and the share of rays through an eye. These are the measures of placement.beam_qc. With manual placement, the red flags also appear in the Issues panel.
  • Snap to scalp keeps the beam axis and puts the exit plane a chosen gap outside the scalp.
  • Trajectories import from Brainsight, 3D Slicer, and k-Plan; see Importing a Trajectory.
  • Other modes show the positions the last run's placement stage resolved (sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json). To get them without simulating, run once with only modules.run_transducer_placement enabled.
Beam axis, 3D, and several transducers
  • Beam axis shows the last layered run's medium_masks, or before a run the SimNIBS labels mapped through layers without PRESTUS's smoothing. The free-water profile is read from the run's axial profile (img/sub-XXX_<medium>_axial_profile<affix>.csv); before a run, it is predicted in MATLAB from the device's library model at the focal depth setting (annular library devices only). Absolute needs a run, since the prediction has no absolute scale.
  • 3D draws each transducer in a cylindrical housing sized from housing: in its equipment entry; without one, the aperture's diameter, reaching 15 mm behind the bowl apex. The face is removed by default so the view does not identify the participant. It needs graphics support (Qt Quick 3D).
  • Several transducers: Grid orientation sets grid.mode (Grid Alignment). It warns when focal_axis falls back to transducer 1's axis (grid.focal_axis_min_norm), and when a beam tilts 20° or more on a grid with fewer than 6 points per wavelength in water. Each FOV box is resolved from its own transducer: coherent coupling simulates their union, async coupling one box each (Partial Acoustic FOV).
PlanTUS, heuristic, and TUS entry pages
  • PlanTUS shows the skin maps of the last run (plantus_metrics.mat in the placement run folder). Place here sets placement.plantus.vertex and places the transducer on the same maps without recomputing them. Choose in Workbench… needs a display and always runs on this computer (Running PlanTUS).
  • Heuristic shows the candidates of the last run (tpars_sub-XXX_<target>.csv). Place here sets placement.heuristic.candidate; Use the heuristic's choice clears it. Distances are in voxels, as the heuristic computes them.
  • TUS entry shows the result from tus_entry_report.csv (TUS_entry placement).
  • Computing maps, candidates, or entries runs as a placement-only job: on the cluster where the Run tab submits there, else in MATLAB on this computer.

items.title: Localite Page
items.text:
Placement ▸ Localite ingests the Localite recordings under path.localite_raw in the Nexus's MATLAB session, with the study config's settings (path.localite_raw/_post, placement.localite.*, io.overwrite_files, neuronav.*). These are edited on the Settings sub-tab (Edit settings), not on the page. The config is saved before each step, because MATLAB reads it with load_parameters as a run does. The steps are those of neuronav_gui (Neuronavigation Read-In).

Detect series and write outputs
  1. Detect series (neuronav_detect_series, neuronav_name_series) lists the series of the chosen subject and session with their QC (pulses, position and rotation deviation, tracking flags). Each series is named after the coil table, the planned target nearest its beam axis, or series_<k>. Tabs show the pulse positions in 3-D (with the beam direction and the planned targets), the deviation per pulse, the marker files found, and the log.
  2. Write outputs (neuronav_check_target_map, neuronav_ingest_markers) writes the ticked series under their (editable) names and colours to path.localite_post/sub-XXX/ses-XX/. When the inputs or the settings change after detection, the page asks you to detect again.
Using the written outputs, batch ingestion, and MNI view
  • Use in this study sets placement.localite.session and .target to the written session and target(s) (one per transducer).
  • Import into study… builds manifest rows from all ingested sessions (Study tab).
  • Ingest all sessions… scans every session (neuronav_scan_sessions) and lists the planned-target labels found, whose target names you can edit (Group labels by stem, Use labels as found). Save label map and run batch writes the map to neuronav.target_labels and the write mode to neuronav.batch_write, then runs ingest_<study>.m (neuronav_ingest_batch on the ticked sessions) on the Run tab.
  • MNI view… maps neuronav_ingest_summary.csv to MNI space with each subject's SimNIBS warp (neuronav_summary_to_mni, needs path.seg). It plots transducer, focus, and beam axis over the MNI152 head outline, with filters per subject, session, and target.

items.title: Issues Panel
items.text: The panel lists what PRESTUS would otherwise report only at load or run time: unknown or misspelt keys, deprecated keys, wrong types and values, unsupported backend and multi-transducer combinations, missing inputs and calibration entries, heating timing problems, a path.acoustic_input or follow-up parent that is missing or does not match, a target_isppa_wcm2 that cannot be met or that adds a free-water simulation, and a project config_default.yaml that lacks keys added since it was copied. Clicking an issue opens its field. Open the panel from the error and warning counts in the header, or with Ctrl+Shift+I.

items.title: Run Tab
items.text:
• Validate in MATLAB only runs load_parameters.
  • Run locally writes run_<study>.m next to the config and runs it with matlab -batch, with platform: matlab for that run only. You can run the launcher yourself with run('run_<study>.m').
  • Submit to cluster (with sbatch or qsub on this computer) writes submit_<study>.m, which keeps the config's platform and hpc.* settings, and runs it; PRESTUS submits the jobs. MATLAB exits once they are submitted, unless hpc.wait_for_job is set.
  • Plan shows what the run will do: each stage as run, reused, or skipped, the jobs it submits, the files it writes, and the predicted load (Run Time and Resources).
  • Pipeline options (sequential follow-ups, per-stage limits of the multi-ISPPA and uncertainty pipelines) are not config keys. The Nexus keeps them per user and study and writes them into the launchers.
  • Stop ends MATLAB together with its launcher.

The Jobs sub-tab reads the job IDs from the log and follows them; their logs are read from <output>/log_hpc, from the file system when the folder is visible, else over SSH. Cancel selected runs scancel or qdel. Jobs that a job submits itself (the k-Wave drive check, pipeline stages) join the list, marked ↳. The list is kept when the Nexus closes; Clear finished removes the jobs that have ended. When a job completes, the Results tab reads its outputs; when a run or job ends while the Nexus is in the background, it notifies you.

A progress bar above the log (local runs) and above the selected job's logs (cluster jobs, also in the Progress column) shows the current stage, how far its solver is, and the time left; for a whole-pipeline run also the whole run, from the predicted stage times. A job whose time left exceeds its remaining time limit is flagged in red (it will probably end in TIMEOUT). Drive checks and study runs also count their depths or runs. How exact this is depends on the solver (backends): the k-Wave C++ binaries and the thermal simulation report their progress, the k-Wave MATLAB solvers only a time estimate (shown with ~), and the jwave Helmholtz solver only its GMRES residual, with live view (else elapsed time only). Cluster jobs are checked every 30 s. With simulation.live_view: 1, a Live view sub-tab appears with the first frame and shows the evolving pressure and temperature fields, one tab per field, in mm with the transducer and focus marked, and the peak temperature over time. A local run switches to it once; Live view on the progress card returns to it, also for the selected cluster job. examples/example_progress_water.yaml is a free-water run of a few minutes to try both.

Submitting over SSH

Submit over SSH submits from a computer without a scheduler, e.g. a laptop with the project drive mounted.

  • Set the login node (Host, e.g. user@mentat005.dccn.nl or an alias from ~/.ssh/config), the folder mapping (Local folder /Volumes/myproject is on the cluster /project/myproject), and the Setup commands run before MATLAB (e.g. module load slurm matlab/R2024a). The study folder must be under the mapped folder. The settings are kept per user in ~/.config/prestus_nexus/last_session.yaml.
  • Paths in the config under the mapped folder are translated, e.g. /Volumes/myproject/data/sim runs as /project/myproject/data/sim. They are passed to load_parameters as overrides; the config file stays unchanged. A local path outside the mapped folder cannot be translated, and the Nexus asks before submitting.
  • Connect… logs in once and keeps a shared OpenSSH connection for 8 h of idle time; with an SSH key it is not needed. Without a key or an open connection, commands fail with "Permission denied". Connection sharing needs OpenSSH 8.4 or later on macOS or Linux; on Windows, use a key.
  • If the host's matlab is a site wrapper that needs a display (the log says "No DISPLAY variable set"), set Remote MATLAB to <matlabroot>/bin/matlab.

items.title: Results Tab
items.text:
The Run list names each run in the results folder from its output affix. For async coupling, a second list switches between the joint result and each transducer's own field (_trans-NN).

  • Overview groups the run's values as the ITRUSST consensus asks TUS studies to report them, with the non-significant risk limits of the HTML report. Each row names its source (metrics CSV, free-water run, targeting CSV, placement record, equipment library, or open config). Pulse timing and transducer geometry come from the open config, which can differ from what the run used. ISPTA per tissue is that tissue's ISPPA times the run's duty cycle. For runs without the focal_fwhm_* columns, the Nexus measures the focal widths on the run's intensity map, which can differ from PRESTUS's by a fraction of a voxel.
  • Spatial shows only the maps the run wrote; positions come from the run's placement record, else from the config.
  • Heating reads cache/sub-XXX_<medium>_HEAT<affix>.mat (written by modules.run_thermal_analysis; not with the BabelBrain thermal backend). It needs SciPy, or h5py for -v7.3 files.

items.title: Follow-up Runs
items.text:
Follow-up… creates a new study config that starts from the selected run:

Type What it reuses New intensity The run's pressure map (path.acoustic_input): no acoustic simulation (Reusing outputs). New timing (thermal only) The pressure map; only the thermal simulation runs. New placement, same head The head model, built once (headmodel.reuse_across_placements). Pose from the time-reversal search A pose or its refocusing phases from the run's pose table (Pose search). Sequential The run's end temperature and thermal dose. Added to this config's Pipeline options rather than run on its own (Sequential runs).

Each follow-up gets a new io.output_affix and is saved next to the parent as <parent>_<type>_<affix>.yaml. It records its parent in a # nexus-followup: comment line, which MATLAB ignores.

items.title: Study Tab
items.text:
The run table is the study manifest (study.manifest; Study setup): one row per run, and settings not in the table come from the study config. An empty cell takes the study value.

  • Without a Table file, the first save writes <config name>_runs.tsv next to the config and sets study.manifest.
  • Import from Localite… reads the neuronav_gui outputs under path.localite_post and makes one run per target, or one per session with the targets assigned to transducers (Importing runs from Localite).
  • Check all runs runs prestus_study_start(config, 'DryRun', true); Run all runs locally writes and runs run_study_<study>.m; Build group report runs prestus_group_report_start(config). Their output streams to the Run tab.

items.title: Timing Diagram and TUS Calculator
items.text:
The Sonication protocol card draws the protocol from timing.* and writes back what you change in it: drag an edge, or click it and type a duration (20 ms, 500 µs; the PRI also takes a frequency, 5 Hz). Dragged values snap to two significant digits.

The TUS calculator (Radboud University, MIT licence) estimates derived quantities for a protocol. The Nexus does not repeat its calculations; it exchanges settings files with it. Export for TUS calculator… writes a JSON file for the calculator's Upload settings; Import from TUS calculator… reads a file downloaded from it (JSON or YAML) and shows the values before setting them.

Both use the same ramp convention: the ramp duration is the rise (= fall) time at each end of a pulse (timing.pulse_ramp_dur, timing.pulse_ramp_shape). PRESTUS models pulse ramps only, so the calculator's pulse-train and repetition ramps are exported as 0 and reported when an imported file sets them. A level disabled in the calculator sets the matching PRESTUS durations to 0.

The Sonication sequence card below sets up stances fired one after another (Planning a Sequence in the Nexus).

items.title: MATLAB Session
items.text:
The Calibration and Localite pages bring calibration_gui and neuronav_gui into the Nexus and compute in MATLAB, with the same functions. Their first step waits for MATLAB to start.

When the session starts and ends

The Nexus keeps one MATLAB session open, started the first time an action needs it, e.g. Load, Predict, or Fit on the Calibration page or Detect series on the Localite page; showing a page does not start it. The MATLAB binary is the one set on the Run tab. The first call takes as long as MATLAB needs to start (15–60 s); later ones take only the computation. The pages show the session's state (starting, ready, working), and Stop ends it.

  • The session ends by itself after 30 min without use, since it holds a MATLAB licence, and when the Nexus quits or stops answering. The next call starts a new one, and the pages open their transducer or session again.
  • Long work does not use the session: batch ingestion and the k-Wave drive check are written as scripts and run on the Run tab, where the log streams and Stop works.
How the session exchanges data

The session is nexus_bridge, started with matlab -batch. The Nexus and MATLAB exchange JSON files in a temporary folder. MATLAB runs only nexus_calibration, nexus_neuronav, and nexus_ping from it.

items.title: Standalone MATLAB GUIs
items.text:
The Tools menu opens the Localite and Calibration pages, and also opens PRESTUS's standalone MATLAB GUIs in an interactive MATLAB session (they need the MATLAB desktop):

  • neuronav_gui in MATLAB… (Localite ingestion). The study config is saved first and passed to the GUI.
  • calibration_gui in MATLAB… saves entries to transducer.library_path when that is set. Its View geometry and New… are on the Equipment sub-tab (New transducer or driving system in the Nexus).

items.title: Simulation Outputs
items.text:
A run writes its results as files: a metrics table, NIfTI maps, figures, and an HTML report, plus caches and stage outputs that a later run can reuse instead of recomputing. Knowing which file holds a value lets you check that the numbers you report come from the settings you intended.

On this page:

  • Output Directory Structure: the folders and files of a run.
  • Where Outputs Live: which folder each stage writes and what it depends on.
  • NIfTI Images: the medium, acoustic, and thermal maps in T1 and MNI space.
  • Figures: the PNG overlays of intensity and temperature.
  • HTML Report: the sections of the per-run report.
  • Debug Outputs: the intermediate figures and volumes of debug mode, and the debug report.
  • Group Outputs: the files of the group report and maps.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To find a specific file, or to see where a stage writes its results. Read Reading your results first.
  • Before you start: A finished run.

Subpages:

  • Metrics Table Columns: every column of the metrics CSV and the reference levels; for anyone reporting or checking a value.
  • Reusing Earlier Outputs and Caches: starting a run from earlier stage outputs, overwrite behaviour, and cache checks; for anyone re-running, resuming, or chaining runs.

items.title: Output Directory Structure
items.text:
A finished run writes to <path.sim>/sub-XXX/:

sub-XXX_<medium>_report<affix>.html       ← self-contained HTML report
sub-XXX_layered_segmentation_report<affix>.html ← head-model postprocessing, step by step (layered; report.segmentation)
sub-XXX_<medium>_debug_report<affix>.html ← all debug outputs (simulation.debug; report.debug)
sub-XXX_<medium><affix>.csv               ← quantitative metrics
sub-XXX_<medium><affix>_targeting.csv     ← targeting accuracy (layered or phantom)
sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json             ← resolved transducer positions (T1 voxels; every placement mode)

nii/                                       ← NIfTI maps (medium, transducer model, acoustic, thermal); not created with modules.run_nifti_creation: 0
img/                                       ← PNG figures (acoustic, thermal, preprocessing)
babelbrain/                                ← BabelBrain inputs (io.export_babelbrain or acoustic_backend: babelbrain)

cache/                                     ← regenerable intermediates
    sub-XXX_<medium>_parameters_<yyMMdd_HHmm><affix>.mat   parameters snapshot at start
    sub-XXX_<medium>_report_parameters<affix>.mat          final parameters (report re-rendering)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_cropped_smoothed<affix>.mat           cropped/smoothed head (layered)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_segqc<affix>.mat                      head-model postprocessing records (segmentation report)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_grid_cache<affix>.mat                 grid stage (io.save_grid_cache)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_planimg<affix>.mat                    planning-image sidecar (always)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_medium_cache<affix>.mat               medium stage (io.save_medium_cache)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_kwave_source<affix>.mat               source (io.save_source_matrices)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_results<affix>.mat                    acoustic results + provenance
    sub-XXX_<medium>_heating_res<affix>.mat                thermal results (io.save_thermal_matrices)
    sub-XXX_<medium>_HEAT<affix>.mat                       thermal time courses (thermal analysis; not BabelBrain)

log/
    sub-XXX_<medium>_<timestamp><affix>.txt                MATLAB diary of the run
    sub-XXX_<medium>_parameters<affix>.yaml                resolved parameters (human-readable; io.prestus_version: version, commit, commit date, uncommitted changes)

debug/                                     ← diagnostic artefacts (simulation.debug: 1 only)
    manifest.jsonl  one line per debug file: stage, caption, writing function
    preproc/        head preprocessing (rotation, cropping, skull visualisations)
    medium/         medium mapping (grid-space property matrices, pCT)
    source/         source/transducer setup (element distribution plots)
    babelbrain/     BabelBrain FOV and domain-coverage diagnostics
  • Cache files are regenerable. With io.overwrite_files = 'never', existing files are reloaded instead of recomputed (Overwrite behaviour). io.save_matrices = 0 writes none of the optional cache matrices; 1 saves all of them. The parameter snapshots and the planning-image sidecar are always written. Per-step flags such as io.save_acoustic_matrices override it when set.
  • Debug files are written only with parameters.simulation.debug = 1 (Debug outputs).
  • Run statistics: each run with an acoustic or thermal simulation adds one line to <path.sim>/run_stats.jsonl (one file per path.sim, shared by all subjects): grid size, time steps, thermal steps, simulation durations, solver, partition, and peak RAM. The Nexus estimates resources from it (Resource estimates).

items.title: Where Outputs Live
items.text:
Each location belongs to one level. A level only reads the levels above it, and each folder has one writer.

Level Depends on Locations Written by Inputs none path.anat (T1/T2), path.localite_raw (raw Localite exports), path.localite_t1 (planning T1s) you / the scanner / Localite; PRESTUS only reads them Subject derivatives the subject's images path.seg (SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX), path.pct (pseudo-CT), <parent of path.seg>/mni/sub-XXX/ (T1 in MNI space), path.localite_post (ingested Localite markers) segmentation (layered media; io.overwrite_simnibs), pseudo-CT generation, neuronav_ingest_markers Placement subject derivatives, target, transducer geometry, placement settings path.placement (default <path.sim>/placement): sub-XXX/<mode>/<target_name>/ the placement stage (heuristic, PlanTUS, TUS_entry) Simulation everything above, plus the acoustic/thermal setup path.sim/sub-XXX/ (this page) the simulation pipeline
  • Placement does not depend on the medium, grid, or drive level. Point several setups at one path.placement to reuse a heuristic, PlanTUS, or TUS_entry result. Each run folder holds everything the run produced and a run record, placement_run.json. manual, mni, and localite placements have no run folder. The simulation records the positions it used in sub-XXX_placement<affix>.json.
  • path.localite_export is a hand-off folder, not a level. It holds copies of placement results for import into Localite (heuristic position table, Localite-ready T1).
  • SimNIBS m2m_sub-XXX folders are only read after segmentation. For the pseudo-CT location, see (pseudo-)CT.

items.title: NIfTI Images
items.text:
PRESTUS exports 3D volumes (2D for axisymmetric simulations) in subject-native T1 space and MNI-152 space. Each group of maps is written as soon as its stage finishes. MNI maps (layered media, io.save_MNI) are warped with the nonlinear SimNIBS charm transform (subject2mni) onto SimNIBS's MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz: FSL's 1 mm MNI152 template, BIDS/TemplateFlow MNI152NLin6Asym (identical to FSL's file in SimNIBS 4.1.0).

  • Subject T1 space: sub-XXX_<medium>_T1w<affix>_<type>.nii.gz
  • MNI space: sub-XXX_<medium>_MNI<affix>_<type>.nii.gz
Medium maps (written after medium setup) Type Resampling Description medium_masks nearest Tissue label mask (integer indices)

With io.save_property_maps: 1 (layered media), each acoustic and thermal property map is also written, to nii/properties/<property>_T1w<affix>.nii.gz (and _MNI<affix>), without the sub-XXX_<medium> prefix: sound_speed, density, alpha_coeff, alpha_power, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, perfusion_coeff, absorption_fraction, and absorption_np.

Transducer model (written after medium setup) Type Resampling Description transducer none (built on the T1 grid) Model of the planned transducer bowl(s), from the planned T1-voxel positions; the bowl's rear centre is at trans_pos. 1 = emitting face across the active aperture (smallest elem_id_mm to largest elem_od_mm), 0.5 = the display thickness behind it (io.transducer_nii_back_mm), 0 = elsewhere, including the central opening. The aperture edges follow the profile's mm limits, not whole voxels. Layered medium, annular transducers, io.save_transducer_nii. T1 space only. Acoustic maps (written after acoustic analysis) Type Description Itp Temporal-peak intensity [W/cm²] Ipa Pulse-average intensity (IPA) [W/cm²]; with io.save_Ipa and timing.pd Ita Temporal-average intensity [W/cm²]; with io.save_Ita MI Mechanical index pressure Peak pressure [Pa]; with a JSON sidecar so a later run can start from it (Starting from earlier stage outputs) focal_mask_3dB −3 dB focal zone binary mask (IPA ≥ 50 % of peak; restricted to brain for layered, to beyond-exit-plane for free-field) focal_mask_6dB −6 dB / FWHM focal zone binary mask (IPA ≥ 25 % of peak = P ≥ Pmax/2; same region restriction) Thermal maps (written after thermal analysis) Type Description heating Maximum temperature during sonication [°C] heating_end Temperature at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) [°C] heatrise Temperature rise above baseline [°C] heatrise_end Temperature rise above baseline at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) [°C] CEM43 CEM43 thermal dose, k-Wave form [min] CEM43_end CEM43 (k-Wave) at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) [min] CEM43_iso CEM43 thermal dose, ISO form [min] CEM43_iso_end CEM43 (ISO) at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) [min]

items.title: Figures
items.text: PRESTUS saves PNG overlays of intensity and temperature on the segmentation.

items.title: HTML Report
items.text:
sub-XXX_<medium>_report<affix>.html is a self-contained report in the output directory. Sections:

Section Content Safety dashboard colour-coded cards for all ITRUSST-limited metrics (green / amber / red); thermal cards use the formulation selected by parameters.thermal.cem43_iso Simulation summary key acoustic and thermal values Methods ITRUSST-aligned methods text (CC0) with reference list: software, transducer, grid, tissue properties, pulse timing, thermal model, exposure values. Copy methods text / Copy text + references copy it as formatted text with a plain-text fallback. Check it against your study before use Configuration summary parameters used for the run Medium properties per-tissue acoustic and thermal properties (layered only) Acoustic results intensity overlays and the full acoustic metrics table Thermal results temperature, CEM43 (k-Wave), and CEM43 (ISO) plots (if heating was simulated) Post-hoc water simulation free-field reference results (if run) Diagnostics links to the segmentation report and the debug report Log full pipeline execution log

Example report on a phantom: Download example HTML

items.title: Debug Outputs
items.text:
When a result looks wrong, the intermediate states of the run show where it went wrong. simulation.debug: 1 writes them to debug/, one subfolder per stage, and sub-XXX_<medium>_debug_report<affix>.html collects them on one page: the figures of each stage with a caption and the function that wrote them, and a table of the volumes. If the run fails, the page is still written and opens with the error and its stack.

Finer settings choose what debug mode writes. simulation.debug_stages limits the outputs to some stages (preproc, medium, source, babelbrain), simulation.debug_figures and simulation.debug_volumes switch the figures (PNG) and the intermediate volumes (NIfTI) on or off, and report.debug the report. Each volume is about the size of the head volume, so simulation.debug_volumes: 0 saves most of the disk space. See simulation parameters.

The report also links the segmentation report, the SimNIBS charm outputs (segmentation.debug keeps more of them), the pseudo-CT folder (pct.debug keeps its intermediates), and the run logs. Figures are linked, not embedded, so keep the report next to its debug/ folder when you move it.

Reading the debug volumes

The *_final volumes in debug/preproc/ are back-projected to the T1 and overlay it in any NIfTI viewer. The matrix_* volumes in debug/medium/, the balloon_mask* volumes, and debug/source/*_source_mask are in simulation-grid voxels without a T1 header; open them alongside each other, not over the T1. The source mask shows where the transducers sit against the skin in matrix_density; with a partial acoustic FOV it is on the cropped grid and no longer overlays the medium matrices.

items.title: Group Outputs
items.text:
The group tools read existing per-run outputs and never simulate; see Group analysis.

Study (prestus_group_report_start on a config with study.manifest, or the end of prestus_study_start), written to <path.sim>/group/<study.name>/:

group_<name>_report.html                  ← self-contained group HTML report
group_<name>_runs.csv                     ← one row per run: settings, metrics, targeting
plots/
    group_<medium>_<metric>_<name>.png      box plots (intensity, mi, conditions, targeting, maxT, riseT, cem43)
    group_<cond>_focal_overlap.png          MNI overlap figure per condition
maps/
    group_<cond>_focal_overlap_3dB.nii.gz   fraction of runs covering each voxel
    group_<cond>_<Ipa|Itp>_mean.nii.gz      mean intensity (and _sd)
    group_<cond>_heatrise_mean.nii.gz       mean temperature rise (heating runs)
log/
    plan_<time>.tsv / launch_<time>.tsv     study dry-run plan / launch log
log_hpc/                                  ← dependent study-report job (HPC)

Subjects (no manifest: all subjects with the same simulation.medium and io.output_affix; prestus_group_report_start, or modules.generate_group_report = 1 after each subject), written to path.sim:

group_<medium>_report<affix>.html         ← self-contained group HTML report
group_<medium>_runs<affix>.csv            ← one row per subject
group_plots/
    group_<medium>_<metric><affix>.png      box plots: intensity (Isppa / Ipa_target), mi (per tissue),
                                            targeting (MNI centroids, focus error), maxT, riseT, cem43
group/<medium><affix>/maps/, plots/       ← group MNI maps (manual prestus_group_report_start only)

Thermal plots (maxT, riseT, cem43) need a layered medium with heating results. See Group HTML report for the report contents.

items.title: Metrics Table Columns
items.text:
The metrics CSV holds every number a run reports: intensities, pressures, mechanical indices, focal volumes, and, with heating, temperatures and thermal doses. Each column has a precise definition and unit, and several are checked against the ITRUSST non-significant risk limits, so the column you quote decides what your reported value means.

On this page:

  • Metrics Table: the file and where targeting accuracy is written.
    • Intensity nomenclature: how IPA, ISPPA, and the mechanical index are computed.
    • Acoustic metrics: global and tissue-specific acoustic columns.
    • Thermal metrics: global and tissue-specific thermal columns.
    • Non-significant risk limits: the reference levels the report flags against.

At a glance

  • When you need it: To report a value from the CSV, or to check what a column measures.
  • Before you start: A finished run; see Simulation Outputs for where the CSV is written.

items.title: Metrics Table
items.text:
Filename: sub-XXX_<simulation_medium><affix>.csv

One CSV holds all quantitative metrics: acoustic metrics first, then thermal metrics if heating was simulated. Tissue-specific columns exist for layered and phantom simulations.

Targeting accuracy (modules.run_targeting_analysis, layered or phantom media) goes to sub-XXX_<simulation_medium><affix>_targeting.csv; see Targeting accuracy.

items.title: Intensity Nomenclature
items.text:
All intensity values are pulse-average intensity (IPA), computed from the steady-state peak pressure amplitude:

I = p² / (2ρc)   [W/cm²]

p is the peak pressure amplitude, ρ density, and c sound speed. The factor 2 averages over the sinusoid's cycle. The result is the temporal-peak intensity (ITP). IPA, the time-average intensity during the pulse, is ITP times the ramp factor of timing.pulse_ramp_dur and timing.pulse_ramp_shape; for pulses without a ramp IPA = ITP. The average over the repetition interval (ISPTA) also applies the duty cycle PD/PRI: it is the average within a pulse train, without the pulse-train duty cycle PTD/PTRI.

The spatial peak of IPA is ISPPA. IPA at a specific location (target point, radius average) is labelled IPA.

The mechanical index per voxel is MI = p⁻ / √f, with p⁻ the peak rarefaction (negative) pressure in MPa and f the centre frequency in MHz (IEC 62359 / FDA). PRESTUS uses the absolute value of p_min_all from k-Wave. For multi-transducer async combinations it uses the per-voxel most-negative pressure across transducers (p_min_async).

Darmani et al. (2022, Clinical Neurophysiology) give an overview of the nomenclature.

References

Darmani, G., Bergmann, T. O., Butts Pauly, K., Caskey, C. F., de Lecea, L., Fomenko, A., Fouragnan, E., Legon, W., Murphy, K. R., Nandi, T., Phipps, M. A., Pinton, G., Ramezanpour, H., Sallet, J., Yaakub, S. N., Yoo, S. S., & Chen, R. (2022). Non‑invasive transcranial ultrasound stimulation for neuromodulation. Clinical Neurophysiology, 135, 51–73. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinph.2021.12.010

items.title: Acoustic Metrics
items.text:
Focal distances come in two references: columns ending in _ep_mm count from the exit plane, as focal_distance_ep does; columns ending in _bowl_mm from the bowl apex (trans_pos). Group and comparison reports read the earlier real_focal_distance_mm as real_focal_distance_bowl_mm. See Transducer-Target Distance.

Global acoustic columns Column Unit Description subject_id none Subject identifier freq_Hz Hz Transducer centre frequency Isppa W/cm² ISPPA: maximum pulse-average intensity across the entire simulation grid Isptp W/cm² Spatial-peak temporal-peak intensity across the grid Ispta W/cm² Spatial-peak temporal-average intensity across the grid Isppa_after_exitplane W/cm² Maximum IPA beyond the transducer exit plane (or within brain if modelled) real_focal_distance_bowl_mm mm Distance from the bowl apex (trans_pos) to the location of maximum IPA real_focal_distance_ep_mm mm Distance from the exit plane to the location of maximum IPA; compare with focal_distance_ep Ipa_target W/cm² IPA at the specified target coordinate Ipa_target_radius W/cm² Mean IPA within a sphere of radius analysis.focus_area_radius mm centred on the target trans_pos_vox voxels Transducer position in simulation grid coordinates focus_pos_vox voxels Target focus position in simulation grid coordinates TIC none Cranial thermal index freefield_isppa_wcm2 W/cm² Free-water ISPPA of the same drive (layered and phantom simulations)

Water/free-field simulations also include Psptp (spatial peak temporal peak pressure), Ptp_target (temporal peak pressure at the target) and MI (global mechanical index from peak rarefaction pressure, unitless; ITRUSST limit 1.9, labelled "MI (free water)" in the report). They also include the ITRUSST focal metrics (focal_vol_3dB_mm3, focal_vol_6dB_mm3, focal_centroid_3dB_bowl_mm, focal_centroid_3dB_ep_mm, focal_flhm_center_bowl_mm, focal_flhm_center_ep_mm, focal_fwhm_axial_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_min_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_max_mm), computed beyond the transducer exit plane.

Tissue-specific acoustic columns (layered and phantom simulations) Column Unit Description Isppa_brain W/cm² Maximum IPA within brain tissue (GM + WM) Isppa_skull W/cm² Maximum IPA within skull bone Isppa_skin W/cm² Maximum IPA within skin Psptp_brain Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within brain tissue Psptp_skull Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within skull bone Psptp_skin Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure within skin Psptp Pa Global spatial peak temporal peak pressure across the entire grid (also written for water/free-field runs) Ptp_target Pa Temporal peak pressure at the target coordinate MI_brain none Maximum mechanical index within brain tissue (GM + WM) MI_skull none Maximum mechanical index within skull bone MI_skin none Maximum mechanical index within skin MI_tc none Transcranial MI: maximum mechanical index across all intracranial voxels (WM, GM, CSF, blood; skull bone excluded). Primary safety metric for cavitation risk at the sonication target. Empty when the focal lobe reaches the grid edge focal_fwhm_lateral_min_mm, focal_fwhm_lateral_max_mm mm Narrowest and widest −3 dB focal width through the brain peak in the plane perpendicular to the transducer axis, measured every 5°; equal for a round focus Air-cavity columns (with headmodel.air_cavities)

Written for layered simulations when the air-cavity check is on.

Column Unit Description aircav_n_vox voxels Internal air-cavity voxels on the simulation grid Psptp_aircav Pa Spatial peak temporal peak pressure inside the cavities aircav_rel_db dB Psptp_aircav relative to Psptp_brain aircav_beam_frac_max 0–1 Largest share of the −6 dB beam cross-section inside the cavities at any depth between the exit plane and the focus aircav_beam_frac_depth_mm mm Depth of that share from the exit plane aircav_beam_frac_vol 0–1 Share of the prefocal −6 dB beam volume inside the cavities aircav_flag 0/1 1 when aircav_rel_db exceeds warn_db or aircav_beam_frac_max exceeds warn_beam_fraction

items.title: Thermal Metrics
items.text:
Thermal columns are only written when heating simulations are run. Temperature is simulated over the full sonication protocol (on/off cycles) with the Pennes bioheat equation. All values are spatial maxima within the respective tissue.

Global thermal columns Column Unit Description maxT °C Global maximum temperature reached at any point during sonication endT °C Global maximum temperature at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) maxCEM43 min Global maximum CEM43 (k-Wave form) over the full protocol maxCEM43end min Global maximum CEM43 (k-Wave form) at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) maxCEM43iso min Global maximum CEM43 (ISO form) over the full protocol maxCEM43isoend min Global maximum CEM43 (ISO form) at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) Tissue-specific thermal columns Column Unit Description maxT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature in each tissue during sonication. ITRUSST limit: 39 °C endT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature in each tissue at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) riseT_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature rise above baseline (maxT − baseline). ITRUSST limit: 2 °C riseT37_brain/skull/skin °C Maximum temperature rise above 37 °C. ITRUSST limit: 2 °C rise_endT_brain/skull/skin °C Temperature rise above baseline at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) CEM43_brain/skull/skin min Maximum CEM43 (k-Wave form) in each tissue. ITRUSST limits: brain 2 min, skull 16 min, skin 21 min CEM43_end_brain/skull/skin min CEM43 (k-Wave form) in each tissue at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur) CEM43iso_brain/skull/skin min Maximum CEM43 (ISO form) in each tissue CEM43iso_end_brain/skull/skin min CEM43 (ISO form) in each tissue at the end of the simulated protocol (after the last pulse train and timing.post_ptri_dur)

Both CEM43 formulations are always computed; see Thermal simulations for the formulas. The HTML report shows the one selected by parameters.thermal.cem43_iso.

items.title: Non-Significant Risk Limits
items.text:
The HTML report flags each metric against the ITRUSST consensus non-significant risk limits for transcranial ultrasound (Aubry et al., 2025, Brain Stimulation):

Metric Limit MI transcranial 1.9 MI (free water) 1.9 Temperature rise (a) 2 °C Maximum temperature (b) 39 °C CEM43 (brain) (c) 2 min CEM43 (skull) (c) 16 min CEM43 (skin) (c) 21 min

For thermal estimates, non-significant risk can be characterised by a, b, or c. These limits are for quick reference. Always check the original reference and possible consensus updates. PRESTUS does not make independent recommendations.

items.title: Reusing Earlier Outputs and Caches
items.text:
A run can start from results an earlier run wrote instead of recomputing them: a segmentation, pseudo-CT, placement, or pressure map, or the caches in its own cache/ folder. Reuse saves time, but a reused file built from other settings gives results that do not match the configuration, so PRESTUS records and checks the settings each file depends on.

On this page:

  • Starting from Earlier Stage Outputs: starting a run from a placement, pseudo-CT, or pressure map.
  • Overwrite Behaviour: when existing files are reused or recomputed.
  • Cache Reuse Checks: how a reused cache is checked against the current settings.

At a glance

  • When you need it: You re-run or resume a subject, run a chained pipeline, or start a run from an earlier placement or pressure map.
  • Before you start: An earlier run's output folder; see Simulation Outputs for the folder layout.

items.title: Starting from Earlier Stage Outputs
items.text:
PRESTUS keeps two kinds of intermediate results apart:

  • Within-run caches (cache/ of a simulation folder) are reloaded only by the run that wrote them, or a re-run of it. io.overwrite_files decides reuse (Overwrite behaviour).
  • Stage outputs are complete results that a later, separate run starts from. Each has a BIDS-style JSON sidecar whose signature lists the settings the output depends on. The later run compares it with its own settings.
Stage outputs and compared settings Stage output Sidecar Picked up by Compared settings SimNIBS segmentation, path.seg/m2m_sub-XXX/ none (standard SimNIBS output) every layered run, when final_tissues.nii.gz exists (io.overwrite_simnibs) SimNIBS version (charm_log.html) and charm settings (settings.ini): a warning, see Segmentation Pseudo-CT, <pct folder>/pseudoCT.nii.gz pseudoCT.json every run with pct.enabled: 1, when it exists pct.skull_mapping (with custom_slope / custom_intercept) and the segmentation (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz) Placement run, <path.placement>/sub-XXX/<mode>/<target_name>/ placement_run.json heuristic, PlanTUS, and TUS_entry placement, per placement.reuse placement.<mode> (without tool install paths), the transducer without its positions, and the segmentation (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz) Pressure map, nii/sub-XXX_<medium>_T1w<affix>_pressure.nii.gz …_pressure.json a run with path.acoustic_input set to the NIfTI simulation.medium, grid (without thermal_*), layers, headmodel, pct, medium_properties, the transducer (geometry and grid positions), the subject, and, for layered, the segmentation

io.cache_signature_check handles a mismatch (error by default, warn, off). An output without a sidecar (e.g. a pressure map from another tool) is used with the warning prestus:cache:unverified.

Placement (placement.reuse).

Value Effect auto (default) Reuse a recorded run whose settings match; otherwise run the placement again and replace the record. Under io.overwrite_files: never, a mismatch is handled like always always Require a recorded run never Always run the tool

placement.reuse is independent of io.overwrite_files: a PlanTUS or TUS_entry result is reused while the simulation stages are recomputed. placement_run.mat records are also read.

Pressure map (path.acoustic_input). Point path.acoustic_input at a T1w pressure NIfTI from an earlier run. The new run skips the acoustic simulation and the free-water baseline, puts the map onto its own grid (including an acoustic FOV), rescales it to its transducer.target_isppa_wcm2 using the sidecar's isppa.level_wcm2, and then runs acoustic analysis and the thermal stage as after a simulation. It needs the T1 → grid transform (simulation.medium layered or phantom, a 3D grid) and the k-Wave grid of the source stage (modules.run_source_setup: 1). In the Nexus, Results ▸ Follow-up… with New intensity or New timing writes such a config for you (Follow-up runs).

Limits:

  • The map is stored at T1 resolution, so a map from a finer simulation grid has lost some peak sharpness.
  • The map has no peak negative pressure, so the mechanical index uses the peak pressure (with a warning).
  • A map without a sidecar is used as it is and cannot be rescaled.
Sidecar format

Every sidecar starts with the same header:

{
  "sidecar_version": 1,
  "kind": "acoustic_pressure",
  "created": "2026-10-07T16:00:00",
  "generated_by": {"name": "PRESTUS", "version": "v0.6.1-42-gabc1234",
                   "commit": "abc1234", "commit_date": "2026-10-07", "dirty": "no"},
  "subject_id": 1,
  "...": "kind-specific fields",
  "signature": {"...": "settings the output depends on"}
}

items.title: Overwrite Behaviour
items.text:
io.overwrite_files controls whether existing files are reused or recomputed.

Value Single run Chained pipelines: intermediate stages Chained pipelines: output stages never Reuse every existing file Resume from cache Skip if the output exists always (default) Recompute everything Resume from cache Always re-run, overwrite outputs force Same as always Always re-run Always re-run, overwrite outputs ask Prompt per file (interactive only) Resume from cache Skip if the output exists

Under never or ask, an acoustic or thermal stage that recomputes its results (no cache to reuse, e.g. with io.save_matrices: 0) still replaces its existing NIfTI outputs, so the NIfTI and CSV outputs of a folder always come from the same run. io.overwrite_simnibs governs SimNIBS segmentations separately.

Use force when an input of the intermediate caches has changed: transducer placement, transducer or source parameters, grid, segmentation, or medium properties. Grid, medium, and acoustic caches detect such changes when they are reused (Cache reuse checks); force rebuilds them instead of stopping the run. Alternatively, delete the relevant cache/ files before resubmitting.

Chained pipelines

Chained pipelines split one run into separate jobs. Each job reuses what the previous stage wrote:

Pipeline Intermediate stages Output stages Async multi-transducer (Multi-Transducer Modelling) Stage-0 preproc, per-transducer acoustic, combine Joint thermal + report, water validation Multi-ISPPA (Multi-ISPPA Mode) Stage-1 acoustic Per-ISPPA thermal + report, summary report Uncertainty (Uncertainty Quantification) Stage-1 preprocessing Variant simulations + reports, uncertainty report

With the default always, resubmitting a finished chained run reuses the acoustic simulations and regenerates the CSV, NIfTI, and HTML outputs. Within a chained run, sub-jobs that consume a shared cache (e.g. per-transducer acoustic jobs loading the Stage-0 grid) always load it, even under force. Only the stage that owns the cache rebuilds it.

items.title: Cache Reuse Checks
items.text:
Grid, medium, and acoustic caches are named by subject, medium, and affix only. Each cache therefore stores the settings it depends on (cache_signature). A reused cache built from different settings stops the run by default (io.cache_signature_check).

Mismatch handling

When a cache is reused (under io.overwrite_files: never, after a declined overwrite prompt, or in the intermediate stages of a chained pipeline under always) and the settings differ, io.cache_signature_check decides:

Value Effect error (default) Stop with prestus:cache:signatureMismatch, naming the differing keys. warn Warn and reuse the cache anyway. off No check.

A cache without a signature is reused with the warning prestus:cache:unverified. Stage-output sidecars are checked the same way (Starting from earlier stage outputs).

Acoustic cache on a different grid

A reused acoustic cache whose grid size differs from this run's (for example after a change to the head model, which sets the grid extent) is re-simulated, or stops the run when it sets up no source. With io.acoustic_cache_remap: 1, the field is mapped onto this run's grid instead: both grids are placed in world space by their planning images (the cache run's *_planimg*.mat sidecar and this run's), partial FOV boxes by their offsets, and pressures are resampled as p² so that intensity and heat source keep their average. The run warns (acoustic_stage:cacheRemapped) with the shift, scale, and coverage, which are also stored in the acoustic provenance (cache_remap). The field was computed through the cache run's head model, so near tissue boundaries it may not match this run's medium; to keep the two together, reuse the cache run's head and grid caches instead (io.preproc_affix with io.reuse_upstream_caches).

What each cache compares Cache Compared settings Grid (*_grid_cache*.mat) simulation.medium, grid, layers, headmodel, pct, and the transducer (geometry and positions after placement) Medium (*_medium_cache*.mat) the grid settings above, plus medium_properties Acoustic (*_results*.mat) the medium settings above except absorption_coeff (thermal only), plus subject_id and grid.acoustic_fov_*; not grid.thermal_*

For simulation.medium: phantom, each also compares the phantom file (size and modification date of final_tissues.nii.gz). For layered, each compares the segmentation by content (checksum of final_tissues.nii.gz), so a re-run of charm with another SimNIBS version or other settings is detected, while a copied or moved segmentation still matches. A cache written before the checksum was recorded counts the segmentation as changed when final_tissues.nii.gz is newer than the cache file.

Not compared, because they do not change these caches: paths, I/O, HPC, and module flags; the drive level (target_isppa_wcm2, tx_calibration), which only scales the acoustic field; and, for grid and medium caches, the partial acoustic FOV (grid.acoustic_fov_*), which is cropped after the grid and medium stages. A run that reuses a cache keeps its own values of these settings.

Sub-jobs that load a cache owned by another stage of the same chained run are not checked.

items.title: PRESTUS Parameters
items.text:
Every configuration parameter is listed with its default and what it does, grouped by the YAML struct it belongs to. The structs are spread over six pages by topic:

Page Structs Run, Paths, and Outputs subject_id, platform, path, startup, io, modules, report, study, hpc Transducer transducer Calibration calibration (config_calibration.yaml) Placement and Time Reversal placement, time_reversal Head Model and Grid segmentation, headmodel, pct, layers, medium_properties, grid Simulation and Sonication simulation, acoustic_backend, thermal_backend, timing, thermal, analysis

To find one key, use the search box or Find setting… (Ctrl+F) in the Nexus.

Parameters are organised in nested structs that map directly to YAML keys. config_default.yaml defines all parameters and their default values and should not be edited; a study config is merged on top and only needs the values that differ (see Configuring a study for the full layering, project defaults, and overrides). Parameters can also be set in MATLAB before calling prestus_pipeline_start(parameters). Mandatory parameters have no meaningful default and must always be provided.

items.title: Calibration Parameters
items.text:
Calibration fits a library entry to measured hydrophone profiles. These runs read their own config, config_calibration.yaml, loaded as parameters.calibration; this page lists its keys. How the fits work is described in Transducer Calibration.

On this page:

  • Transducer Calibration (calibration): keys of config_calibration.yaml.

items.title: Transducer Calibration (calibration)
items.text: Parameter Description Comments path_input_axial Directory containing axial intensity profiles; char_data_path in the equipment YAML is relative to it. Usually <PRESTUS>/local/profiles/ (see doc_transducer_library.md, Appendix). path_output Directory for saving free-water simulation results. path_output_profiles Directory for saving optimised profile data. filename_calibrated_CSV Filename of calibrated CSV data. Mandatory only when not generated within standalone script. save_in_calibration_folder Save in path_output (TRUE) or sim_path (FALSE). If TRUE, results are appended to existing calibration data. combinations Equipment combinations (must refer to combos in the transducer library, config/equipment/, or your own library). Multiple combinations can be specified. focal_depths_wrt_exit_plane List of focal depths to characterise [mm]. desired_intensities Desired free-water intensities [W/cm²]. add_FDO Append Focal Distance Offset (bowl-to-exit-plane distance)? Set to 1 if zero point in profiles reflects exit plane rather than bowl. axisymmetric2D Use axisymmetric 2D instead of default 3D free-water simulations? 1 = yes, 0 = no force_kwavearray Force use of kWaveArray for free-water simulations? If 0, uses the setting in the default/study config. opt_method Optimisation method. FEXminimize (open source) / GlobalSearch (MATLAB Global Optimization Toolbox) opt_limits Distance limits for optimisation [mm]. opt_weights Weighting of original profile during fitting. 1 = equal; >1 = Gaussian (narrower with larger values) opt_seed Random seed for optimisation. opt_use_initial_phases Use phases from transducer.annular.elem_phase_deg as the initial guess instead of random initialization. false (default); set to true when manufacturer-provided or previously calibrated phases are available. opt_upper_velocity Upper velocity in global search opt_phase_precession Constrain element phases during optimisation. false (default) = independent; 'linear' = strict ramp (phase_start + i * phase_step, 2 free params); 'monotonic' = ordered phases via cumulative non-negative increments (N params, monotonically constrained). opt_amp_validation Run free-water simulation to validate phases and amplitudes? 'always' (default) / 'never' / 'initial' (only for the first target intensity) / 'final' (only for the final target intensity) skip_front_peak_mm Distance from profile start to ignore [mm]. Avoids near-field artefacts in peak/FWHM calculations. profile_align Focus alignment when interpolating measured profiles to an unmeasured focal depth. 'label' (default) = column focal-depth headers; 'peak' = intensity peak beyond skip_front_peak_mm. See interpolate_axial_profiles. max_extrapolation_mm How far outside the measured depth range a desired depth may lie [mm]. 0 (default) = no extrapolation (error). Otherwise the nearest measured profile, shifted to the desired depth. focal_reference Convention for what a quoted focal depth means. flhm_3db (default, ITRUSST, intensity ≥ peak/2) / flhm_6db (Imasonic/IGT, intensity ≥ peak/4) / peak (raw intensity peak). Recorded into the sidecar YAML's meta.calibration.focal_reference. See Transducer Calibration.

items.title: Head Model and Grid Parameters
items.text:
These parameters turn the MRI into the simulation medium: segmentation, head-model preprocessing, pseudo-CT, tissue layers and properties, and the simulation grid.

On this page:

  • Segmentation (segmentation): options passed to SimNIBS charm, and defacing.
  • Head Model & Segmentation Preprocessing (headmodel): padding and mask preprocessing of the head model.
  • Pseudo-CT Skull Property Mapping (pct): pseudo-CT generation and its mapping to skull properties.
  • Tissue Layers (layers): which segmentation labels form each tissue layer.
  • Tissue Acoustic & Thermal Properties (medium_properties): per-tissue acoustic and thermal properties.
  • Simulation Grid (grid): resolution, dimensions, axisymmetric mode, and PML.

items.title: Simulation Grid (grid)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments resolution_mm Grid resolution (must be isotropic) [mm]. 0.5 default_dims Requested grid dimensions [voxels per dimension], or 'auto'. 'auto' Directly sets the simulation grid for water and phantom media (a phantom uses its own size unless it matches). For layered, the grid is determined by head preprocessing and this value is not used. 'auto' (water only, water_grid_dims) sizes the grid to the transducer, as the acoustic FOV of a head simulation: aperture + 2 × water_margin_mm (default 5 mm) laterally, focal distance from the bowl + z_beyond_focus_mm (default 40 mm) axially; [Nlateral, Naxial] with axisymmetric. For the shipped transducers this is 15–80 % of the points of [144, 144, 400] with the same free-water ISPPA (within 0.003 %) and focus (k-Wave drive benchmark). A non-annular (matrix) transducer placed by trans_pos/focus_pos, which are grid indices, keeps [144, 144, 400] ([144, 400] axisymmetric) with a warning. axisymmetric Run axisymmetric 2D simulation (kspaceFirstOrderAS). 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. See Acoustic Simulations. axisymmetric_output Form of axisymmetric results. 'auto' 'auto': expanded to 3D for phantom media or when heating is requested, otherwise the mirrored 2D plane. '2d': always the plane (not with heating); for fine grids, where the 3D expansion would not fit in memory. '3d': always expanded. mode Grid orientation before cropping. 'focal_axis' focal_axis: rotate so the mean beam axis of all transducers (beams averaged as axes) is z. transducer_axis: focal axis of transducer 1. ras_plus: no rotation, only rescaling. (principal_axis was removed and errors.) See Head preprocessing. async_layout Async coupling: one grid or one per transducer. 'shared' shared: one grid for all transducers, oriented by mode. per_transducer: one grid each, as a solo run would use (parallel on HPC). See Grid Geometry Mode. focal_axis_min_norm Fallback threshold of focal_axis mode. 0.5 When the mean beam-axis vector is shorter than this (beam axes too spread; only possible with three or more transducers), transducer 1's axis is used. pml_size Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) size [voxels]. 'auto' 'auto' chooses a size that keeps FFT grid sizes small-prime (k-Wave getOptimalPMLSize); a number fixes it. Absorbs waves at boundaries. Recommended for 3D. See k-Wave docs. For jwave, 'auto' is about 2.5 wavelengths instead (see jwave PML size). water_baseline_grid Grid of the k-Wave free-water baseline (ISPPA targeting). 'beam' 'beam': the box around the source and each beam axis from the bowl to 40 mm beyond the deeper of focus and geometric focus, +10 mm (WATER_BASELINE_BOX); in water nothing outside reflects back, so the free-field result is the same at a fraction of the cost. 'full': the whole simulation grid. jwave and axisymmetric runs use the full grid. pml_size_range Search range [min, max] of pml_size: 'auto' [grid points]. [10, 40] Passed to k-Wave's getOptimalPMLSize, which picks the FFT-friendliest size in the range. A thicker layer absorbs better at grazing incidence and costs grid points. pml_alpha PML absorption [Nepers per grid point]. [] Empty: k-Wave's default (2). Passed as k-Wave's PMLAlpha. source_ppw Points per wavelength (PPW) override. [] Calculated internally from resolution_mm and the medium's maximum sound speed if not set. Setting this overrides the internal calculation and fixes the number of spatial samples per wavelength used to derive the time step. min_ppw Minimum acceptable PPW at the fundamental frequency. 6 Checked against the slowest medium sound speed (worst-case spatial sampling). A warning is raised if the actual PPW falls below this value, along with the maximum resolution_mm that would satisfy it. source_cfl Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) fraction. 0.15 Controls temporal resolution independently of spatial resolution. Given a fixed spatial step dx, the time step is dt = CFL × dx / c_max, where c_max is the fastest medium sound speed (typically skull at ~2800 m/s). Smaller CFL = finer temporal sampling and must remain below the stability limit. Set to 0.15 (half k-Wave's default of 0.3) for additional stability margin in heterogeneous skull simulations. Can be relaxed toward 0.3 to reduce runtime, but should be validated against checkStability output. source_limit_fraction Fraction of the stability limit to use for time step. 0.9 After source setup, checkStability is called; if the CFL-derived dt exceeds the estimated limit, source setup reruns with dt = source_limit_fraction × dt_stability_limit. The final effective dt may therefore be smaller than CFL × dx / c_max. Set to 0 to disable. steady_state_transits Number of domain-diagonal one-way transits (at min. sound speed) before recording starts. 1 Total simulation duration is transits × diagonal / c_min. Compact, highly reflective domains (e.g. a partial-FOV crop with a high skull/water impedance mismatch, ~50% reflection coefficient for typical skull properties) may need more than one transit for multiply-reflected energy to decay to true periodic steady state. jwave's own cross-validation test uses roundtrips=20. steady_state_num_periods Number of trailing wave periods recorded as the steady-state window. 3 sensor.record_start_index is set so the last num_periods periods of the simulation are recorded for p_max_all/p_min_all/p_final. Increase together with steady_state_transits if reported Isppa/focal depth are still drifting as either is increased; a converged setup should stop changing further. bli_tolerance kWaveArray band-limited interpolation (BLI) tolerance. [] Empty: 0.1 (3D), 0.01 (axisymmetric). Smaller values keep more of the sinc tails (more source grid points). bli_upsampling_rate kWaveArray integration points per grid point. [] Empty: 10 (3D), 100 (axisymmetric). source_ppp Time steps per wave period (PPP) override. [] When set, dt = period / source_ppp; source_ppw and source_cfl are not used. For matching a reference simulation's time step (e.g. the ITRUSST k-Wave references). The stability recheck (source_limit_fraction) still applies. sim_time_us Fixed simulation duration [µs]. [] When set, replaces steady_state_transits (and jwave's PML margin); the last steady_state_num_periods periods of this duration are recorded. max_expand Maximum grid expansion for prime-number FFT optimisation [voxels]. 40 use_kWaveArray Use the kWaveArray class for transducer modelling? 1 1 = yes, 0 = no acoustic_fov_diameter_mm Lateral extent of the acoustic simulation FOV [mm], centred on the beam axis. When set together with acoustic_fov_length_mm, the acoustic simulation runs on a cropped sub-grid rather than the full head grid. Thermal simulation runs on the full head grid unless thermal_use_acoustic_fov: 1. [] Optional. 'auto': the outer element diameter of transducer(1) plus 4 voxels per side; a smaller numeric value is enlarged to that with a warning. See Partial FOV. acoustic_fov_length_mm Axial extent of the acoustic simulation FOV [mm], starting from the bowl apex (trans_pos) and extending distally. Must be large enough to enclose the focus and any near-field region of interest. [] Optional. Requires acoustic_fov_diameter_mm. 'auto': the trans_pos-to-focus_pos distance + z_beyond_focus_mm. See Partial FOV. thermal_use_acoustic_fov Run the thermal simulation within the acoustic FOV instead of the full grid. 0 1 is faster, with a less accurate cooling boundary. See Partial FOV. thermal_resolution_mm Grid resolution for the thermal simulation [mm]. When set to a value larger than resolution_mm, the acoustic pressure field is resampled to a coarser grid before thermal simulation, reducing memory and runtime. Heating and CEM43 maps are mapped back onto the acoustic grid (each thermal voxel's value kept). 3-D grids only. [] Optional. Defaults to resolution_mm (same grid). origin_ras_mm Phantom and water grids: RAS position of voxel [1,1,1] [mm]. (not set) Output NIfTIs get a diagonal RAS affine from it and resolution_mm, so they open in place in viewers; the simulation is unaffected. See Coordinate Reference Systems. thermal_fov_mm Spatial extent of the thermal simulation domain [mm], as a [1×3] vector [x y z]. When set, the thermal grid is cropped to a box of this size centred on the focus. Unlike the acoustic FOV crop, the thermal FOV has no physical justification for excluding regions: heat diffuses well beyond the focal zone, and cropping can underestimate temperature rise in neighbouring tissue. Use only for rapid prototyping, not for safety-critical results. Outside the box, the heating maps hold the baseline temperature and CEM43 maps zero. 3-D grids only. [] Optional. See Partial FOV.

items.title: Segmentation (segmentation)
items.text: Parameter Description Default Comments use_qform Force qform reorientation before charm segmentation? 0 Set to 1 if charm reports a qform/sform mismatch error. debug Pass --debug to charm for verbose segmentation output? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no noneck Pass --noneck to charm: the scan contains no neck. 0 1 = yes, 0 = no settings_file charm settings file (.ini), passed as --usesettings. '' '' = the charm.ini of the SimNIBS install. Start from a copy of that file. Keep it outside the m2m folder, which charm deletes when it re-runs. deface Create a defaced copy of the SimNIBS m2m folder (m2m_sub-NNN_defaced/) for safe sharing? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. Made again when the segmentation changes. See Defaced copy for sharing. Runs pydeface (must be installed in startup.simnibs_bin_path) on T1, UTE, bias-corrected, and MNI-space anatomical images. The original m2m folder is never modified. Only affects saved files; see io.deface_plots for figure defacing.

items.title: Head Model & Segmentation Preprocessing (headmodel)
items.text:
See Head Model.

Parameter Description Default Comments head_pad_mm Symmetric padding of the rotated head volume before CSF expansion and cropping [mm]; bowls outside the volume are auto-padded. 0 csf_expansion Dilation of the CSF brain mask into surrounding head regions, along each axis [mm]. 20 Converted to voxels at the grid resolution (preproc_crop_eCSF). smooth_method Mask smoothing filter type. 'gaussian' gaussian: isotropic blur, smooth edges, moderate erosion. box: uniform kernel, fastest, blocky, prone to skull holes. off: raw mask, no filtering or binarisation. See Layer mapping and smoothing. smooth_threshold_skull Binarisation threshold for skull mask; higher = thinner mask. 0.5 smooth_threshold_other Binarisation threshold for other masks; higher = thinner mask. 0.5 smooth_fwhm_mm FWHM of smoothing kernel [mm]. 1 Converted to voxels at the grid resolution, not the T1 resolution. smooth_properties Apply smoothing to acoustic property maps as well? false skull_fill_method Method for filling holes in the skull. 'rubberwrap' rubberwrap / imclose / off (skull as segmented, e.g. for animal or phantom label volumes). Filled holes become cortical skull. skull_wrap_radius_mm Rubber-wrap radius [mm]. 5 The wrap bridges skull holes up to about twice this width where brain meets skin; larger fills wider holes. Replaces skull_wrap_radius [grid voxels], which is converted at the run's grid.resolution_mm. skull_wrap_visualize Visualize rubber-wrap result? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. Avoid on HPC. reuse_across_placements Build the smoothed head model once per subject and only rotate and crop it for each transducer placement. false Saves the smoothing and hole filling (most of head preprocessing at fine resolution) in every run after the first of a subject: other poses, aims, or affixes in the same output folder. Cached as <dir_cache>/sub-XXX_<medium>_headmodel_<res>mm.mat with the settings it depends on; rebuilt when they change. With grid.mode: ras_plus the result equals per-placement preprocessing exactly (checked on one head, two poses). With a rotated mode the smoothing precedes the rotation and the labels are resampled once more (nearest neighbour), which changes thin skull layers (skull-layer Dice 0.80–0.90 against per-placement preprocessing at 1 mm; a warning says so). Needs the planning T1 and the segmentation on one voxel grid.

items.title: Air-Cavity Check (headmodel.air_cavities)
items.text:
See Air-Cavity Check.

Parameter Description Default Comments source Where the internal air cavities come from. 'simnibs' none: off. simnibs: the charm Air-Internal label (simnibs_labels) from segmentation/labeling.nii.gz in the m2m folder. segmentation: voxels with the labels in labels. hu: CT or pseudo-CT voxels in hu_window; needs pct.enabled: 1. Layered medium only. simnibs_labels Label indices of internal air in the charm labelling. [501] source: simnibs. 501 is Air-Internal in segmentation/labeling_LUT.txt (SimNIBS 4.0 to 4.6). labels Segmentation label indices of internal air. [] Required with source: segmentation, for a segmentation that labels air. SimNIBS final_tissues.nii.gz has no air label (internal air is 0); use source: simnibs. Label 0 (background) is not allowed. hu_window HU range classified as air. [-1200, -400] source: hu. As babelbrain.air_hu_window. keep_boundary Keep air components that touch the grid edge. false source: hu. By default they are removed with the air around the head. warn_db Flag the run when the peak pressure inside a cavity exceeds this level relative to the brain peak [dB]. -6 warn_beam_fraction Flag the run when, at any depth before the focus, cavities fill more than this share of the −6 dB beam cross-section. 0.1 Between 0 and 1.

items.title: Pseudo-CT Skull Property Mapping (pct)
items.text:
See CT-Based Skull Mapping.

Parameter Description Default Comments enabled Map skull properties from a CT? 0 1 = yes, 0 = no. Reads the measured CT in path.ct_pattern; when that is empty, a pseudo-CT is generated from the UTE image (path.t2_pattern) if not already present in the pseudo-CT folder. skull_mapping UTE→HU linear mapping algorithm used during pseudo-CT generation (not with a measured CT). 'kosciessa' kosciessa / miscouridou / wiesinger / treeby / custom; carpino is deprecated. See Choosing the UTE-to-HU Mapping. custom_slope Slope of the custom UTE→HU map (HU per normalised UTE unit). [] Scalar; required when skull_mapping is custom. custom_intercept Intercept of the custom UTE→HU map [HU]. [] Scalar; required when skull_mapping is custom. debug Keep intermediate NIfTI files in the debug_pct/ subfolder of the pseudo-CT folder. 1 1 = keep, 0 = delete after generation. mapping_density HU-to-density mapping algorithm. 'k-plan' k-plan / k-wave / marsac / marsac-babelbrain / aubry / air-tissue / none. See Mapping Skull Density. density_calibration HU-to-density table for mapping_density: k-plan; use the table of the measured CT, or of the CT the UTE→HU line was fitted to. '' '' (k-Plan default) / ucl_lowdose_80kvp (for treeby) / cph2025 / path to a CSV (HU, density [kg/m³]). See Mapping Skull Density. mapping_soundspeed HU-to-sound-speed mapping algorithm. 'k-plan' k-plan / marsac / aubry / webb / pichardo / mcdannold / none. See Mapping Skull Sound Speed. mapping_attenuation HU-to-attenuation mapping algorithm. 'k-plan' k-plan / mueller / aubry / webb / pichardo / mcdannold / none. See Mapping Skull Attenuation. interpolation Resampling of the CT onto the simulation grid. 'linear' linear / cubic (cubic convolution) / spline (interpolating cubic spline, as BabelBrain). Cubic and spline overshoot at bone edges; the HU limits clip the overshoot. See Limits and Interpolation. limits.hu_min Lower HU limit of the CT [HU]. [] [] = none. Acts before the skull is defined and mapped. limits.hu_max Upper HU limit of the CT [HU]. [] [] = none. BabelBrain CT: 2100. limits.density_min Lower limit of the mapped skull density [kg/m³]. 'water' A number, water (the water density), or []. limits.density_max Upper limit of the mapped skull density [kg/m³]. [] A number, water, or []. limits.sound_speed_min Lower limit of the mapped skull sound speed [m/s]. 'water' A number, water, or []. limits.sound_speed_max Upper limit of the mapped skull sound speed [m/s]. [] A number, water, or []. limits.alpha_coeff_min Lower limit of the mapped skull attenuation [dB/(cm MHz^y)]. [] A number, water, or []. limits.alpha_coeff_max Upper limit of the mapped skull attenuation [dB/(cm MHz^y)]. [] A number, water, or []. hu_reference_layers Layers whose CT values over the whole head set the densest-bone HU. ['skull'] For mappings that scale by it: density marsac-babelbrain and aubry, sound speed aubry, attenuation mueller and aubry. See The HU Reference. hu_reference_percentile Percentile of the CT in hu_reference_layers taken as the densest bone. 99.9 100 = the largest HU. Below 100, single bright voxels (metal, artefacts) do not set the scale; voxels above the reference map as the densest bone. hu_reference_resolution_mm Grid on which the densest-bone HU is taken [mm]. [] [] = the segmentation grid. A spacing = after resampling the whole-head CT onto that grid with interpolation, as BabelBrain does. Not recommended outside tool comparisons: spline overshoot raises the reference. See The HU Reference. bone_source Where the skull is. 'segmentation' segmentation: the segmentation's skull labels, with headmodel.skull_fill_method. hu: voxels whose HU exceed bone_hu_threshold on the simulation grid, as BabelBrain's CT path; needs enabled: 1. mask: a bone mask file (path.bone_mask_pattern). See Skull from the CT. bone_hu_threshold HU above which a voxel is bone (bone_source: hu) and below which bone HU are raised to it (hu and mask) [HU]. 300 BabelBrain: 300. bone_median_mm Width of the median filter of the bone mask (bone_source: hu or mask) [mm]. 0 0 = off. BabelBrain: 7 voxels (2.6 mm at 6 PPW, 500 kHz). bone_open_mm Edge of the cube that opens the bone mask before the closing, removing specks and spurs narrower than the cube (bone_source: hu or mask) [mm]. 0 0 = off. bone_close_mm Edge of the cube that closes holes in the bone mask (bone_source: hu or mask) [mm]. 0 0 = off. BabelBrain: 5. bone_soft_layer Medium that segmentation skull voxels outside the bone mask join (bone_source: hu or mask). 'nearest' nearest: the medium of the nearest voxel outside both skull definitions (skin on the outer side, brain or CSF on the inner). Or a layer of the run, for all of them. soft_hu_threshold HU that separates soft tissue from water on the simulation grid, outside the skull: tissue below it becomes water, water at or above it takes the nearest soft tissue [HU]. [] [] = off: the segmentation decides. Needs enabled: 1. See Soft Tissue from the CT. webb_sos_slope Slope of the webb sound-speed line [m/s per HU]. [] → 0.75 Not in config_default.yaml; set for your scanner from Webb et al. (2018), Tables I and II. [] = GE 120 kVp, B kernel. webb_sos_intercept Intercept of the webb sound-speed line [km/s]: c = slope · HU + 1000 · intercept [m/s]. [] → 1.32 As webb_sos_slope. webb_att_alpha0 α₀ of the webb attenuation model α₀ · exp(c · HU). [] → 26 Not in config_default.yaml; set for your scanner from Webb et al. (2021), Table IV. [] = GE 120 kVp, B kernel. webb_att_beta Frequency exponent β of the webb attenuation model; used as the skull alpha_power. [] → 1.3 As webb_att_alpha0. webb_att_c Exponent coefficient c of the webb attenuation model [1/HU]. [] → -0.0016 As webb_att_alpha0.

items.title: Tissue Layers (layers)
items.text:
See Head Model.

Maps tissue compartment names to their SimNIBS charm label indices. Compartments are modelled in listed order; any voxel label not assigned to a named compartment is treated as water. Charm label values are hardcoded in charm_seg_labels(). Layers can be removed or added.

Layer Default charm labels Comments water [0, 3, 6, 9, 10] Baseline layer; all unassigned voxels are treated as water brain [1, 2] White matter + grey matter skin [5] skull [4] Single skull layer; used when cortical/trabecular split is not needed skull_cortical [7] Cortical bone; used in multi-layer skull model skull_trabecular [8] Trabecular bone; used in multi-layer skull model

items.title: Tissue Acoustic & Thermal Properties (medium_properties)
items.text:
See Medium Properties.

Each tissue compartment (water, brain, skin, skull, skull_trabecular, skull_cortical) carries the following fields:

Field Description Units / Reference sound_speed Speed of sound. m/s; source: ITRUSST benchmarks density Density. kg/m³; source: ITRUSST benchmarks alpha_coeff Attenuation coefficient. dB/cm/MHz alpha_power Attenuation power law exponent. dimensionless thermal_conductivity Thermal conductivity. W/m/°C; source: Tissue Properties DB specific_heat_capacity Specific heat capacity. J/kg/°C; source: Tissue Properties DB perfusion Perfusion / heat transfer rate. mL/min/kg; source: Tissue Properties DB absorption_fraction Fraction of attenuation converted to heat.
